pagine.descrizione: What TALOS for Android keeps — chats, the Library, memory, notes, tasks and researches — how the PIN protects it, what leaves the device, and how to take it with you.

sezioni.testo: Everything TALOS keeps, it keeps on the device. There is no account and no copy elsewhere, which makes the device — and the PIN that locks it — the whole story.

With App lock on, in Settings → Account, TALOS asks for a PIN when it starts, and that PIN is the key that encrypts your chats and documents on the device. It never leaves the device.

- There is no recovery. Forget the PIN and the data cannot be opened — not by you, and not by anyone else.
- Without the lock, your chats and documents can be read by anyone with access to the device.
- Biometrics can unlock it once the PIN has been entered.
- Hide in app switcher and block screenshots stops Android from capturing TALOS’s window.

See Lock TALOS with a PIN.

Where | What it holds
Chats | Your conversations. An incognito chat is saved nowhere: leaving it discards it.
Library | Files you bring — copied in, never uploaded — files TALOS makes, and pages it reads, each with where it came from.
Memory | What TALOS carries into your next conversations, one typed memory at a time.
Notes | Notes in Markdown, with checklists you tick inside the card.
Tasks | To-dos with a state and a priority, and tasks that repeat on a schedule.
Research | Deep researches: the question, the sources, and a report whose claims are checked.

### The Library

A file you give TALOS is copied into its own Library: searchable inside the text, and private to the app. Each file records where it came from — which model made it, when and in which chat; or that you brought it in; or that it was downloaded from the web. A file is either available to every chat or only where explicitly attached. Deleting it removes it from the device; past chats keep only its name. How chats may use the Library is up to you: see Use the Library in chats.

### Memory

A memory is written only because you asked, or because the model asked and you approved. Each one has a kind — preference, project fact, procedure or policy note — and a scope: global, one project, or one chat. It can be on, paused, or waiting for your review when the model suggested it. Memories are always given to the model as untrusted context: they can never override TALOS’s rules. See Review what TALOS remembers.

Even your name, entered during setup, is kept as a global memory you can read, change or delete.

Settings → Backup and restore exports everything — chats, messages, attachments, the Library, notes, tasks, memory, researches and settings — into one file encrypted with a passphrase you choose, saved where you choose, so it survives uninstalling TALOS. Provider keys are included only if you ask. See Back up and restore.

A single chat can also be exported, as a Markdown transcript or as a JSON evidence pack with its tool activity and sources.

pagine.descrizione: How TALOS for Android uses the device — typed device tools, actions in other apps, driving an app’s screen, and the bridge that reaches what apps normally cannot.

sezioni.testo: TALOS reaches the device in four ways, from the narrowest to the widest. Each one is a tool, and every tool passes the powers you set — whatever Android itself would allow.

Typed tools for one thing each: the torch, the volume, an alarm, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Do Not Disturb, the wallpaper, opening an app or a settings screen, reading the calendar or your location. Many of them need no Android permission — Android lets any app do them — so the only thing between a request and the action is your gate.

Each one is written to do what it says and no more:

- A screenshot is taken by the system and saved to your gallery, as the hardware buttons would: the image never reaches TALOS.
- A call, a message or a share is prepared and handed to you: TALOS never calls or sends by itself — you press the button.
- Your location is read at the moment it is needed, never in the background.
- Notifications can be read and answered once you open that access by hand. Android hides passcodes and two-factor codes from them: TALOS cannot see those, and never will. A reply is a real message, so it always asks.
- Speaking out loud counts as leaving the device: anyone in the room hears it.

The full list is in the This device group of the tools reference.

Instead of hunting on a screen, TALOS can open the right app with everything already filled in — a message, a navigation, a song, a calendar event — or attach a file from your Library in the app you name. It tells you which apps on this device can receive it, and you press send. See In other apps.

With Screen reading — Android Accessibility, switched on in the system settings — TALOS reads what is on the screen and can tap, type and scroll inside another app to reach a goal. It says out loud what it is about to do before each move, and stops on its own after 20 steps, after 2 minutes, after two failures in a row — and the instant you touch the screen.

Some things Android does not let apps do at all: listing everything installed, changing system settings, reaching parts of the device no app can. The bridge does them with the same powers as a computer plugged in over USB — no root, and no third-party app.

- It works only after you pair it once, with a six-digit code you read on your own screen, through Android’s wireless debugging.
- Wireless debugging switches off at every restart of the device. The pairing stays: you reconnect, without a new code.
- Every command still passes your permission gate.
- Code runs its terminal through it: with the bridge down, no command runs there.

See Connect TALOS to the device.

One tool deserves its warning: turning airplane mode on takes the device off the network, and with it the bridge — TALOS will not be able to turn it back off by itself.

Devices differ: a feature this device does not offer is reported as unsupported, an access you refused as denied, and neither as a failure. Where the effect of an action can be observed, TALOS looks before calling it done — see “Done” is a state it checks.

pagine.descrizione: An agent that lives on the device — no account and no server of ours — with a model you choose, typed tools, and outcomes it checks.

sezioni.testo: TALOS for Android is an agent that runs on your device. You talk to it; it answers with the model you chose, and when the answer needs it, it uses tools — your Library, your notes, the web, the device itself — each one under a permission you set.

sezioni.titolo: No account, and no server of ours
sezioni.testo:
There is no TALOS backend. Conversations, Library files, memory and settings stay on the device, and no account is needed to use any of it.

- A cloud model is reached directly: what you send goes from the device to the provider you chose, with your own key, kept in the device’s Keystore.
- A model on the device answers without the network at all, and keeps working in airplane mode.
- The web is contacted only by the operation that needs it: a search sends its words to the search service you chose; reading a page downloads that page.

Three things work with no server anywhere: models on the device, the “hey TALOS” wake word, and everything you keep — Library, memory, notes, tasks and conversations. See Your data on the device.

sezioni.titolo: The model, and what surrounds it
sezioni.testo:
The model writes the answer; everything around it is TALOS: which tools the model is offered, whether a tool may run, what happens when a call fails or repeats, and whether an action really happened.

- Tools are typed. Each one has a declared input, a power — read, write, or off-device — and a risk level. A tool you switch off is not sent to the model and cannot run. Every tool is listed in the tools reference, in the groups the app uses: Library, Personal, Web, Create, Models on this device, This device, and actions in other apps.
- Tools are disclosed progressively. Instead of every tool’s full description at every turn, the model gets a compact catalog — or the provider’s own deferred loading, where it has one — and asks for a tool’s full schema the first time it needs it: one more round trip, and a much smaller prompt, which also helps smaller models avoid the wrong tool.
- Every action passes a gate. Read, write and off-device are each allowed, asked or denied, and an approval is bound to the exact input it was given. See Powers and consent.

A tool saying it succeeded does not prove the world changed. Where the result can be observed, TALOS looks: for a message sent through another app, the input field emptied and the message appeared in the conversation. A result is then verified success, failed or unable to confirm — and after a timeout TALOS inspects the state instead of trying again blindly and doing the thing twice.

Android differs from device to device, so TALOS also keeps unsupported, denied, failed and succeeded apart: a feature this device does not offer is not reported as an error, and an error is not reported as success.

The menu holds the chats and the app’s stations:

Station | What it holds
Tasks | Your to-dos, and tasks that run on their own on a schedule.
Library | Files you brought, files TALOS made, and pages it read.
Models | The Model Lab: providers, the catalog, and the models on this device.
Research | Deep researches and their reports.
Memory | What TALOS carries into your next conversations.
Notes | Notes, yours and the ones TALOS writes.
Tool Forge | Tools you add from a manifest. See Tool Forge.
Code | Coding sessions that run on the device. See Start a Code session.
Doctor | Checks of what works on this device. See Check what works on this device.
Settings | Everything else, grouped as Intelligence, Connections, Interface and Privacy.

Settings also keeps an Unavailable group — Integrations, Email, Reminders and System — so that a capability the app does not have yet reads as missing, not as broken. Each one says why when you open it.

pagine.titolo: Models on the device and in the cloud
pagine.descrizione: Which models TALOS for Android can use, where their keys are kept, how it tells whether a model fits this device, and the defaults that pick a model for each job.

sezioni.titolo: Models on the device and in the cloud
sezioni.testo: TALOS does not ship a model. It works with the one you choose: from a provider, with your own key, or downloaded onto the device and run there.

Provider | How it connects
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek | Your API key.
OpenRouter | Your API key, or sign in with OpenRouter and let it issue one. Hundreds of models through one key.
Ollama | The address of an Ollama server you run. No key.
On the device | A GGUF model run by the engine built into the app. No key, no network.

A key is kept in the device’s Keystore and sent only to its provider; the app shows only whether one is saved. Every provider, with what it needs, is on Providers.

All of this lives in the Model Lab — Models in the menu, or Settings → Models:

- Providers and access — keys, local addresses, whether each provider is ready, and an optional Hugging Face token;
- Model catalog — the models your providers list, with what each declares it can do;
- Local models — the models on this device, and those you can download;
- This device — usable memory, storage and the reserve TALOS keeps free, measured on request.

The Model Lab and the chat’s quick picker share one selection: the model you pick in either is the one that answers.

sezioni.titolo: A catalog that does not guess
sezioni.testo: The catalog keeps what a provider observed about a model apart from what is merely declared. A model can be tested from the catalog with a short completion; until then it reads “not tested”, not “working”. A model the provider does not list can be added by hand under Advanced manual models — its capabilities are then marked as yours, not the provider’s.

Each model is chosen where it is used:

- the model that answers — in the composer, while you write;
- the two models of a deep research — the one that writes the report and the one that checks its citations — in the research itself, next to the plan they govern.

Settings → AI Defaults holds what applies to every conversation:

- Assistant tone — Balanced, Engineering, Friendly or Concise. The model may suggest a better tone for a conversation; you decide from the notification.
- Vision routing preference — prefer a model that sees images when you attach one.
- Let chats use your Library — see Use the Library in chats.

pagine.descrizione: The two gates every action passes — Android’s permissions and TALOS’s own powers — how an approval is scoped, and why what a conversation has seen matters.

sezioni.testo: Before TALOS does anything on your behalf, two gates must open. Android decides what the app may reach; TALOS decides, by your rules, what the agent may do with it.

Android permissions are asked only when a feature needs them, at the moment you use it, and Android always has the final word: anything granted can be taken back in the system settings. Settings → Privacy and permissions lists every access the app can have and its state — allowed, not requested, not allowed, blocked by Android — and, for the ones that need no permission at all, says so instead of leaving a blank. Each row says why TALOS would need it.

The full list, with how each permission is obtained, is on Android permissions. A permission Android granted is only the first gate: every tool still passes the second.

Every tool declares the power it uses:

Power | In Settings | What it covers
Read | Read your things | The Library, notes, tasks, memory, the calendar, the state of the device.
Write | Create or change things | A note, a document, a switch, an alarm — on the device or in your records.
Off-device | Send anything off this device | A search, a page, a message, a model download — or words spoken out loud.

Each power is set to Always allow, Ask me every time or Never allow, in Settings → Agent Tools. By default all three ask. When a tool asks, a card appears in the chat with what it is about to do; the card itself offers to always allow, so “ask me” costs one question per tool. See Choose what TALOS may do.

Below the powers, each tool has its own switch. A tool you switch off is not sent to the model and cannot run.

sezioni.titolo: An approval is bound to its input
sezioni.testo:
Choosing a tool and being allowed to run it are separate decisions. An approval covers the exact, validated input it was shown — not the tool in general, and not a different input the model tries next.

How long an approval lasts is your choice, under Approval duration:

- This message — it ends with the answer;
- The conversation, while trusted — it lasts for the conversation, and expires as soon as an untrusted page or document enters it.

Revoke saved authorizations removes every “always” you gave; the tools stay on and ask again.

TALOS keeps track of where content comes from — you, something derived from it, or the outside world — and whether a conversation has already read your private data or taken in untrusted outside content. Reading private data, reading something untrusted, and then sending something off the device is treated as more dangerous than any one of the three alone, and a tool that would send is judged with that history in view.

Memories and Library documents are context, not authority: what they say cannot change these rules. Doctor shows, for the current chat, whether private data was read and outside content entered.

Each tool also carries a risk level, from touching nothing of yours to acting in the world in a way that cannot be taken back, and whether its effect can be undone. Both are listed for every tool on Consent.

Turning on “hey TALOS” means talking to TALOS without touching the screen, so it cannot stop to show you a card. Before it turns on, TALOS asks once to set all three powers to always allow. Before anything that cannot be undone — deleting, sending, calling — it says so out loud and waits for your answer. See Call TALOS from anywhere.

pagine.descrizione: One task per page — from the first setup to a backup you can restore — checked against TALOS for Android 0.1.38.

sezioni.testo: Each guide does one thing, in the order you would do it. To understand how the parts fit together first, start with How TALOS for Android works.

- Use TALOS on your PC from the device Connect a computer, follow and start its sessions in Code, answer its approvals, and choose where research runs.
- Keep TALOS up to date TALOS updates itself — it checks once a day, downloads on Wi-Fi and asks before restarting. Check by hand or turn it off in Settings.
- Set up TALOS the first time The first-run setup, step by step — language, your name, the PIN, a model, what TALOS may do on its own, and long work in the background.
- Connect a cloud model Save a provider key — or sign in with OpenRouter, or point TALOS at your Ollama server — test a model, and make it the one that answers.
- Run a model on the device Find a model this device can hold, check its variants, download it, and let TALOS find the fastest engine — then answer with no network at all.
- Choose what TALOS may do Set the three powers, switch single tools on and off, decide how long an approval lasts, and take back every “always”.
- Call TALOS from anywhere Make TALOS the device’s assistant, choose the gesture or keys that open it, turn on “hey TALOS”, and use the bar over any app.
- Connect TALOS to the device Pair the bridge once through wireless debugging, reconnect after a restart, and understand what it can reach.
- Turn on web search Choose the service that answers TALOS’s searches, give it a key or an address, and allow the query to leave the device.
- Use the Library in chats Bring files in, attach them to a message, decide how much of the Library a chat may read — for every chat, one chat, or the next message.
- Review what TALOS remembers Approve a memory in the chat, add one by hand, give it a kind and a scope, pause it, correct it or delete it.
- Run a deep research Ask one question, review the plan before anything is spent, choose the writer and the checker, follow the run, and read a report whose every claim is checked.
- Schedule a task Write a task with its checklist, then let it repeat on its own — once, every day, on chosen days or at an interval — and hear back only when something changed.
- Dictate, listen, and use your own voice Speak instead of typing, have replies read aloud, and train a personal voice from twelve phrases — all on the device.
- Start a Code session Connect the bridge, open a coding session that runs on the device, choose its model, and follow its commands, approvals and changes.
- Back up and restore Export everything into one file encrypted with a passphrase, keep it where you choose, and bring it back — merging, replacing or skipping what is already there.
- Lock TALOS with a PIN Turn on the app lock, whose PIN encrypts your chats and documents; unlock with biometrics; keep TALOS out of screenshots and the app switcher.
- Keep long work running Let TALOS work with the screen off, so researches, model downloads and scheduled tasks reach the end — and the extra steps some devices ask for.
- Check what works on this device Run Doctor’s checks, read what a chat has seen, test a local model before
relying on it, and copy a report that carries no keys, messages or documents.

pagine.descrizione: Set the three powers, switch single tools on and off, decide how long an approval lasts, and take back every “always”.

sezioni.testo: Why there are three powers, and what an approval covers, is explained in Powers and consent. Everything here is in Settings → Agent Tools.

Under What TALOS may do on its own, each power has one choice:

Power | Always allow | Ask me every time | Never allow
Read your things | Runs without asking | A card asks first | Never runs
Create or change things | Runs without asking | A card asks first | Never runs
Send anything off this device | Runs without asking | A card asks first | Never runs

All three start at Ask me every time.

Web search and page reading send search words or an address off the device, and also save their sources in the Library: they need both Send anything off this device and Create or change things.

Below the powers, the tools are grouped — Library, Personal, Web, Create, Models on this device, This device — each group with how many of its tools are on. A tool switched off is not sent to the model and cannot run, whatever the powers say.

A tool switched on can still be unable to run: it may need a model that supports tools, a service you have not set up — web search needs a search engine — or a power you refused.

sezioni.titolo: Decide how long an approval lasts

sezioni.testo: Revoke saved authorizations removes every tool you set to always allow. The tools stay on, and follow your powers again.
Settings → Privacy and permissions → Content and models holds three choices that decide what reaches a model: Library access, Writing memories and Sending attached images.

pagine.descrizione: Let TALOS work with the screen off, so researches, model downloads and scheduled tasks reach the end — and the extra steps some devices ask for.

sezioni.testo: A deep research or a model download takes minutes, sometimes hours. To save battery, Android suspends an app soon after you leave it or lock the screen — and the work stops there. One setting decides whether it does.

- Open Settings → Privacy and permissions.
- Find Running in the background and tap Allow. Android asks you to confirm.

The same choice is offered during the first setup, as Let TALOS work in the background. Until it is allowed, keep TALOS open during long work.

Notifications are worth allowing too: long work runs without them, but you will not see how far along it is.

sezioni.titolo: The extra steps some devices ask for
sezioni.testo:
Some device makers suspend apps beyond what Android does. When TALOS recognizes the device, it lists the extra steps under Extra steps this device asks for:

Device | Extra steps
OnePlus, OPPO (ColorOS) | Settings → Apps → Auto-launch: on for TALOS. Settings → Battery → Battery optimization → ⋮ → Advanced: turn off “Deep optimization” and “Sleep standby optimization”. In Recents, hold the TALOS card and tap the lock.
Xiaomi | Settings → Apps → Permissions → Background autostart: on for TALOS. Settings → Battery → TALOS → No restrictions. In Recents, hold the TALOS card and tap the lock.
Samsung | Settings → Battery and device care → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps: add TALOS.
Huawei | Settings → Apps & services → App launch: turn off “Manage automatically” for TALOS, then enable “Auto-launch”, “Secondary launch” and “Run in background”. In Recent tasks, swipe down on the TALOS card until the lock appears.
Honor | Settings → Apps → App launch: turn off “Manage automatically” for TALOS, then enable “Auto-launch”, “Secondary launch” and “Run in background”. In Recent tasks, swipe down on the TALOS card until the lock appears.

The names are the device maker’s own, as they appear on the device, and can differ between versions.

pagine.descrizione: Export everything into one file encrypted with a passphrase, keep it where you choose, and bring it back — merging, replacing or skipping what is already there.

sezioni.testo: Your data lives only on the device — see Your data on the device. A backup is how you take it with you: to a new device, or across a reinstall. It is one file, encrypted, saved where you choose, so it stays even if you uninstall TALOS.

- Open Settings → Backup and restore.
- Under Export, choose a passphrase you will remember. Without it the backup will not open, and it cannot be recovered — not even TALOS knows it.
- Decide whether to Include provider keys. You will need them after a reinstall — but the file then is a key: keep it like one.
- Tap Export and choose where to save, and pick the place.

The backup holds your chats and their messages and attachments, the Library, notes, tasks, memory, researches and settings — and the provider keys, if you included them. Before handing the file over, TALOS reads it back; if it does not read back the same, it says which part and does not hand it over. When it is done, it says how many rows it saved, and the size.

- Open Settings → Backup and restore, and under Restore tap Choose a backup file.
- Enter its passphrase.
- Choose what to do with what is already on the device:
- Merge — combine the two;
- Replace — the backup wins;
- Skip existing — keep what is here, add only what is missing.
- Tap See what it would do. TALOS shows where the backup comes from — the device and the date — and how many rows would be overwritten, before anything changes.
- Tap Restore to apply it.

sezioni.titolo: A deleted memory, and a backup
sezioni.testo: Deleting a memory removes it from the device, not from a backup exported before: that backup still holds a copy. The same is true of anything else you delete after exporting.

pagine.descrizione: Pair the bridge once through wireless debugging, reconnect after a restart, and understand what it can reach.

sezioni.testo:
The bridge lets TALOS do what Android does not let apps do — turn Wi-Fi on and off, change system settings, see which apps are installed — with the same powers as a computer plugged in over USB. Code runs its terminal through it. Why it exists, and what it can reach, is explained in Acting on the device.

Every command it runs still passes your permission gate.

The device must be on Wi-Fi, and Android’s developer options must be on. If they are not yet, turn them on first — on most devices, by tapping Build number seven times in the device’s About page.

- Open Settings → Device control in TALOS, and find Pair TALOS with your device.
- Tap Open developer options, turn on Wireless debugging, then tap Pair device with pairing code. Android shows a six-digit code.
- Type the code into TALOS. The easiest way is Open settings with the field on top: a small field floats over Android’s settings, so you can read the code and type it without leaving. Do not leave Settings — Android closes the code’s dialog the moment you do.
- TALOS finds the addresses by itself and connects. The card then reads TALOS is connected to your device.

The floating field needs the permission to draw over other apps. Without it, you can type the code in TALOS instead — but leaving Settings to do it closes Android’s dialog, so pairing that way usually fails.

Wireless debugging switches off every time the device restarts, and the bridge with it; TALOS tells you it can do less than before. The pairing stays:

- Turn Wireless debugging back on.
- In Settings → Device control, tap Reconnect. No new code is needed.

Keep it alive makes the bridge reconnect on its own after a restart, without turning wireless debugging back on. While it is on, anyone on your network can see the port it listens on; getting in still needs TALOS’s own key.

TALOS says | What to do
The code is six digits | Type all six.
It cannot hear the pairing announcement | The code’s dialog has closed, or the device is not on Wi-Fi. Open it again.
Pairing worked, but it cannot find the connection port | Try again in a few seconds: the device announces it shortly after.
The device refused the connection | Wireless debugging was switched off in the meantime.
That did not work | Android shows a new code every time: open the dialog again and type the new one.

If it keeps failing, turn wireless debugging off and on again.

pagine.descrizione: Make TALOS the device’s assistant, choose the gesture or keys that open it, turn on “hey TALOS”, and use the bar over any app.

sezioni.testo: Everything here is in Settings → Device control, under How you call it. Each way shows whether it works right now — Ready, Try it, Role missing or Not set yet — and the button that sets it.

Most ways of calling TALOS go through Android’s assistant, so start here.

- Tap Make TALOS the assistant. Android does not let an app switch this by itself, so TALOS opens the page where you choose.
- On that page, tap Default digital assistant app and choose TALOS.
- Come back: the row updates by itself.

If neither Android nor TALOS could set it, do it by hand: Settings → Apps → Default apps → Digital assistant in the device’s own settings. If that list is empty, connect the bridge and try again.

Way | When it works
Press and hold the power button | Opens the device’s assistant — but the device decides whether to route the gesture.
Swipe in from the screen corner | The swipe from the bottom corner, if you navigate by gestures.
Press and hold Home | If you navigate with three buttons: hold the middle one.
Press and hold both volume keys | Goes straight to TALOS, skipping the assistant. Android asks you to confirm the first time.

The volume-key shortcut is an Accessibility shortcut, and there is one per device: if another service takes it, TALOS loses it.

Say “hey TALOS” and it opens. The wake word is recognized on the device, by a small local model: no audio leaves the device just to notice that you called.

- Tap Turn on “hey TALOS”.
- The first time, TALOS asks to act on its own: talking without touching the screen means it cannot stop to show you a card. Accepting sets the three powers — read, write and off-device — to always allow. Before anything that cannot be undone — deleting, sending, calling — it still says so out loud and waits for your answer.
- The microphone stays on to wait for the word, transcribing nothing. A notification says so, and turns it off.

To stop, tap Stop waiting for the word, or use the notification. To take the powers back, set them again in Agent Tools.

pagine.descrizione: Connect the bridge, open a coding session that runs on the device, choose its model, and follow its commands, approvals and changes.

sezioni.testo: Code is the coding agent, and it runs on the device: sessions open on the device, commands run in a sandboxed terminal on the device, and the files it reads and writes are the device’s. No computer has to be awake.

The terminal of a Code session runs every command through the bridge — the same one Settings → Device control pairs. With the bridge down, no terminal and no command can start, and Code tells you so when you open it, with a way to Settings. Connect TALOS to the device first; after a device restart, reconnect it.

- Open Code from the menu.
- Tap New, or simply write below: the first message starts the session.

Sessions are listed by date — today, yesterday, the last 7 and 30 days — each with its state: Running, Waiting for approval, Interrupted or Concluded with an error. A session can be renamed or deleted from its actions; deleting removes it from the device for good.

Each session has its own model and provider: any OpenRouter model, or OpenAI, DeepSeek or Ollama directly. Anthropic and Gemini are recognized and refused with that reason, rather than pretending to work. A model on the device cannot drive a Code session yet: choosing one is refused, not left to fail halfway through an answer.

- Commands run on the device, shown in plain words before they run; their output comes back into the conversation.
- Approvals are per tool, not per session: reading a file and deleting one are separate decisions.
- Tool calls collapse into groups, with a diff for each file changed.
- Long conversations are compacted, and you see it happen.
- Delegation: a session can hand a self-contained sub-task to a child agent that starts with nothing but the instruction it was given.

Close the app and come back: the session is where you left it, with the model it was using and what it was waiting for.

- The bridge is not connected — the bridge is down: turn on wireless debugging, then reconnect from Settings → Device control.
- “Code couldn’t start its terminal on this device” — close and reopen TALOS; that usually fixes it.
- “Session not found” — the session no longer exists; go back to Code and choose one from the list.

pagine.titolo: Check what works on this device
pagine.descrizione: Run Doctor’s checks, read what a chat has seen, test a local model before relying on it, and copy a report that carries no keys, messages or documents.

sezioni.titolo: Check what works on this device
sezioni.testo: Android differs from device to device, and so does what TALOS can do on each. Doctor, in the menu, answers the question honestly: every row is a real check, run on this device, offline.

Open Doctor. It scans the device and sums up: how many checks passed, and how many problems it found. Open the checks to see each one — the platform, the encrypted local storage, the database lock, the speech recognizer, biometric unlock, the personal voice engine, the local engine, and whether Code can see and read its workspace. Run diagnostics runs them again.

The checks are grouped as Status, Data and Advanced. Recent issues lists what went wrong lately.

For the current chat, Doctor shows what the permission gate is weighing: whether your private data was already read, whether outside content entered, how far an approved plan reaches, and which tools could send something out.

Before relying on a model that runs on the device, three checks tell you how it behaves here:

- Which engines actually load — tries the engine libraries shipped with the app, one by one, and says which ones load on this device. It does not measure speed and does not drain the battery.
- Local model parity — runs real checks with no side effect: plain text, no false tool call, a tool call, the result returned, the protocol kept hidden, and Stop. A model is compatible when it passes them. It also says whether the model’s tool requests can be held in check, and whether its reasoning can be turned off.
- Measure this model’s threads — with a local model open, tries several configurations with a real prompt and remembers the best one for this model on this device.

- Turn on Show technical detail under Advanced. Errors then carry their internal code, and each send records how long it took — rounds, first word, tool calls, and time spent waiting for you. Nothing is measured while it is off.
- Reproduce the problem.
- Tap Copy diagnostics.

The report carries timings, check results, provider and model names and the build. It is never given your keys, messages or documents — and anything that looks like a key in the device log is removed on the way out. Clear timings empties them when you are done.

pagine.descrizione: Bring files in, attach them to a message, decide how much of the Library a chat may read — for every chat, one chat, or the next message.

sezioni.testo: The Library holds what you bring, what TALOS makes, and the pages it reads — see Your data on the device. A chat can use it in two ways: you attach a file, or the model reads the Library by itself, as far as you allow.

- In the Library, tap Add file and pick files from the device. They are copied in; nothing is uploaded.
- In a chat, Attach takes files, images or Library files: up to 6 per message, 10 MB each, 20 MB in all.
- With Auto-save generated files, in Settings → AI Defaults, the documents and images a chat makes are saved to the Library by themselves.

The Library shows images, files and saved links, as a grid or a list, grouped by the chat that produced them. Each file can be opened, shared, saved to the device or deleted, and says where it came from.
Each file is either available to every chat or only available where explicitly attached. A private file stays out of every chat you did not attach it to, whatever the settings below say.

Settings → AI Defaults → Let chats use your Library lets the model use your Library as context. It adds tokens to every message. Choose a Library context mode first:

Mode | What it does
Broad compatibility | Includes every eligible document that fits the context budget.
Relevant sources only | Uses only documents with evidence that they relate to the conversation.
Ask before using sources | Finds candidate sources, then asks before any document is sent to the model.
Only when requested | Adds nothing by itself; the model uses the Library tools when asked and allowed.

The Library tools themselves — browse, search, read — also need Library access, in Settings → Privacy and permissions, and the read power.

sezioni.titolo: One chat, or the next message
sezioni.testo:
- Context for this chat — inherit the global setting, turn the Library off for this chat, or include or exclude single files.
- Library context for the next message — a mode and single files for one message only. The choice clears once TALOS accepts the message.

Excluding always wins over including, and private files stay unavailable either way.

pagine.titolo: Run a model on the device
pagine.descrizione: Find a model this device can hold, check its variants, download it, and let TALOS find the fastest engine — then answer with no network at all.

sezioni.titolo: Run a model on the device
sezioni.testo: A model on the device is a GGUF file run by the engine inside TALOS. It needs a 64-bit ARM device, and enough memory for the model to stay resident while it writes. How TALOS judges that is explained in Models on the device and in the cloud.

- Open Models from the menu, then Local models, and the Hugging Face tab.
- TALOS measures this device first — free memory, space, temperature and memory speed — and shows the models Recommended for this device.
- Narrow the list with the filters — Fits in memory, Chat, Code-oriented, Q4, Declared permissive license — or by publisher and model size, or search by name.

A model marked license required is gated: accept its license on huggingface.co, then search again.

- Tap Download on the variant you chose.
- Follow it in the Download Center: one download at a time, which you can pause and resume where it left off. The file is verified when it arrives.

Long downloads need TALOS to keep running with the screen off: see Keep long work running. Without a Hugging Face token you share a request limit with everyone else behind your carrier; an optional token, in Providers and access, gives you your own.

Already have the file? Add a model from this device copies a GGUF file in — for a few minutes it takes twice the space.

Pick the model in the composer, like any other. The first message after starting can take a while: the model has to load. When the device is too warm, or short on free memory, TALOS waits for your first message instead of loading it in the background.

- Settings → Privacy and permissions → Which engine is fastest here runs a short, real generation on each engine this device offers and remembers the fastest. It costs some battery and heat, and runs only when you ask.
- Doctor → Measure this model’s threads finds the best thread count for the open model on this device.
- Doctor → Local model parity checks that a model handles text, tool calls and Stop correctly before you rely on it. See Check what works on this device.

A model on the device cannot drive a Code session yet.

pagine.descrizione: Turn on the app lock, whose PIN encrypts your chats and documents; unlock with biometrics; keep TALOS out of screenshots and the app switcher.

sezioni.testo: With the app lock on, TALOS asks for a PIN when it starts, and that PIN is the key that encrypts your chats and documents on the device. Without it, they can be read by anyone with access to the device. Why that matters is in Your data on the device.

- Open Settings → Account, and under App lock turn on Require PIN on start.
- Choose a PIN of at least 6 digits, not a predictable one, and confirm it.
- Keep TALOS open while it locks your data with the new key — this happens once.

If you forget the PIN, the data is lost for good. There is no recovery — not for you, and not for anyone else. The PIN never leaves the device. A backup, which has its own passphrase, is the only copy that does not depend on it.

Enter the PIN. After too many wrong attempts, TALOS makes you wait before you can try again.

Unlock with biometrics lets a fingerprint or your face open TALOS. The PIN is still the key: enter it once after turning biometrics on, and biometrics work from then on. The biometric key stays in the device’s secure hardware and never reaches TALOS itself.
Hide in app switcher and block screenshots stops Android from capturing TALOS: no screenshots, no screen recording, and a blank card in recent apps.

sezioni.titolo: Turn it off, or change it
sezioni.testo: Turning Require PIN on start off asks for the current PIN first. A PIN shorter than the current 6-digit minimum, set by an older version, can be replaced by turning the lock off and on again.

pagine.descrizione: Approve a memory in the chat, add one by hand, give it a kind and a scope, pause it, correct it or delete it.

sezioni.testo: Memory is what TALOS carries into your next conversations — see Your data on the device. Nothing is remembered behind your back: every memory is one you wrote, or one you approved.

Tell TALOS to remember something, and it asks first, with a card in the chat showing the title, the content and the kind. Allow it, refuse it, or always allow it. Whether TALOS may write memories at all is Writing memories, in Settings → Privacy and permissions.

A memory the model only suggested waits in Memory as Needs review. Turning it on approves it; a suggested memory with no kind yet asks you to pick one first.

- Open Memory from the menu and tap New memory.
- Write a title and what TALOS should remember.
- Choose a kind and a scope, and save it.

Kind | For
Preference | How you prefer to work.
Project fact | A reference to remember.
Procedure | A way of working.
Policy note | A boundary to keep in mind.

Scope | Where it applies
Global | Every conversation.
Project | One project.
This chat | This conversation only.

Open a memory to see its kind, scope, state and source — content you provided, or content gathered from outside.

- Use in your next conversations — on, TALOS reads it again in every new conversation; off, it is paused until you turn it back on.
- Edit corrects it in place. When TALOS itself corrects a memory, it rewrites it instead of adding a second one that contradicts it.
- Export text copies it to the clipboard.
- Delete removes it from the device. A backup exported earlier still holds a copy.

Search, filter — all, or needs review — and sort by date, title or kind when the list grows.
A memory is given to the model as untrusted context, in every case: what it says can never override TALOS’s rules or your permissions.

pagine.descrizione: Save a provider key — or sign in with OpenRouter, or point TALOS at your Ollama server — test a model, and make it the one that answers.

sezioni.testo: How providers, keys and the catalog fit together is explained in Models on the device and in the cloud.

- Open Models from the menu, then Providers and access.
- Choose the provider — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek or OpenRouter.
- Paste the key and save it.

The key goes into the device’s Keystore. From then on the app shows only that a key is saved, never the key itself. To change it, paste a new one over it; to remove it, use Remove key.

### OpenRouter without copying a key

For OpenRouter you can tap Sign in with OpenRouter instead: the browser opens, you sign in, and OpenRouter issues the key straight to TALOS. If the browser cannot open, or the sign-in fails, paste a key instead.

Ollama needs no key, only its address:

- In Providers and access, open Ollama and enter the endpoint.
- Save it, then refresh its models.

The address must start with http:// or https://, and must not contain a username or password. A plain http:// address is accepted only for a machine on your own network, written as a number — for example http://192.168.1.20:11434. Anything else needs https://.

Each provider also has a timeout, and a custom endpoint can be reset to the official one.

sezioni.titolo: Test a model, then use it
sezioni.testo:
- Open Model catalog. It lists the models your providers offer, with what each declares it can do — context, inputs, reasoning — kept apart from what was actually observed.
- Pick a model and run Test completion. Until it passes, the model reads “not tested”.
- Use model makes it the default; Show in composer puts it in the chat’s quick picker.

The Model Lab and the composer share one selection: change the model in either, and the next answer uses it.

If a provider does not list a model you know exists, add it under Advanced manual models with its provider and model ID. What it can do — reasoning, image input — is then declared by you, and marked as such.

- “Add your … API key before continuing” — no key is saved for that provider.
- “… answered with nothing at all” — try another model.
- “… spent its whole token budget thinking” — the model reasoned until it ran out; pick one that reasons less, or a larger one.
- “Ollama requires an endpoint reachable from this device” — the device cannot reach that address; check that the server listens on your network, not only on its own machine.

pagine.titolo: Use TALOS on your PC from the device
pagine.descrizione: Connect a computer, follow and start its sessions in Code, answer its approvals, and choose where research runs.

sezioni.titolo: Use TALOS on your PC from the device
sezioni.testo: Computer — Use TALOS on your PC from here. Pair the device with TALOS Desktop once, and the PC’s sessions, models and approvals are on the device. The work runs on the computer.

- On the PC, open Connected devices and show the pairing code (see Remote Control on Desktop).
- On the device, open Computer and tap Connect a computer, then scan the code.
- The device and the PC show the same 6-digit number. Confirm on the PC.

Each computer gets a card: its name, Online or Offline · last seen …, how many sessions it has, how many are running and how many are waiting for you, and Open sessions in Code. Open a computer for its settings: Notifications from this computer (when a session is waiting for you, or a long job is done), Send a test notification, the path of the connection (for example Direct · 61 ms) and Forget this computer.

- In Code, the Where filter chooses All, Here (this device) or one computer.
- New session on … asks Which computer folder should TALOS work in? A folder the PC has not allowed yet says The PC will ask your permission the first time; after Start, the device shows Confirm on the computer until you answer on the PC. The answer is remembered for this device and this folder.
- In a session whose folder is not allowed yet, Writing here needs the PC’s permission: you can read everything, and Ask the PC sends the same question to the computer.
- TALOS is asking for permission cards are answered from the device with Deny or Approve.
A new research asks Where it runs: on the computer, or This device; then Start research. Research started on the PC keeps running when you close the app. The model picker shows the PC’s models too.

pagine.descrizione: Ask one question, review the plan before anything is spent, choose the writer and the checker, follow the run, and read a report whose every claim is checked.

sezioni.testo: A deep research takes one question, reads many pages, keeps the passages it relies on, and writes a report in which every claim is checked against its source. It searches the web, so set up web search first; it takes minutes, so let TALOS keep working in the background.

- Open Research from the menu and tap New research.
- Write the question, and choose a reading depth: Quick, Deep or Exhaustive.
- Tap Draw up the plan. TALOS proposes the lines of enquiry, with how many searches and pages, about how long, and about how many tokens. Change it before anything is spent: add a line, remove one, or draw it up again.

A research uses two models, and you choose both:

- Writes the report — by default, whatever the composer is set to;
- Checks the citations — by default, automatic, preferring a model on the device.

The writer never checks its own work: a model judging its own output is more lenient. The checker works one citation at a time, so a small model suits it — and one on the device costs nothing and sends nothing. When both come from the same provider, TALOS says the guarantee is weaker. When the provider publishes its prices, TALOS shows an estimate of the cost.

A model on the device can write the report too, sending nothing out; at deeper depths that takes a long time, and the screen says so.

Tap Start.

The research says what it is doing — working out the plan, looking for sources, reading the pages, checking the claims, writing the report — and how many sections are done.

- Pause saves the step under way and stops. Resume carries on from there.
- Cancel the research finishes the step already under way, keeps what it gathered, and starts no more: it will not resume.

A research that ended without a report says why, and what to do: a refused permission (resume with the right one), a run that ran out of turns, or a report written but not readable (resume, and it is written again — the gathering stays).

The report opens on its sections, its claims and its sources. Every claim carries the passage it rests on, checked twice — that the passage is really in the source, and that it really supports the claim — and a verdict: supported, partial, contested, contradicted or unchecked.

- Talk about it in a chat opens a conversation with the report.
- Ask this research more follows up on the same question.
- Export it as a Full report, a one-page Brief or an Evidence dossier in PDF; its sources as BibTeX or RIS; or the raw text as Markdown.

pagine.titolo: Set up TALOS the first time
pagine.descrizione: The first-run setup, step by step — language, your name, the PIN, a model, what TALOS may do on its own, and long work in the background.

sezioni.titolo: Set up TALOS the first time
sezioni.testo: Install the app first: Install TALOS for Android. The first time it opens, a short setup runs. Every step can be skipped and done later from Settings.

- Choose your language — follow the device, or pick English or Italian: the language of menus, settings and controls. It can be changed later in Settings → Language.
- The introduction — what TALOS is, in a few lines. Tap Set up TALOS.

- Name — what TALOS should call you. It stays on the device, and is also saved as a global memory you can read, change or delete.
- PIN — choose a PIN of at least 6 digits. It becomes the key that encrypts your chats and files on this device. Lose it and the data cannot be opened: there is no recovery. Skipped, the conversations are stored unencrypted until you set one — see Lock TALOS with a PIN.
- Model — paste a key for a provider you already pay for. It is kept in the device’s Keystore and sent only to that provider. To start with a model on the device instead, skip this step and see Run a model on the device.
- Autonomy — what TALOS may do while answering, in three lines: read what you put there, create or change things, and leave the device. Choose Ask me every time or Let it act without asking. It can be changed later, one power at a time.
- Background — a deep research or a model download takes minutes, sometimes hours, and Android suspends apps when you lock the screen. Let TALOS work in the background keeps that work alive; the device’s own extra steps, when it has any, are listed here. The Android permissions TALOS can ask for are listed in the same step, to handle now or later.

Tap Start using TALOS.

- To run the setup again: Settings → Account → Run setup again.
- To change what TALOS may do: Choose what TALOS may do.
- To add or change a model: Connect a cloud model.

pagine.descrizione: Write a task with its checklist, then let it repeat on its own — once, every day, on chosen days or at an interval — and hear back only when something changed.

sezioni.testo: Tasks are your to-dos, kept on the device and usable offline. A task can also repeat on its own: at the time you pick, TALOS runs its instruction and sends you the result — even with the app closed.

- Open Tasks from the menu and tap New task.
- Give it a title and, if you like, a description. A line written as - [ ] step becomes a check you can tick inside the task.
- Set its priority — low, normal or high — and save it.

A task is To do, In progress or Done; tap its status to move it along. TALOS can add, edit and complete tasks too, through its tools, under your powers.
Scheduled runs happen while you are away, so TALOS must be allowed to work in the background: see Keep long work running. What a run may do follows your powers, like any other request.

pagine.descrizione: TALOS updates itself — it checks once a day, downloads on Wi-Fi and asks before restarting. Check by hand or turn it off in Settings.

sezioni.testo: TALOS now updates itself: it checks once a day, downloads on Wi-Fi and asks before restarting.
Update ready appears with What’s new, the notes of the new version. Choose Restart now, or On next launch to install it the next time you open TALOS.

sezioni.titolo: Check by hand, or turn it off
sezioni.testo: In Settings › Updates: Check now looks for a new version at once, and Automatic updates turns the daily check on or off.

pagine.titolo: Dictate, listen, and use your own voice
pagine.descrizione: Speak instead of typing, have replies read aloud, and train a personal voice from twelve phrases — all on the device.

sezioni.titolo: Dictate, listen, and use your own voice
sezioni.testo: Everything about speech is in Settings → Voice, apart from the interface language. To open TALOS by voice, see Call TALOS from anywhere.

Tap the microphone in the composer and speak. Your voice becomes text on the device; the audio is never stored or sent. Dictation needs the Microphone permission, asked the first time.

Dictation language is Automatic by default: TALOS works out which language you speak, and follows it even mid-sentence. You can also follow the device’s language, or pick one.

Tap the speaker on any reply to hear it. Under Read replies aloud, choose the reading voice — a voice of the device, by default its own — and its rate and pitch, then Preview voice. Turn on Show voices for every language to choose beyond your own.

TALOS can read replies in your voice, built from twelve phrases you record once. Recording, analysis and speech all happen on the device.

- Under Personal voice, tap Download the voice engine — about 160 MB, once.
- Tap Create your voice and confirm the three statements: that you are the person being recorded, that the file stays encrypted on the device and can be deleted, and that the microphone is used only while you record.
- Find a quiet place: hold the device about 20–30 cm from your face, and speak in a natural tone.
- Record the 12 phrases — four whispered, four normal, four loud — holding the button for each. A phrase too quiet, too loud, too short or too silent is refused with the reason; record it again. It takes about 3 minutes.
- The whole set is checked together, then Encode the voice.
- Listen to how it turned out. If it does not convince you, train it again; otherwise name it and Save voice.

The recordings are encrypted with a key held in the device’s hardware keystore, and the raw audio is destroyed once the voice is built: what remains is the voice, not the recording.

### Manage voices

Each voice can be previewed, renamed or deleted, and one is in use for reading. Delete forever deletes its encryption key too: the file becomes unreadable for good, even if a copy remained. A voice marked Incompatible was made by an older engine and needs to be recorded again.

pagine.descrizione: Choose the service that answers TALOS’s searches, give it a key or an address, and allow the query to leave the device.

sezioni.testo: TALOS has no index of the web, so it asks a search service. Only the query leaves the device; the pages themselves are downloaded and read on the device, and their sources saved in your Library.

Open Settings → Search engine and pick one:

Service | What it needs | Worth knowing
Tavily | An API key | 1,000 searches a month at no cost, no card required. Built for agents.
Brave Search | An API key | An independent index; a card is required. Brave does not let TALOS save its results, so TALOS opens the sources it uses instead.
SearXNG | Your instance’s address | No third party sees the query. Turn on JSON output in the instance’s settings, or TALOS gets a web page back.
Custom endpoint | An address | Any search API that answers with a top-level results list.
DuckDuckGo | Nothing | No key and no account; not an official API, so under heavy use it can answer with a block — and TALOS says so.

Paste the key, or the address, and save it. The panel then says where things stand: Ready, a key or an address still needed, or blocked by a permission.
Turn web search off removes the service: TALOS stops offering web search to the model. Forget the key removes the key from the device; turning search back on then needs a new one.

pagine.descrizione: What the device needs, the APK and how to check it, updating without losing data, and the first model.

sezioni.testo:
- Android 8.0 or later (API 26).
- A 64-bit ARM handset or tablet (arm64-v8a).

TALOS for Android is published as a testing build: it is young, actively used software, and some behavior still depends on the device maker’s Android.

TALOS for Android is a signed APK from the TALOS releases on GitHub, not from the Play Store.

TALOS-0.1.46.apk · 147 MB · TALOS for Android 0.1.46 SHA-256d13d29dcf170bdc0e594771135fa9a5a4e097b3fa60bf3f2087f30bcb85cb0c1

Compare the file with the SHA-256 published with the release:

```
sha256sum TALOS-<version>.apk
```

Then check that it was built by the repository’s own workflow, with the GitHub CLI:

```
gh attestation verify TALOS-<version>.apk --repo Ninozzz95/talos
```

Android asks you to confirm an install from an unknown source: allow it for the app you downloaded the APK with.

To update, install the new APK over the existing app and keep the existing app installed: that preserves its data.

TALOS works with a model on the device or with the cloud model you choose.

- On the device. TALOS can browse Hugging Face and filter models by what this device can actually hold. Every quantization is shown against the device’s memory — fits, little room, or tight — before you download it.
- In the cloud. OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek or OpenRouter with your own API key, or your own Ollama endpoint.

Android permissions are requested only when a feature needs them:

Permission | Why TALOS may need it
Microphone | Dictation and the local wake word
Accessibility | Read the structure of the screen and act inside other apps
Location | Location-specific requests
Contacts | Find a person for a communication you asked for
Calendar | Read or change the calendar
Camera | Take a picture for an attachment
Notifications | Read, reply to or dismiss notifications where allowed
ADB bridge (optional) | Selected system operations Android apps cannot normally perform

Android permissions are only one layer: every TALOS tool must still pass its own read, write and outbound policy — see The assistant & device control.

pagine.descrizione: The commands you can type in the chat of TALOS for Android, after a slash.

sezioni.testo:
Type / at the start of the message to open the list; keep typing to filter it, by the command or by its name.

/new New session
Starts a new, empty chat.
/file Attach file
Opens the file chooser to attach a file to the message.
/context Open Context Vault
Opens the Library: your documents, images and saved pages.
/model Open model center
Opens Settings → Models: providers, keys and models.
/doctor Open doctor
Opens Doctor: what is ready, what is missing, and how to fix it.
/export Export report
Exports this chat, made on the device: as JSON, as Markdown, or as the list of files it used. Where files are stored is left out.
/notes Open notes
Opens your notes.
/tasks Open tasks
Opens your tasks.

pagine.descrizione: What the assistant of TALOS for Android may do on its own, when it asks you first, and what it can never be allowed to do without asking.

sezioni.testo: Before a tool runs, TALOS decides — in the app, never in the model — whether it may run, must ask you, or must not run. Three things decide it: the powers you allow, the risk of the tool, and what the conversation has already seen.

Every tool declares the powers it needs. In Settings → Agent Tools you give each power one of three answers; “Ask me every time” is the default for all of them.

readRead your things
Reading your things: the Library, notes, tasks, memory, the calendar, the device’s state. 22 tools.
writeCreate or change things
Creating or changing something: on this device, in your records, or in the world (a switch, an alarm, a vibration). 51 tools.
outboundSend anything off this device
Sending something off this device: to the network, to another app, to a person — or out loud, through the speaker. 14 tools.

execute — Running code. Part of the vocabulary, not yet declared by any tool: until one does, the setting is not shown.

allow Always allow
The tools that need this power run without asking.
ask Ask me every timedefault
Each use asks you first, on a card in the chat. The default for every power.
deny Never allow
The tools that need this power never run; the model is told your settings refuse it.

A tool that needs two powers asks if either one asks, and does not run if either one is refused.

When a tool must ask, a card shows what it is about to do, with its arguments. “Allow” runs this call and saves nothing. “Always allow” saves a grant for this tool on this device: from then on it runs without asking, until you revoke it in Settings → Agent Tools. “Don’t allow” stops it; the model is told you declined. “Decide later” leaves the card for later.

When the model asks for several such steps at once, and one of them cannot be undone or together they reach R2, TALOS shows them as one plan: you can take steps out, then approve the rest at once. An R4 step is never part of a plan; it keeps its own card. How long an approval holds is set in Settings → Agent Tools → Approval duration: “This message”, or “The conversation, while trusted”, which ends as soon as pages or documents from outside come into it.

Can be undone: edited again, switched back, deleted.
compensable 2 tools
Cannot be undone, but another action can make up for it.
irreversible 13 tools
Cannot be undone: there is no bin, or the world has already seen it.

Three marks of each tool say what it brings into the conversation and what it can let out:

private data readsPrivateData
Reads something of yours: files, notes, memory, the calendar, where you are, the screen.
untrusted content readsUntrustedContent
Brings in text someone else wrote — a page, a document, a notification — which may carry instructions.
leaves the device canTransmit
Can send something off the device: to the network, to another app, to a person, or aloud.

The conversation remembers whether private data and untrusted content have already come in. Two rules follow, checked before every call:

- Effective risk. A tool that can let something out climbs one level of risk if untrusted content has already come in, and one more if private data has, up to R4. A search after reading a web page and your notes is not the same search as on an empty conversation.
- The trifecta. When private data and untrusted content have both come in, and the next tool can let something out, TALOS asks you — even for a tool you set to always allow, save the exceptions below — and the card says why. It asks rather than refuses, so the protection is never worth switching off.

“Always allow” is not offered when the card is forced by the trifecta or by a tool that always asks, nor when the effective risk is R4 and the tool writes (the card says why). Three tools are exceptions, decided one by one where asking every time would make the tool useless: for them the choice is always offered and, once made, holds — web_search, device_screen_drive, app_azione.

sezioni.titolo: When a tool does not run
sezioni.testo:
The model is told why, in a result with one of these codes, so that it can tell you the truth instead of guessing:

Code | Meaning
TALOS_TOOL_DISABLED | The tool is switched off in Settings → Agent Tools.
TALOS_TOOL_ARGUMENTS_INVALID | The arguments did not match the tool’s parameters; nothing was asked or run.
TALOS_TOOL_DENIED_BY_POLICY | A power the tool needs is set to “Never allow”.
TALOS_TOOL_DECLINED | You answered “Don’t allow” on the card.
TALOS_TOOL_PREMISE_ABSENT | What the tool acts on is not there (the torch is already off, the file does not exist): nothing was asked or changed.
TALOS_TOOL_PREMISE_UNKNOWN | For a tool that must be sure of its target, TALOS could not check it: not run.
TALOS_TOOL_CONSENT_BUSY | Another card was already waiting for an answer.
TALOS_TOOL_AWAITING_AUTHORIZATION | The card has not been answered yet. This is not a refusal; the model should say the request is pending.
TALOS_TOOL_POSTCONDITION_FAILED | The tool ran, and the check after it shows the change did not happen.
TALOS_TOOL_EFFECT_UNKNOWN | The tool ran, and TALOS cannot tell whether the change happened: the model must not claim it did.
TALOS_DB_KEY_LOCKED | The app is locked: its storage cannot be read until you unlock it.
A tool the security catalog does not list — a forged tool among them — is checked against the cautious default: R3, irreversible, private data, untrusted content, leaves the device.

pagine.descrizione: New tools for TALOS for Android, built from a manifest of steps rather than code: what they can do, the manifest, and how it is checked.

sezioni.testo:
A forged tool is a flow of steps over capabilities TALOS already has, described in a .talostool manifest (talos.local-tool.v1) — never code the model writes. Import one on the Tool Forge screen, or ask the assistant to make one with tool_create. Either way it is checked before it installs, and it stays off until you turn it on. Each version is kept, so you can roll back; rolling back turns the tool off again.

Once on, it is a tool like the others, named dynamic:<id>: it needs the powers its steps need, its marks are worked out from them, and one whose steps reach R4 always asks. It passes through the same consent.

What a step can call:

Capability | What it does | Power | Risk
tasks.list | Read local TALOS tasks.input up to 1 KiB | Read | R1
tasks.create | Create a local TALOS task.input up to 16 KiB | Write | R2
tasks.setStatus | Change local task status.input up to 1 KiB | Write | R2
notes.list | Read local TALOS notes.input up to 1 KiB | Read | R1
notes.create | Create a local TALOS note.input up to 32 KiB | Write | R2
notes.update | Update a local TALOS note.input up to 32 KiB | Write | R2
memory.search | Search active local TALOS memories.input up to 1 KiB | Read | R2
memory.create | Create durable TALOS memory.input up to 32 KiB | Write | R3

schema stringrequired
Always talos.local-tool.v1. Valuestalos.local-tool.v1
id stringrequired
The tool’s permanent id: 3–64 characters, lowercase letters, digits, ., _ and -. The tool is named dynamic:<id>.
version numberrequired
A positive integer; each new version keeps the previous ones, so you can roll back.
title stringrequired
The name shown on the Tool Forge screen and on the consent card (1–120 characters).
description stringrequired
What the tool does, for you and for the model (1–1000 characters).
createdAt stringrequired
When this version was written (ISO 8601).
parentVersion numberrequired
The version this one replaces, or null for the first.
execution stringrequired
Always declarative-flow: a forged tool is a flow of steps, never code. Valuesdeclarative-flow
installScope stringrequired
Always device: the tool lives on this device. Valuesdevice
network objectrequired
Whether the tool may reach the network (forbidden) or only the exact hosts listed (allowlist). No capability of this release uses the network.
credentialRequirements array of objectrequired
Keys or accounts the tool needs, each with its purpose and the hosts it may reach. A tool whose access is missing cannot run.

What the model steps of the flow need: structured output, context, privacy (local only, local preferred, or remote allowed), reasoning effort.

The tool’s parameters, as a JSON Schema subset; the model is offered exactly these.

The shape of the result, as a JSON Schema subset.

The steps: an entry node, a bound on transitions, and the nodes.

Data the tool keeps between runs, with its own fields and a size limit.

When the tool would run by itself (manual, schedule, app-resume, task-changed). Accepted in the manifest; this release does not start a tool on its own.

A summary card for the result: its title and the values it shows.

The flow starts at its entry node and follows next (or then and else) from node to node. It may not loop back on itself; repetition is a bounded foreach.

pagine.descrizione: What TALOS for Android asks of Android, why, and the permissions its package declares.

sezioni.testo: Settings → Privacy and permissions lists what TALOS may reach on the device, with the reason for each, in these words. A permission Android asks about is asked the first time TALOS needs it, never when the app starts.

Android asks you in a dialog, the first time TALOS needs it — never at start.

Microphone
Dictation. Your voice becomes text on this device, and the audio is never stored or sent anywhere.
Notifications
Progress for long tasks. Without it those tasks still run — you just will not see how far along they are.
Contacts
Sending a message to someone by name. TALOS looks up the name you said and takes the number for that one message — it does not read, copy or send your address book anywhere.
Calendar
Answering "what do I have tomorrow", and putting an appointment in when you ask. Reading and writing are two separate permissions, asked at different moments, and every single appointment TALOS writes is confirmed by you first. Nothing leaves the device.
Unread mail count
Answering "how much unread mail do I have". TALOS reads Gmail’s own counter on this device and gets a number, per account — never the sender, the subject or the text of an email, which this route cannot reach at all. Nothing leaves the device.
Where you are
Answering questions about places near you — a restaurant tonight, the closest shop, how long it takes to get somewhere. TALOS reads the location at the moment it needs it, never in the background and never while it is closed, and the coordinates go no further than the answer you asked for.
Camera
Taking a photo to attach to a chat. The picture goes where you send it and nowhere else; TALOS never opens the camera on its own.

Android grants it with the app; nothing is asked.

Network access
Reaching the AI provider you configured. Nothing is sent anywhere else, and nothing leaves the device until you send a message.

A system setting that keeps long tasks alive in the background.

Running in the background
Long tasks — a research, a model download — keep going after you leave the app or lock the screen. Without it the device suspends TALOS within seconds and the work is lost; this is the one setting that decides it.

Only you can turn these on, by hand, in a screen of the system settings; TALOS can open the screen for you.

Screen reading
Reading the visible screen so TALOS can understand the app you are using and control it when you ask. It does not enable an accessibility button, a volume-key shortcut or listening to volume keys; Android Accessibility settings remain the only place to enable or disable this access.
Reading your notifications
Telling you what arrived and replying for you. TALOS sees the notifications of every app on this device, including their text — this is the widest window it has into your device, and it stays closed until you open it by hand in system settings.
Running commands on this device
Doing things Android does not offer apps: listing what is installed, changing system settings, reaching parts of the device no app can. It runs with the same powers as a computer plugged in over USB. Nothing works until you pair it once with a six-digit code you read on your own screen, and every command still passes your permission gate.

Android lets any app do this; the only gate is yours, in Agent Tools.

App lock
Unlocking TALOS with your fingerprint or face. The key stays in the device’s secure hardware and never reaches TALOS itself.
Files you choose
Attaching documents. TALOS can only open the files you pick in the system chooser; it has no access to the rest of your storage.
Controlling the device
Torch, volume, alarms, wallpaper, opening an app or a settings screen. None of these needs a permission — Android lets any app do them — so the only thing standing between a request and the action is the permission gate you control in Tools.
Models that run here
A model downloaded onto this device answers without the network. What you write to it never leaves the device — not to us, not to anyone — and it keeps working with the device in flight mode.

pagine.descrizione: What changed in each version of TALOS CLI, newest first, from the changelog of the release in force.

sezioni.testo: What changed in each version of TALOS CLI, as its changelog says — read from the npm package of 0.6.14. Newest first; every published version is listed on Versions, and the three apps share one timeline.

Released Oct 25, 2026 · On npm

### Added

- Artifacts the model updates keep every version. When the model changes an artifact it made earlier, the change is a new version of the same Library entry, kept in the project’s Library folder (.harness-ui-library), never in your own files. The version is part of the turn’s checkpoint, so talos checkpoint undo takes it back. talos library versions <id> lists the versions, oldest first. talos library restore <id> <version> brings an old one back as a NEW version, so the history is never rewritten. An id or a version that is not there says so, with the commands that show the right ones.

### Fixed

- talos remote no longer reaches the model. Before, it was sent as the prompt «remote», which cost a paid turn. It now says that remote control is not in TALOS CLI yet, and where to find it (TALOS Desktop), without starting anything.
- A compaction at the emergency threshold says so. When the conversation reached 90% of the window (1.2 times the threshold when the window is unknown), the line said «at 75% of the window», which is the normal rule. It now says what started it, live and after --resume, and protocol v2 context.compacted carries emergency.
- The read row is right in more cases. An extracted document whose text starts indented no longer counts the coverage warning as lines of the file. In a terminal narrower than about 34 columns, the count moves to the detail line so the row stays on one line.

### Changed

- The engine is TALOS Desktop’s current one, with its device folders, remote control and sending a file to a device. The CLI does not offer these to the model, because they need a paired device, which the CLI does not handle yet. If a saved conversation mentions them, they are shown by name.
