conversation is already past its emergency limit, and only while it still covers this history; Stop ends the wait. If it arrives but is not enough, it is kept and only the rest is summarized on top of it, so the history is never summarized twice.
- /compact without the Context Engine compacts the way the automatic compaction does: on the light model, from what the model really sees, keeping what the automatic one keeps, and replacing the previous summary. Before, it kept only the first two messages and wrote on the conversation’s model. Every summary now carries a fingerprint of the history it covers, and is never applied to another history.
- A summary the turn waits for has a ceiling: 10 minutes, or 5 minutes with nothing coming from the model; one that was already being written when the turn needed it is waited for 10 minutes at most. Past it TALOS stops waiting, compacts without the model (CTX_COMPACTION_TIMEOUT with the Context Engine) and the turn goes on.
- The reasoning of past rounds is removed, no longer cut to 300 characters, when the Context Engine clears old tool results, for every provider: a past reasoning cut short and ending in «…» is a changed reasoning, which Z.AI and Qwen answer worse to, while a missing one is accepted as it is. Reasoning of 300 characters or less stays as it is. Signed reasoning blocks were never touched and still are not.
- Providers (the Desktop’s current engine): Z.AI and Qwen keep their past reasoning (clear_thinking:false, preserve_thinking on qwen3.8-flash); Vertex AI’s thinking off, by model; DeepSeek’s own request shape; the cache marker sent only to providers that accept it; together, deepinfra and novita; OpenRouter’s session_id from the conversation; MiniMax M3.1 Flash’s effort on its Anthropic address; Gemini without a limit asks for 65,535 output tokens.
- A compaction that did not happen is said. When the Context Engine fails and the simple compaction takes over, when the history had to be realigned, or when a summary failed, was cut short or came back empty, the conversation shows one warning with its reason and code (COMPACTION_FALLBACK, COMPACTION_HISTORY_REALIGNED, COMPACTION_FAILED). Before, all of these were silent. A model whose window is too small for TALOS’s tools and the part a summary always keeps is said once for that window, with both numbers and COMPACTION_WINDOW_TOO_SMALL, and no summary is paid for it. The same warnings are in talos -p output: in json and stream-json (v1 and v2) as a warning event, in text on stderr.
- A message too large for the model is neither summarized nor paid for. When your newest message alone does not fit the model’s window together with the system and the tools, the turn stops before anything is paid: before anything reaches the provider when TALOS knows the window, otherwise at the provider’s refusal (after a free shortening, when one could help), whose window TALOS then remembers for that model while it stays open (so the next request is judged befo

re it is sent, and the attachment goes at once; a new talos -p, even with --resume, meets one more refusal). The message goes back into the composer (unless you have already started typing a new one) and a small dialog says how big it is, the model’s window and, when one is kept, the room for the answer, with one action, «Send as attachment»: the same text goes again, and the model gets its start and its end and reads the rest from a file saved with the conversation. «Edit the message» or Esc closes the dialog and leaves the text to shorten. When not even the attachment would fit, or the message has images, the dialog offers only «Edit the message» and says why. In the conversation the message stays, marked «Not sent», also after a restart. In talos -p the run ends with REQUEST_TOO_LARGE (exit 70) and its numbers: in text on stderr, and in json and stream-json (v1 and v2) as requestTooLarge (in v1 json, under error.details); protocol v2 also has the durable event request.not_sent. --attach-if-too-large sends such a message as an attachment instead, on a new turn, with --resume and when it waits in the queue; when the attachment cannot fit either, the error says to shorten the message or choose a larger model.
- Paused automatic summaries are said once. When the automatic summaries stop because the last ones did not make the conversation shorter, or because it filled up again right after each one, one warning says which and that /compact forces one (COMPACTION_PAUSED; in talos -p text on stderr). It is said again only when the summaries pause anew. Older long messages shortened for the model, with their full text saved, are not announced; older tool results shortened or older images replaced with a placeholder, without a summary, are said as that («Shortened older tool results for the model, nothing summarized», «Replaced 2 older images with a placeholder…»), not as a summary.
- When the provider says the conversation does not fit, it is shortened toward what fits. The free shortenings come first, then at most one paid summary, then a summary TALOS writes itself without a model; at most three retries, and never the same request twice. A summary is paid for only when it can remove at least a tenth of the compaction threshold, measured on the real summaries of this conversation (and, for how TALOS’s count compares with the provider’s, of this model). A compaction the refusal started is said as that, not by the automatic rule; a summary written without a model is said as that, with its reason («Shortened older messages without a model summary (the provider said the conversation did not fit)»), never as a model’s. If the turn then fails, that shortening is undone and its line leaves the screen, so the next turn starts from the whole conversation and nothing says it was shortened. After --resume, and after a /resume of the conversation already open on the screen, each of these lines comes back once with the same words and numbers it had live (protocol

v2 reads it from the saved conversation as a durable context.compacted, and its undoing as context.compaction.undone). When it still does not fit, the error says whether it was shortened first and the provider’s own count when it gave one («The conversation is too long for this model even after shortening it (the provider counted 9,000 tokens; its maximum is 8,192)»); talos -p in json and stream-json (v1 and v2) carries it as contextFull. On the screen such an error was said as «The model provider did not accept the request», and a provider’s empty balance on HTTP 429 as a rate limit: the screen now keeps the provider’s class of the failure (protocol v2 providerClass). Text in Chinese, Japanese and Korean is now counted the way the providers count it, so such a conversation is compacted in time.
- /compact says why it did not compact. «Context is already compact.» is said only when there is nothing to summarize. Otherwise the answer says what happened, with its code, and that nothing was replaced: a summary would save little because the older part is too small (COMPACTION_LITTLE_GAIN); what is kept word for word (your first request, your latest requests and the latest exchanges) already fills the space (COMPACTION_AT_MINIMUM); the summary was written but would have made the conversation longer, so it was not used (COMPACTION_INEFFECTIVE); or the summary failed, was cut off or came back empty. When the model’s window is too small even for TALOS’s tools and the part a summary always keeps, /compact says so after its answer, with both numbers, and points to /model.
- A turn quiet for 45 seconds is noted in the development log (talos logs), never printed on stderr in talos -p.
- A shell result tells the model that stdout and stderr are mixed. What the model reads of a command now starts with [shell output: stdout and stderr combined in arrival order; stream identity is not preserved], before the exit N line, and so does the content of a shell tool’s result in talos -p --output-format json and stream-json (v1 and v2); the exit code is still its own field. The screen does not show that line.

- A full context window on Anthropic, OpenAI Responses or Gemini direct now compacts and tries again, like every other provider. It came back as «response incomplete, try again», and in streaming it was sent again up to 10 times. A response cut by the output limit on those providers is now continued, as on the others.
- /compact no longer says «Context is already compact» when it failed. «Already compact» now means only that there was nothing to compact. A summary that failed, was cut short, came back empty, answered with a tool call or was refused, or a Context Engine summary that failed, says what went wrong, with its code, and that nothing was replaced.
- A conversation with the characters U+2028 or U+2029 in it no longer reads as damaged after a restart. The saved journal was read line by line with Node’s readline, which takes them for line ends.
- /compact while a tool call has no result yet says so («A tool call in this conversation has no result yet…»), instead of «An extension failed».
- A read row says how much of the file the model got. Now that a read reaches the model whole, its row counted only the last 8 KB the screen keeps: a page of 2,000 of a file’s 3,000 lines showed as «304 lines». It now says «2,000 of 3,000 lines», and a whole long read counts all its lines.
- The engine is TALOS Desktop’s current one.

Released Oct 21, 2026 · On npm

### Changed

- Gemini connected directly gets the full list of tools again. With the lighter list of 0.6.11, TALOS Desktop measured slightly fewer code tasks solved on Gemini direct (27 of 30 instead of 29), so for the gemini provider and gemini: models the tools used only on request are sent in full again. Every other provider keeps the lighter list, OpenRouter’s Google models included; TALOS_ATTREZZI_DIFFERITI=0 still sends the full list to all.
- The trust of a hook or MCP server now also covers the scripts it loads through a link. In 0.6.11 a script the command named through a junction or link pointing outside the project was pinned, but one it only imported through such a link was not. Now it is pinned by the name written in the project, and its own imports are followed too: a JavaScript file’s from where the file really is, as Node resolves them, a Python file’s from its written name. A file Node really runs outside the project, reached that way, is pinned by its real path (its own imports are not followed): one with an extension Node adds by itself (.js, .cjs, .mjs, .json, .node), or any file the import names in full, such as import "../shared.ts". Two links that point at each other are followed once and no longer lengthen the list. On a project whose hooks or MCP servers import through such a link, the trust is asked once more, with the usual sentence.
- Python imports are read as Python runs them, inside the project too: import a.b.c covers a/__init__.py and a/b/__init__.py, from . import x and from .. import x count their dots as folder levels, and through a link from pkg import a, b covers pkg/a.py and pkg/b.py as well as pkg/__init__.py. The trust of a Python hook or MCP server may be asked once more if its scripts import several modules on one line (import os, helper), import a dotted name from a package with an __init__.py (import a.b, from a.b import x), or use relative imports (from . import x, from .. import x).
- A trust check has a ceiling on the paths it resolves (100,000 per check), like the ceiling of 2,000 scripts it already had: past it the rest is marked as not checked in the trust record, as past the other two ceilings. The trust question does not show that mark yet.
- The engine is TALOS Desktop’s current one.

### Fixed

- No more paid summary that nothing used. After a turn with a long history (past 200,000 tokens) the CLI asked the model, in the background, for a summary of the conversation that it then never used; 0.6.11 paid for it too. It is no longer asked. /compact and the automatic compaction work as before.
Released Oct 21, 2026 · On npm

- The theme’s background fills the whole window. Around the screen TALOS draws, the terminal kept its own background: Windows Terminal’s padding, the scrollbar gutter and, on Windows, the last row showed as a black border. While the screen is up TALOS now sets the terminal’s default background to the theme’s (OSC 11) and gives it back when it leaves (OSC 111), also on an error. Not inside tmux or GNU screen, not with the mono theme, and never with TALOS_TUI_TERMINAL_BACKGROUND=0. On Windows only inside Windows Terminal: the console Windows uses for other terminals (VS Code’s, for example) drops the sequence that gives the background back, so there it stays off unless TALOS_TUI_TERMINAL_BACKGROUND=1. The same rule holds inside WSL. On Windows, a terminal that names itself (VS Code opened from a Windows Terminal tab, for example) does not count as Windows Terminal; inside WSL that terminal cannot be told apart, so there use TALOS_TUI_TERMINAL_BACKGROUND=0 if the colour stays.
- The model starts with a lighter list of tools. The tools used only on request (notes, tasks, library, research, automations, provider exclusions and the like) are no longer sent in full with every request: the model finds and loads them when it needs them (tool_search, tool_describe, tool_call), and permissions, Plan mode and approvals apply to the real tool as before. The first request of a short task drops from 51 tools and about 54,000 characters to 23 tools and about 29,000. A task that needs one of those tools can take a step or two more. TALOS_ATTREZZI_DIFFERITI=0 sends the full list again. With Gemini connected directly (gemini: models) TALOS Desktop measured slightly fewer code tasks solved with the lighter list (27 of 30 instead of 29); the next version sends Gemini the full list, and until then TALOS_ATTREZZI_DIFFERITI=0 does it.
- The model is told where it is working. The engine now gives the model the project folder’s full path and the real platform (Windows, Linux, macOS); the old platform line is gone. When the model reads or lists /<folder>/x or <folder>/x and nothing by that first name exists, it gets x inside the project, before every permission check, and the tool result says so. Writes and edits keep the path exactly as written (only ~ is expanded), so a project laid out as myproj/myproj/... can still be created.
- One rule, shared with TALOS Desktop, for the project scripts a trust covers. A hook or MCP server is trusted together with the project scripts it runs; the CLI and the desktop app now read those scripts with the same code, and a repeated check reads an unchanged file only once (about 0.1 s instead of 1 s on a large project). Nothing changes for a trust you already gave, except one rare case: a script the command names through a junction or link that points outside the project is now pinned too, so that trust is asked once more. A script it only imports through such a link is still not covered, as in 0.6.10.
- The engine is TALOS Desktop’s curre

nt one. A refused delegation now says only its reason, in plain English. Three new errors are worded with what to do next: a model the provider no longer serves, a hooks file TALOS cannot read, an MCP server script TALOS cannot read. The device’s local engine («On this device») is not offered by the CLI, and neither are the desktop’s tools for undoing file changes and pairing devices.
- The project folder’s full path now reaches the model’s provider, a cloud provider too. On most computers that path contains the name of your user account (for example C:\Users\<name>\...).

Released Oct 17, 2026 · On npm

### Fixed

- A long ChatGPT chat no longer breaks after the project changes. When the project changed between two messages (a file written, a new folder, an edited AGENTS.md), TALOS adds a project update to the request; in a long chat that update was marked for caching in a form the ChatGPT plan and the OpenAI Responses API refuse (HTTP 400 «Invalid value: ‘text’»), so that message and every later one of the chat failed at once with «The request to the ChatGPT plan did not complete». The same malformed request went to Anthropic, the Z.AI and MiniMax Anthropic-compatible endpoints and Gemini. The update is now sent as plain text to every provider TALOS talks to natively, Anthropic-style providers get the cache marker where their API reads it, and a chat that already broke works again.
- A command that ends with a line break is no longer refused. A command with a trailing or leading line break, a blank line, a break after && or |, or a final ; was refused as «unsupported shell composition», even in Full access. A line with nothing on it is now just skipped; a command left incomplete (git status &&) is still refused.
- The ChatGPT plan error no longer says «The ChatGPT sign-in failed» when the sign-in is fine and a request did not complete; it says so, and points at talos logs.

Released Oct 17, 2026 · On npm

### Fixed

- talos mcp trust, talos mcp test, talos hook trust and talos hook dry-run no longer fail with MCP_TRUST_INVALIDATED / HOOK_TRUST_INVALIDATED for a server or hook that runs a script of the project: they pin the same content as the project trust, the project scripts included. A script changed after the review is refused by mcp test, hook dry-run and the session until it is trusted again.
- talos mcp test works again: in 0.6.8 it failed for every server («Cannot read properties of undefined»), because the start-up line of the MCP client’s bundled code read a name that the code itself redefined.

### Added

- When a trusted MCP server does not start, TALOS says so on the screen and in -p (on stderr in text, as a warning event with code MCP_START_FAILED and its serverId in --json, stream-json and --protocol v2): «MCP server “x” did not start: <reason>. Its tools are not available in this turn. Check it with: talos mcp test x». It is said on every run of a session where the server is down. Before, it was silent and the model only met an unknown tool.

Released Oct 17, 2026 · On npm

### Added

- In --protocol v2, agent.changed and a delegation result carry the agent’s name (null for agents started before this version).

### Changed

- A sub-agent is called by its name everywhere: in the agents panel and page, the footer, the line that says which agent asks for a permission, and the «Agent finished» row and notification. Its name is its task’s short name, and two sub-agents with the same task are told apart: «Write the tests» and «Write the tests-2». In the same TALOS, a conversation that starts with the name of another one gets «-2» too.
- A long turn no longer stops to be summarised. When a conversation grows past the point where TALOS starts summarising it, the summary is prepared in the background while the request goes out whole. A request that still fits the model’s window is not held back for a summary already on its way. If the provider then says the context is full, TALOS waits for that summary and sends the request again, once.
- With nobody in front (talos -p, a command), TALOS tells the engine so on every turn instead of once for the whole process: what would wait for a person (a plan, a question, an MCP server’s form, a file to adopt) is refused at once with the reason, and a conversation started with talos -p and resumed on the screen gets its plan card and questions back. The same holds for a conversation forked with nobody in front.
- In Full access TALOS reads and writes a project’s secret files without asking, as it does for every other file. What still asks in Full access: reading a login credential of this computer (the SSH keys, ~/.npmrc, ~/.aws and the like), opening a network path (\\server\share), and the actions only a person may take; with nobody in front they are refused. A login credential is recognised however it is written (%USERPROFILE%, $env:USERPROFILE, any other variable, a short name, a link) and under another name too (a hard link), in a command as in a read, in every mode. A login credential of this computer is never written, in any mode. In the other permission modes a project secret still asks first.

- A program planted in a project folder no longer runs in place of the real one. On Windows a program called by its bare name (git, node) was looked for in the project folder first: a git.exe inside a cloned project ran on your computer as soon as you opened TALOS there, even in a folder you never trusted, and a node.cmd ran in place of Node inside the sandbox. TALOS now turns that search off for itself and for every command it runs; .\program still runs a program of the folder.
- talos -p --protocol v2 no longer approves reading a secret file on its own. Asked to read a file such as .env or a private key, it answered «yes» by itself in every permission mode, and the content reached the provider; the other output formats refused it. Now every format decides it by the same rules: refused when nobody is there to answer, except a project’s secret in Full access. A permission request in --protocol v2 names a secret’s class as secret.
- A trusted project’s hooks and MCP servers are pinned with their scripts. Trusting a project remembered a hook’s or a server’s command line, not the project script it runs: editing that script afterwards (outside .talos/) ran the new code in the next session without asking. Now the trust covers what really runs: a hook’s command is read the way the engine reads it, a name finds its file the way Node and Python do (node srv, node ., python -m pkg, npm run start with its pre and post scripts, npm start’s server.js), a script in a folder of its own pins that whole folder, and the files a pinned script imports are followed in turn, folders and packages included. A changed file asks for the trust again. A project always opens: installed libraries (node_modules, a Python virtual environment) are not checked, a link is remembered by where it points, a folder given to a server as data is not read, past 10,000 files a script folder is checked only in part, and past 2,000 scripts the chain of imports is not followed further. A project trusted before whose hooks or servers run a project script asks once after the update, and says so: «TALOS now also checks the scripts».
- talos -p answers a sub-agent’s permission requests. Only the main conversation’s requests were answered: a sub-agent that asked to read .env held the run until it timed out. Each sub-agent’s request is now decided by the same rules, so a secret is refused with nobody in front and a plain read inside the project is allowed.

- talos -p no longer stays open after its answer while a summary prepared in the background finishes: the summary is cancelled when TALOS leaves.
- A token-count endpoint that never answers no longer costs 10 seconds on every request: after the first time it is skipped for ten minutes, and TALOS estimates at once.

Released Oct 16, 2026 · On npm

### Changed

- Stop ends a command’s whole process tree on Linux and macOS. Outside Windows each command TALOS runs starts in its own process group, so Stop, a time limit and leaving TALOS end the command and everything it started. A side effect: a command started by TALOS has no terminal of its own, so it can no longer ask for a password on your terminal (git, ssh, sudo); give it the password another way (a credential helper, an SSH agent, sudo -n or a sudoers rule).
- The short title of a conversation is at most 80 characters with «…», and ends on a whole word when one ends late enough.

### Fixed

- With a model whose window is known (set by you with talos config set models.<id>.contextWindow, or known to TALOS), an OpenAI-compatible server or proxy that does not count tokens could fail every turn: TALOS asks it to count the request first, and a «yes» without a count ended the turn. A count that cannot be read, a busy or failing counter, the network, or a counter slower than 10 seconds now give an estimate, never a failed turn.
- With OpenAI set to an address of your choice (an OpenAI-compatible server), its models whose names do not start with gpt- were left out: /model did not list them and a sub-agent asked to run on one was refused. Every model the server lists is now kept, except the ones that cannot hold a conversation (speech, embeddings, images, transcription, realtime). OpenAI’s own address keeps its list as before.
- With TALOS_MAX_RETRIES=0, a provider’s «too many requests» no longer says «TALOS retried»: it says that it did not retry.
- On the ChatGPT plan, a refusal the plan sends at the start of an answer is read at once, instead of being taken for a server error and sent again ten times.
- talos -p --resume <id> --model <model>: when another TALOS changed the conversation’s model a moment before, the model you asked for is the one used.
- Automations: on Linux and macOS a Ctrl+C on talos automation run or serve stops gracefully again (with the new process groups the first Ctrl+C ended TALOS at once); when TALOS leaves on Ctrl+C it stops the sub-agents of its runs too, not only the runs; a Ctrl+C that has nothing left to stop says so; a run that could not start says why in words, never with a raw message from the disk; the error messages of talos automation say what happened and what to do; the task board no longer marks every linked automation as missing when its store cannot be loaded.
- Plan mode with nobody in front (talos -p --permission-mode plan) tells the model to write the plan in its answer, and a plan it tries to present anyway is refused with that sentence.
Released Oct 15, 2026 · On npm

- The start screen shows the TALOS medal. The mark becomes a two-layer hexagonal medal — a bevelled rim lit from the top left, milled ticks, a raised inner layer with six rivets, fine guilloché rings and the mark in relief — drawn with the terminal’s own cells: the background of each cell is the metal, the dots are the details. It is bigger on a wide terminal and smaller on a narrow or short one, and the block letters of «TALOS» now stay down to 48 columns. Same stages, same 5.2 seconds, any key skips it. Where TALOS does not paint the background, only the gold dots are drawn.
- The ChatGPT plan’s usage limit is told plainly. While TALOS waits for the limit to come back, the line under the conversation says so, with the time it tries again and that /model goes on now with another model. If the limit ends the turn, the message stands out (it was a grey line that read like any error) and says when the limit comes back, when ChatGPT says it.
- Automations work again, and say what to do in plain words. talos automation add "check the build and tell me what broke" --when "weekdays 09:00" makes one in this project; --when takes a short phrase: “every 30m”, “every 2h”, “hourly”, “daily 09:00”, “weekdays 09:00”, “weekly mon 09:00”, “once 2026-10-20 09:00”, a cron line or “manual”. It runs while talos automation serve is running (talos automation install-runner --yes starts it when you sign in to Windows), or now with talos automation run <id>, which waits for the end and prints the report. list, show, history, edit, enable, disable and delete do the rest. Nobody watches a run: it uses the mode you chose (--mode, by default it may edit files in its folder), and anything that would ask you is refused and the model is told, so a run never waits for you. It works only in a folder you have trusted. Automations made by 0.6.5 and before never ran (every run failed with «task list unavailable»): they are listed as «old format» and can be deleted and made again. schedule and dry-run are gone: edit --when and show replace them. In the conversation, /automations shows them; making and changing them from the screen comes later. One TALOS process runs a profile’s automations at a time: while serve runs, talos automation run <id> hands the run to it and waits for the end; a second serve waits to take over; serve --once says another process is running them; a run that finds nobody running them runs the ones that come due meanwhile too, and on Ctrl+C stops what it runs before it leaves. A laptop that slept does not make a waiting process take over a live one. history, show and /automations say every run in words (done, failed, skipped, and why). A run whose model hands work to sub-agents waits for them before the process leaves, and their requests are answered in the run’s mode too.
- The model is told what its mode really does when nobody is in front. In talos -p, in a one-shot command and in an automation, what would ask you is refused, and the model now reads that, i
nstead of «being asked is not a refusal».

- A turn interrupted while a tool was about to run no longer breaks the session: resuming it used to fail at every turn with CTX_HISTORY_DIVERGED. A session already broken that way now says so in plain words and offers /fork, which continues the conversation in a new session.

### Known limits

- Tested on Windows 11 x64 only; Node.js 24 (24.18 or later in the 24 line).
- Context compaction with a local Ollama model is not yet verified end to end.
- A local provider that answers 401/403 without needing a key can be set aside as if its key were wrong.
- The OpenRouter sign-in is tested against a stand-in for OpenRouter; the exchange with the real service follows its published contract.

### Verification

- CLI unit suite on the release tree: 1870 tests, 1866 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail. Acceptance on the built CLI in a synthetic terminal: 263/263.
- The package proof (scripts/prove-standalone.ts), 16/16 on talos-code-0.2.0.tgz (1.76 MB, 407 files): installed into an empty prefix outside the repository, hermetic profile, fake provider on 127.0.0.1; every loaded module resolved inside the package; nothing written inside the package; no stale build output; no outbound request.

Released Sep 25, 2026 · On npm

The first public release: npm i -g talos-code, then talos.

### Added

- An interactive terminal screen and a headless mode (talos -p, --json, --output-format stream-json) on the TALOS kernel, the same one the desktop runs, carried inside the package: it reads no file of a TALOS checkout.
- Providers from the TALOS registry (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Mistral, Groq, xAI and more) and local engines with no key (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp). Keys are typed in hidden input and kept in the operating system’s credential store; a key already in the environment is used only after you agree once.
- Per-tool permissions (allow, ask, deny) with six modes, project trust for hooks, MCP servers, plugins and commands.
- /undo restores the files a turn changed, from checkpoints kept outside the repository and outside Git.
- Sessions: /resume, /fork, export and import (an imported session never runs anything by itself), prompt history.
- Context: with a known window of 64k tokens or more, compaction at half of it, said on screen; after a summary the model did not write properly, automatic compaction pauses (60 s, 5 min, 15 min) and says so, while /compact runs at once.
- /theme with ten accents, /help by group, /status, /retry, /copy, @ file completion that respects .gitignore, Ctrl+R history search.
- talos update asks the npm registry whether a newer version exists and prints the npm command; it changes nothing.
- talos doctor and a redacted talos diagnostic bundle. No telemetry.

### Known limits

- Tested on Windows 11 x64 only; Node.js 24 (24.18 or later in the 24 line).
- Context compaction with a local Ollama model is not yet verified end to end.
- A local provider that answers 401/403 without needing a key can be set aside as if its key were wrong.

### Verification

- CLI unit suite on the released tree: 1839 tests, 1835 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail. Acceptance on the built CLI in a synthetic terminal: 246/247 on the aligned kernel (the one red is a known idle-frame flake).
- The package proof (scripts/prove-standalone.ts), 16/16 on the tarball itself: installed into an empty prefix outside the repository, hermetic profile, fake provider on 127.0.0.1; every loaded module resolved inside the package; nothing written inside the package; no stale build output.
- Installed from the registry after publication: talos --version answered 0.1.0, talos update --check answered up to date.

pagine.descrizione: MCP servers, hooks, plugins, your own commands and forged tools — and why none of them runs before you trust it.

sezioni.testo:
A project can teach TALOS new things. Each of them is code or instructions that came with the project, so each one is trusted explicitly before it runs — first the project, then the extension itself.

Extension | What it is | Manage it with
MCP server | A program that offers tools over the Model Context Protocol. | talos mcp · /mcp
Hook | A command of yours that runs when something happens in a session. | talos hook · /hooks
Plugin | A package of commands, skills, hooks or MCP servers. | talos plugin · /plugins
Custom command | A Markdown file whose text becomes a prompt, with arguments {{arg1}}, {{arg2}}… In the interactive screen it is a slash command. | talos command
Forged tool | A tool TALOS built during a session, as a declarative package: validated, scanned and simulated before use. | talos forge · /forge

- The project. talos project trust trusts the project and the current snapshot of its executable files; talos project status shows what is trusted and why. When those files change, the trust no longer covers them.
- The extension. Each MCP server, hook and plugin is trusted on its own, and can be untrusted at any time.

A hook or a plugin can also be quarantined: it is denied until released, and release does not restore trust. Installing a plugin does not make it run either: the project’s trust must cover the new package first. Every action an extension takes still goes through your permissions.

talos init prepares a project for TALOS: it creates .talos-cli/ with commands/, extensions/ and an empty config.json. See Add MCP servers, hooks and commands.

pagine.descrizione: The interactive screen, one-shot and headless runs, the project folder it trusts, and what stays on your machine.

sezioni.testo:
The TALOS CLI is a coding agent in your terminal: it reads, edits and runs code in your project, on the model you choose. The npm package is talos-code; the command it installs is talos.

Three promises shape it: every tool asks before it acts unless you allowed it, every file it changes can be restored, and every session can be resumed.

You run | You get
talos | The interactive screen in the current folder; a prompt, if given, is the first message.
talos -p "…" | One task without the screen (headless): the answer is printed, and the run ends.
talos -p "…" --json | The same, with one JSON result at the end — or --output-format stream-json for one JSON event per line.

Everything else is a subcommand: talos <family> <operation>, from talos session list to talos doctor. Every family is in the CLI reference.

A headless run cannot ask you anything: an action that needs your approval is denied, and the run says so. It stops after 180 seconds unless --timeout says otherwise. See Run a task without the screen.

TALOS works in one project folder — the current one, or --project <path>. The first time, it asks whether you trust the folder: a project’s hooks, MCP servers, plugins and commands are code, and none of them loads in a folder you did not trust. talos project status says what is trusted and why. See Extensions.

There is no telemetry. Nothing is sent anywhere except:

- your prompts and the files TALOS reads, to the provider you chose;
- the public model catalog at models.dev, for context windows and prices, cached for 4 hours — turn it off with talos config set catalog.modelsDev false or TALOS_MODELS_DEV=off;
- the npm registry, only when you run talos update.

Configuration, sessions, checkpoints and logs stay on your machine:

| Windows | macOS / Linux
Configuration | %APPDATA%\TALOS-CLI | ~/.config/talos-cli
Sessions, checkpoints, logs | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI | ~/.local/state/talos-cli

Every folder and file is listed in Files.

- Permissions — what TALOS may do without asking.
- Sessions, context and undo — resuming, compaction, checkpoints.
- Models and providers — cloud and local models, and where keys are kept.
- Extensions — MCP servers, hooks, plugins and your own commands.

pagine.descrizione: The cloud providers and local engines the TALOS CLI works with, where keys are kept, and how a model is chosen.

sezioni.testo: TALOS ships no model: it works with the one you choose.

- Cloud: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Mistral, Groq, xAI, Kimi, Qwen, Z.AI, MiniMax, Cerebras, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Novita, Nebius, Hugging Face, Azure AI Foundry, Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI.
- Local, with no key: Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp.

TALOS never falls back from a local model to a cloud one on its own. Each provider, with its endpoint and the variable that can hold its key, is on Providers.

You type a key in hidden input, TALOS tests it with a one-token request, and keeps it in your operating system’s credential store — never in a file. A key already in your environment, such as OPENAI_API_KEY, is used only after you agree once. For OpenRouter you can sign in in the browser instead of pasting a key. Every operation is on talos provider.

/model (or Alt+P) picks the model in the interactive screen; talos model use <provider:model> sets it from the shell; --model overrides it for one run. talos model list shows each model’s context window, tool calling and reasoning, and where that data comes from — the public catalog at models.dev, cached for 4 hours, unless you turn it off. For models that support it, talos model effort sets the reasoning effort.

talos provider test <provider> checks that a provider answers, without generating tokens, and says what to do. talos doctor says what is ready and what is missing. See Check your setup and report a problem.

pagine.descrizione: How the TALOS CLI decides whether an action runs, asks you or is denied — modes, rules, protected folders and headless runs.

sezioni.testo: Every action TALOS takes goes through one decision: it runs, it asks you, or it is denied. Two things feed it — the mode of the session, and the rules you wrote — and a few limits that no mode lifts.

The mode is how actions with no rule of their own are approved. In the interactive screen Shift+Tab (or Alt+M) cycles Ask before edits, accept edits, plan and Full access, and /permissions shows the modes with what each one does; --permission-mode sets it for one run.

Mode | In short
default — Ask before edits | Reads freely; asks before changing files, running commands or any other action no rule allows. The default.
acceptEdits — Accept edits | Also allows file edits inside the project, and simple file commands, without asking.
plan — Plan | Reads and proposes; changes nothing: writing, editing, hooks, plugins and commands that change anything are denied.
auto — Auto | A classifier decides for actions no rule covers: allow, deny, or ask you.
dontAsk — Don’t ask | Never asks: what would need your approval is denied.
bypassPermissions — Full access | Allows what would otherwise ask. It asks Enable Full access? before it turns on. Use it only in a disposable environment you can restore.

Each mode in full is on Permissions.

A rule names a tool and a pattern — Bash(npm test), Edit(./src/**), Mcp(github:*) — and goes into permissions.allow, permissions.ask or permissions.deny of a settings file. Rules from every scope are merged: yours, the project’s, and yours for this project. A rule that cannot be read stops TALOS from starting, and says which one. The grammar of each tool’s pattern is on Rules.

When TALOS asks, your answer can become a rule: allow once, allow for this session, always allow (an allow rule is written), or deny. The full review (v) also offers always deny (a deny rule is written).

- Writing outside the project is denied.
- A deny rule denies, and an ask rule always asks — even in Full access.
- Protected folders — .git, .talos-cli, .github, .vscode, .idea, .husky — are never edited by accept edits or Auto.
- A command with &, |, ;, <, > or parentheses never matches a Bash rule, so it cannot slip through one.

The whole order of the decision, step by step, is on How a decision is made.

A run with -p has no one to ask: an action that would ask is denied, and the run says so. To let a script do more, write the rules it needs, or pick a mode for that run with --permission-mode. See Allow, ask or deny a tool.

pagine.descrizione: How the TALOS CLI keeps sessions you can resume and fork, compacts long conversations, and restores the files a turn changed.

sezioni.testo:
Every conversation is a session, kept on your machine. You can leave and come back to it: /resume and /fork open a picker in the interactive screen, and talos --resume last continues the most recent one from the shell. A fork starts a new session from a copy of an existing one, so you can try another way without losing the first.

Sessions can be named, tagged and pinned, searched, exported for your own records (JSON, JSON Lines or Markdown), and shared: talos session share writes a copy with the keys and secrets found in your environment removed. An imported session — from the CLI or from TALOS Desktop — is a read-only archive: it never runs anything by itself. Every operation is on talos session.

A model reads a limited window of text. With a model whose window is known and at least 64k tokens, a long conversation is compacted when it reaches half of the window, and the screen says when and how much. /context shows how full the window is; /compact compacts now; talos session context <id> says when a session will be compacted.

Before TALOS changes a file, it takes a checkpoint — kept outside your repository and outside Git, so your history is never touched. /undo restores the files a turn changed. From the shell, talos checkpoint list shows the checkpoints of the project, undo restores one, and redo applies again what an undo removed. See Undo what a turn changed.
What TALOS should remember from one session to the next is kept apart, in its memory: list, search, add, update and delete it with talos memory, or /memory in the interactive screen.

pagine.descrizione: One task per page — from the first setup to scheduling a task — each checked against the TALOS CLI version it names.

sezioni.testo:
Each guide does one thing, in the order you would do it. To understand how the parts fit together first, start with How the TALOS CLI works.

- Set up a provider and a model Run the guided setup, give TALOS a key or sign in, choose a model, and check that it answers.
- Run a task without the screen Give TALOS one task from the shell or a script, get text or JSON back, and know what it may do on its own.
- Allow, ask or deny a tool Write permission rules for the TALOS CLI, check what a rule would decide before you rely on it, and answer when TALOS asks.
- Undo what a turn changed Restore the files TALOS changed, from checkpoints kept outside your repository, and apply them again if you change your mind.
- Resume, fork and share a session Come back to a session, try another way from a copy, name and find sessions, and export or share one safely.
- Work in the interactive screen Write and send, answer approvals, queue or steer while TALOS works, watch sub-agents, and find your way with the keyboard.
- Adjust the display and notifications Set the width of answers, notifications, the mouse, the theme and what stays on screen when you leave.
- Add MCP servers, hooks and commands Prepare a project, trust it, add an MCP server, a hook, a plugin or a command of your own, and test each before it runs.
- Schedule a task Have TALOS carry out instructions by itself on a schedule, try them first, and keep them running in the background on Windows.
- Check your setup and report a problem Find what is missing with doctor, read the logs, make a redacted report for a bug, and check for a newer version.

pagine.descrizione: Have TALOS carry out instructions by itself on a schedule, try them first, and keep them running in the background on Windows.

sezioni.testo: An automation is a set of instructions, written like a prompt, that TALOS carries out in a folder on a schedule. Nobody is there to approve while it runs, so an action that would ask you is refused: choose its permission mode with that in mind.

```
talos automation add "Run the tests and summarize what fails" --when "weekdays 09:00"
```

--when is required: every 30m, every 2h, hourly, hourly :15, daily 09:00, weekdays 09:00, weekly mon 09:00, once 2026-10-20 09:00, cron '0 9 * * 1-5', or manual (only when you run it). An automation runs at most once every 5 minutes. TALOS says when it runs next.

Optional: --name, --folder (a trusted folder; the project by default), --model, --mode (plan, default, acceptEdits — the default for automations — or bypassPermissions), --repeat <runs> to stop after that many runs, --timezone for the times in --when, and --coordination to let it start agents by itself.

Automations made by an older TALOS, for a task of the board, cannot run or be edited: delete them and make them again with instructions.

```
talos automation list              # id, on or off, schedule, next run and name
talos automation show <id>         # schedule, folder, mode, model, runs left and the instructions
talos automation run <id>          # runs it now, waits for it to end and prints its report
talos automation history <id>      # its runs: when, the outcome and why, the first line of the report
```

talos automation edit <id> changes the instructions (--instructions), the schedule or any other part.

An automation runs while talos automation serve is running — it checks every 30 seconds until you press Ctrl+C, and --once runs what is due now, then exits — or, on Windows, through a task in Task Scheduler that starts serve when you sign in:

```
talos automation install-runner --yes
talos automation health             # whether the task is installed and is the one TALOS set up
```

enable, disable and delete manage an automation; uninstall-runner --yes removes the Windows task. Every option is on talos automation.

pagine.descrizione: Set the width of answers, notifications, the mouse, the theme and what stays on screen when you leave.

sezioni.testo:
/config opens the display settings. Up and Down choose a row; Enter, Left or Right change its value. Each change is saved at once, only for you in this project, outside the repository; Esc closes the panel. A change that cannot be saved leaves the previous value and says so.

Setting | Values | Applies
Response width — ui.maxProseWidth | Full width, 60, 80, 100 or 120 columns | At once, answers already on screen included
Notifications — ui.notifications | auto, bell, off | Next launch
Mouse-wheel scrolling — ui.mouse | On or off | Next launch
On exit — ui.exitOutput | The transcript, or the command to resume | Next launch

The width only limits paragraphs, headings, lists and quotes of answers: code, tables, your messages and the raw transcript keep the terminal’s width, and a narrow terminal wins over the setting. A custom width — any whole number of columns from 40 — can be set in your configuration. Wrapping never adds line breaks to the stored answer, to what you copy, or to an export.

With auto, TALOS tells you that a turn finished or failed, or that it is waiting for your approval — only after the terminal reports that it lost focus; a terminal that never reports focus stays silent. Windows Terminal on Windows shows a desktop notification; iTerm2, kitty and Ghostty use their own; other terminals, SSH and multiplexers ring the bell. bell always rings the bell; off stays silent. Notifications carry fixed messages: never your prompts, file names, commands or answers.

On terminals that support it, the tab or taskbar shows progress while a turn runs, even with notifications off.

- /theme picks the color theme; the arrows preview it.
- --no-color prints plain text.
- TALOS_REDUCED_MOTION=1 turns the animations off.

pagine.titolo: Add MCP servers, hooks and commands
pagine.descrizione: Prepare a project, trust it, add an MCP server, a hook, a plugin or a command of your own, and test each before it runs.

sezioni.titolo: Add MCP servers, hooks and commands
sezioni.testo: Why each extension waits for your trust is explained in Extensions.

```
talos init              # creates .talos-cli/ with commands/, extensions/ and an empty config.json
talos project status    # what is trusted, why, and the project files that can run code
talos project trust     # trusts the project and the current snapshot of its executable files
```

talos project revoke removes the trust: the project’s hooks, MCP servers, plugins and commands stop loading.

```
talos mcp list          # the servers, with their source, trust and state
talos mcp test <id>     # starts it and checks protocol, tools, trust, permissions and recent logs
talos mcp trust <id>
```

Its tools then go through your permissions like any other — as Mcp(server:operation).

```
talos hook list
talos hook dry-run <id> <event>   # runs it with a synthetic event, the way a real one would
talos hook trust <id>
talos hook history <id>           # its last runs
```

talos hook quarantine <id> denies a hook until you release it; releasing does not restore its trust.

```
talos plugin install <source>
talos plugin list
talos plugin trust <id>
```

Installing does not make a plugin run: the project’s trust must cover the new package first.

A custom command is a Markdown file, for example in .talos-cli/commands/ of the project; its text becomes the prompt, with {{arg1}}, {{arg2}}… for its arguments. In the interactive screen it is a slash command.

```
talos command list                 # commands, skills and workflows, with where they come from and whether they are valid
talos command run <name> <arg>     # prints the prompt it expands to
```

pagine.titolo: Run a task without the screen
pagine.descrizione: Give TALOS one task from the shell or a script, get text or JSON back, and know what it may do on its own.

sezioni.titolo: Run a task without the screen
sezioni.testo: For a single task, TALOS can run without the interactive screen: it works, prints the result, and ends.

```
talos -p "inspect this repository and explain the failing tests"
```

When the standard input is not a terminal and no prompt is given, TALOS runs without the screen and reads the prompt from the standard input:

```
cat task.md | talos --json
```

```
talos -p "summarize the changes" --json                          # one JSON result at the end
talos -p "summarize the changes" --output-format stream-json     # one JSON event per line, as they happen
```

--protocol v2 selects the newer format of events and results; it needs --json or stream-json. The exit code says how the run ended: see Exit codes.

```
talos --resume last -p "now fix the first one"
talos --fork <id> -p "try another way"
```

sezioni.titolo: What it may do on its own
sezioni.testo:
A headless run has no one to ask: an action that would ask is denied, and the run says so. To let it do more, write the rules it needs in a settings file, or choose a mode for the run with --permission-mode — see Allow, ask or deny a tool.

A run stops after 180 seconds unless --timeout <seconds> says otherwise. --model <provider:model> and --project <path> choose the model and the folder for this run only. Every option is on Global options.

pagine.titolo: Allow, ask or deny a tool
pagine.descrizione: Write permission rules for the TALOS CLI, check what a rule would decide before you rely on it, and answer when TALOS asks.

sezioni.titolo: Allow, ask or deny a tool
sezioni.testo: How modes and rules fit together is explained in Permissions. Here is how to write the rules.

Rules go in permissions.allow, permissions.ask or permissions.deny, one Tool(pattern) each:

```
talos config set permissions.allow '["Bash(npm test)", "Bash(npm run:*)", "Edit(./src/**)"]' --scope project
talos config set permissions.deny '["Bash(rm:*)"]' --scope project-user
```

- project — shared with whoever uses the project;
- project-user — yours, for this project, kept outside it;
- user — yours, for every project.

Rules from every scope are merged. The pattern of each tool — commands matched word by word, paths relative to the project — is on Rules.

sezioni.titolo: Check a rule before you rely on it
sezioni.testo:
```
talos config permissions dry-run --tool Bash --command "npm run build"
```

It says which rule would allow, ask or deny that action, without running it. talos config origins shows which file each value comes from.

pagine.descrizione: Write and send, answer approvals, queue or steer while TALOS works, watch sub-agents, and find your way with the keyboard.

sezioni.testo: talos opens the interactive screen in the current folder. The welcome screen names the project and the model, with a hint line: / for commands, @ to mention a file, Shift+Tab for the permission mode, ? for all keys. /help lists the commands. Every command is on Slash commands, every key on Key bindings.

- Enter sends. Shift+Enter adds a line where the terminal reports it; Ctrl+J always does.
- Tab completes a command, or a path after @.
- Up and Down walk your previous prompts; Ctrl+R searches them.
- Ctrl+C or Esc cancels the run, closes a dialog, or clears the draft — Up brings it back.

By default, Enter queues your next message until the turn ends. /busy changes what Enter does: queue, steer the running turn with your message, or interrupt it and send. Ctrl+Enter or Alt+S steers at the next safe point; /queue shows the queued messages.

When TALOS asks, a card shows what it wants to do (an edit comes with its diff) and asks a question: Make this edit?, Run this command? Press a number: 1 allow once, 2 for this session, 3 always, 4 deny and go on; v opens the full review, where 5 always denies. Esc denies and stops the turn. See Allow, ask or deny a tool.

- Ctrl+O opens the transcript, the whole conversation with search; Alt+T searches it, PageUp and PageDown scroll it.
- Ctrl+T shows or hides all reasoning; the choice is remembered.
- Alt+A shows the sub-agents while they work; Enter opens one agent’s conversation, live and read-only.
- Ctrl+L, or /redraw, repaints the screen.

The line under the composer shows the permission mode. Shift+Tab (or Alt+M) cycles it: default (Ask before edits), accept edits, plan mode, and Full access, which asks Enable Full access? the first time. /permissions shows the modes with what each one does. Alt+P, or /model, picks the model. See Permissions.
Press Ctrl+D, or Ctrl+C twice, on an empty composer — or type /exit.

pagine.titolo: Resume, fork and share a session
pagine.descrizione: Come back to a session, try another way from a copy, name and find sessions, and export or share one safely.

sezioni.testo:
- In the interactive screen: /resume opens a picker.
- From the shell: talos --resume last, or talos --resume <id>; add -p "…" to continue without the screen.
- When you leave the screen, it prints the transcript — or, with ui.exitOutput set to resume, the command that brings you back.

A fork starts a new session from a copy of an existing one: the original stays as it was.

- In the interactive screen: /fork.
- From the shell: talos --fork <id>, or talos session fork <id>, which prints the new id.

```
talos session list                      # name, project, model, tags and pin
talos session search <text>             # by id, name, project or tag
talos session rename <id> "release notes"
talos session tag <id> docs
talos session pin <id>
```

/rename names the open conversation from inside the screen.

```
talos session export <id> --out notes.md --format md     # for your own records: json, jsonl or md
talos session share <id> --out shared.json                # a redacted copy, safe to share
talos session import shared.json                         # a read-only archive: it never runs anything by itself
```

share removes the keys and secrets found in your environment. /export saves the open conversation, in Markdown by default. import also reads sessions exported by TALOS Desktop.

pagine.titolo: Set up a provider and a model
pagine.descrizione: Run the guided setup, give TALOS a key or sign in, choose a model, and check that it answers.

sezioni.titolo: Set up a provider and a model
sezioni.testo: Install the CLI first: Install the CLI.

```
talos provider set-key openai          # asks for the key without echoing it, tests it, saves it
talos provider login openrouter        # or sign in to OpenRouter in the browser
talos model use openai:gpt-5-mini      # choose the model (and so its provider)
talos provider test openai             # check that it answers, without generating tokens
```

A local engine — Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp — needs no key. To point TALOS at one that is not on its default address, use talos provider configure <provider> --endpoint <url>.

- /provider sets up a provider.
- /model, or Alt+P, picks the model; with no provider chosen yet, the list of providers comes first.
- /effort sets the reasoning effort, for models that support it.
talos provider test <provider> prints its state, latency and what to do; talos doctor says what is ready and what is missing. See Check your setup and report a problem.

pagine.titolo: Check your setup and report a problem
pagine.descrizione: Find what is missing with doctor, read the logs, make a redacted report for a bug, and check for a newer version.

sezioni.titolo: What is ready, what is missing
sezioni.testo:
```
talos doctor            # one line per check: runtime, folders, providers, credentials, catalog
talos doctor --json     # the same, for a script
```

/doctor runs the same checks from the interactive screen. For one provider, talos provider test <provider> says whether it answers, its latency and what to do.

- --verbose shows more detail, with the trace id.
- talos logs --tail 100 prints the last lines of each log file.
- The exit code says how a run ended: see Exit codes.

```
talos diagnostic bundle --out talos-diagnostic.zip
```

It writes a ZIP with the doctor report, the effective configuration and the last 200 log lines — secrets removed and paths replaced, and no prompt or file content. Attach it to your report.

--session <id|last> adds that one conversation. Keys, tokens and the paths of your home folder and of the project are masked, but other paths, names, code, file contents and anything you typed are not: read it before you share it.

```
talos update --check
```

With an npm install, talos update says whether a newer version exists and prints the command to run (npm i -g talos-code@latest); it changes nothing by itself.

- Only Windows 11 x64 is tested; macOS and Linux are not yet.
- Context compaction with a local Ollama model is not yet verified end to end.
- A local provider that answers 401 or 403 without needing a key can be set aside as if its key were wrong.

pagine.descrizione: Restore the files TALOS changed, from checkpoints kept outside your repository, and apply them again if you change your mind.

sezioni.testo: Before TALOS changes a file, it takes a checkpoint. Checkpoints are kept outside your repository and outside Git: your history is never touched.

```
talos checkpoint list            # the checkpoints of the project, newest first
talos checkpoint show <id>       # what it covers: operation, state, files covered and files excluded
talos checkpoint undo            # restore the files as they were before the latest checkpoint
talos checkpoint redo            # apply again what the latest undo removed
```

undo and redo take a checkpoint id to act on an older one.

A checkpoint records the operation it was taken for — an edit, a shell command — and lists the files it covers and those it excluded. Read them with talos checkpoint show before you restore; /diff shows the current Git diff of the project.

pagine.descrizione: Install talos-code from npm, run it in a project, and know where it keeps your data.

sezioni.testo:
- Node.js 24, version 24.18 or later in the 24 line.
- Tested on Windows 11 x64. macOS and Linux are not tested yet.

The npm package is talos-code; the command it installs is talos.

```
npm i -g talos-code
talos --version
```

Open a terminal in a project and run:

```
talos
```

The first time, a short guided setup asks only what is missing: whether to trust the folder, then a provider (a local engine that is running comes first), its key, and a model, one step at a time; Esc skips a step. /setup or talos setup runs it again. A key already in your environment (for example OPENAI_API_KEY) is used only after you agree once; otherwise you type it in hidden input and it is kept in the operating system’s credential store, never in a file. For OpenRouter you can also sign in in the browser instead of pasting a key (talos provider login openrouter).

Then the welcome screen opens on your project, with the model and a hint line for the first keys.

TALOS ~/projects/relay-queue · main Welcome to TALOS C:\demo\projects\relay-queue model lmstudio:openai/gpt-oss-20b Ask anything, for example: "Explain how this project is built" / commands · @ mention a file · Shift+Tab permission mode · ? all keys╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮│ › Ask TALOS, / for commands, @ for files │╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ default · shift+tab · ? keys openai/gpt-oss-20b · lmstudio: verified · ctx ? · ~/projects/relay-queue · main

For a single task, without the interactive screen:

```
talos -p "inspect this repository and explain the failing tests"
```

For machine-readable output, add --json (or --output-format stream-json):

```
talos -p "summarize the changes" --json
```

```
talos update --check
```

With an npm install, talos update tells you when a newer version exists and prints the command to run (npm i -g talos-code@latest). It changes nothing by itself.

Nothing is sent anywhere except your prompts and the files TALOS reads, to the provider you chose; the public model catalog at models.dev, for context windows and prices, cached for 4 hours; and the npm registry, only when you run talos update. There is no telemetry.

- Configuration: %APPDATA%\TALOS-CLI on Windows, ~/.config/talos-cli on macOS and Linux.
- Sessions, checkpoints and logs: %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI on Windows, ~/.local/state/talos-cli on macOS and Linux.

To turn off the models.dev catalog: talos config set catalog.modelsDev false, or TALOS_MODELS_DEV=off.

- Only Windows 11 x64 is tested.
- Context compaction with a local Ollama model is not yet verified end to end.
- A local provider that answers 401 or 403 without needing a key can be set aside as if its key were wrong.

pagine.descrizione: Instructions TALOS carries out by itself on a schedule: add, edit, show, run now, history, and the Windows runner.

sezioni.testo:
An automation is a set of instructions, written like a prompt, that TALOS carries out in a folder on a schedule. It runs while talos automation serve is running; on Windows, talos automation install-runner --yes starts that at sign-in. Nobody is there to approve, so an action that would ask you is refused. <id> is the automation id talos automation list shows. Automations made by an older TALOS (for a task of the board) cannot run or be edited: delete them and make them again with instructions.

Operation | What it does
listdefault | Lists the automations: id, on or off, schedule, next run and name.
add | Makes an automation from instructions and a schedule, and says when it runs next.
edit | Changes the instructions, the schedule or any other part of an automation.
show | Prints an automation: its schedule and time zone, on or off, next run, folder, mode, model, runs left, and its instructions.
history | Prints the runs of an automation: when, the outcome and why, and the first line of its report.
run | Runs the automation now, waits for it to end and prints its report; Ctrl+C stops it.
enable | Turns an automation on.
disable | Turns an automation off: it does not run until you turn it on again.
delete | Deletes an automation with its history.
serve | Runs the automations when they are due, checking every 30 seconds, until you press Ctrl+C.
install-runner | Adds a task to Windows Task Scheduler that starts talos automation serve when you sign in to Windows.
uninstall-runner | Removes the TALOS task from Windows Task Scheduler.
health | Says whether the TALOS task in Windows Task Scheduler is installed and is the one TALOS set up.

Without an operation, talos automation runs list.

Lists the automations: id, on or off, schedule, next run and name.

```
talos automation list
```

Makes an automation from instructions and a schedule, and says when it runs next.

```
talos automation add <instructions> --when <when> [--name <name>] [--folder <path>] [--model <provider:model>] [--mode <mode>] [--repeat <runs>] [--timezone <zone>] [--coordination]
```

Arguments

instructions
What TALOS should do each time, in quotes.

Options

--when <value>
When it runs (required): every 30m, every 2h, hourly, hourly :15, daily 09:00, weekdays 09:00, weekly mon 09:00, once 2026-10-20 09:00, cron '0 9 * * 1-5' or manual (only when you run it). At most once every 5 minutes.
--name <value>
Its name. Default: the first words of the instructions.
--folder <value>
The folder it works in, which must be trusted. Default: the project.
--model <value>
The model it uses. Default: the model in use when it runs.
--mode <value>
The permission mode of its runs: plan, default, acceptEdits (default) or bypassPermissions.
--repeat <value>
Stop after this many runs (a whole number, at least 1). Default: no end.
--timezone <value>
The time zone of the times in --when. Default: the computer's.
--coordination
It may start agents by itself.

Examples

```
talos automation add "Run the tests and summarize what fails" --when "weekdays 09:00"
```

Changes the instructions, the schedule or any other part of an automation.

```
talos automation edit <id> [--instructions <text>] [--when <when>] [--name <name>] [--folder <path>] [--model <provider:model> | --default-model] [--mode <mode>] [--repeat <runs> | --forever] [--timezone <zone>] [--coordination | --no-coordination]
```

Arguments

id
The id talos automation list shows.

Options

--when <value>
A new schedule, written as for add.
--name <value>
A new name.
--folder <value>
A new folder, which must be trusted.
--model <value>
A model of its own.
--mode <value>
A new permission mode: plan, default, acceptEdits or bypassPermissions.
--repeat <value>
Stop after this many runs in all (the runs already made count).
--timezone <value>
A new time zone.
--instructions <value>
New instructions.
--default-model
Use the model in use when it runs.
--forever
No end to its runs.
--coordination
It may start agents by itself.
--no-coordination
It may not start agents by itself.

- At least one change is required.

Prints an automation: its schedule and time zone, on or off, next run, folder, mode, model, runs left, and its instructions.

```
talos automation show <id>
```

Arguments

id
The id talos automation list shows.

Prints the runs of an automation: when, the outcome and why, and the first line of its report.

```
talos automation history <id>
```

Arguments

id
The id talos automation list shows.

Runs the automation now, waits for it to end and prints its report; Ctrl+C stops it.

```
talos automation run <id>
```

Arguments

id
The id talos automation list shows.

- If another TALOS process is running the automations (talos automation serve), the run is handed to it and followed from here.
- An automation without a model of its own uses the global --model option, otherwise the configured model.

Exit codes and errors1
Code | Exit | Meaning
exit | 1 | The run did not start, was stopped, or failed.

Turns an automation on.

```
talos automation enable <id>
```

Arguments

id
The id talos automation list shows.

Turns an automation off: it does not run until you turn it on again.

```
talos automation disable <id>
```

Arguments

id
The id talos automation list shows.

Deletes an automation with its history.

```
talos automation delete <id>
```

Arguments

id
The id talos automation list shows.

Runs the automations when they are due, checking every 30 seconds, until you press Ctrl+C.

```
talos automation serve [--once]
```

Options

--once
Run what is due now, wait for those runs to end (at most 30 minutes), then exit.

- One process runs the automations at a time: a second serve waits and takes over when the first one stops (with --once it exits instead).

Adds a task to Windows Task Scheduler that starts talos automation serve when you sign in to Windows.

```
talos automation install-runner --yes
```

Options

--yes
Confirms the change to Task Scheduler (required).

- Windows only. The task is called “TALOS CLI Automation Runner” and runs under your account.

Exit codes and errors2
Code | Exit | Meaning
AUTOMATION_CONFIRM_REQUIRED | 2 | This changes a task in Windows Task Scheduler, so TALOS waits for your confirmation. Run the same command again with --yes.
WINDOWS_REQUIRED | 2 | The command or the configuration is not valid. Check the command, its options and the configuration.

Removes the TALOS task from Windows Task Scheduler.

```
talos automation uninstall-runner --yes
```

Options

--yes
Confirms the change to Task Scheduler (required).

- Windows only.

Exit codes and errors2
Code | Exit | Meaning
AUTOMATION_CONFIRM_REQUIRED | 2 | This changes a task in Windows Task Scheduler, so TALOS waits for your confirmation. Run the same command again with --yes.
WINDOWS_REQUIRED | 2 | The command or the configuration is not valid. Check the command, its options and the configuration.

Says whether the TALOS task in Windows Task Scheduler is installed and is the one TALOS set up.

```
talos automation health
```

pagine.descrizione: The file checkpoints TALOS takes before it changes files: list, show, undo, redo.

sezioni.testo:
Before a turn changes files, TALOS saves what it will touch, outside your repository and outside Git. /undo in the interactive screen uses the same checkpoints.

Operation | What it does
list | Lists the checkpoints of the project, newest first.
show | Shows a checkpoint: operation, state, files covered and files excluded.
undo | Restores the files as they were before a checkpoint; without an id, the latest.
redo | Applies again the changes an undo removed; without an id, the latest.
prune | Deletes old checkpoints, keeping the newest ones of each project, and the saved file contents no checkpoint uses any more; says what was kept and how much space was freed.

Lists the checkpoints of the project, newest first.

```
talos checkpoint list
```

Shows a checkpoint: operation, state, files covered and files excluded.

```
talos checkpoint show <id>
```

Arguments

id
The id talos checkpoint list shows.

Restores the files as they were before a checkpoint; without an id, the latest.

```
talos checkpoint undo [id]
```

Arguments

idoptional
Checkpoint id.

- Refused while a session is running.

Exit codes and errors1
Code | Exit | Meaning
CHECKPOINT_ACTIVE_RUN_CONFLICT | 70 | TALOS could not finish this action. Try again; if it happens again, keep the log for a report.

Applies again the changes an undo removed; without an id, the latest.

```
talos checkpoint redo [id]
```

Arguments

idoptional
Checkpoint id.

- Refused while a session is running.

Exit codes and errors1
Code | Exit | Meaning
CHECKPOINT_ACTIVE_RUN_CONFLICT | 70 | TALOS could not finish this action. Try again; if it happens again, keep the log for a report.

Deletes old checkpoints, keeping the newest ones of each project, and the saved file contents no checkpoint uses any more; says what was kept and how much space was freed.

```
talos checkpoint prune [--keep <count>] [--days <days>] [--dry-run]
```

Options

--keep <value>
How many checkpoints to keep for each project, at least 1. Default 20.
--days <value>
Also delete the kept ones older than this many days.
--dry-run
Say what would be deleted, and delete nothing.

- It covers the checkpoints of every project, not only the current one. A checkpoint still open, or one being restored, is always kept.

pagine.descrizione: The model providers: keys, sign-in, endpoints and health.

sezioni.testo:
Keys are stored in the system credential store (or in memory for the session, if you choose so). A key is never printed. Choosing a model chooses its provider: see `talos model`. Every provider is in Providers.

Operation | What it does
listdefault | Lists the providers with the state of their key and the environment variable that can supply one.
login | Signs in in the browser: to OpenRouter, saving the key it returns after testing it, or to ChatGPT, so that its models are paid by your plan.
logout | Signs out of ChatGPT: requests stop using your plan, and TALOS asks OpenAI to revoke its access.
status | Says whether a ChatGPT account is connected and its plan allowed, what this TALOS sent with it in the last 5 hours and 7 days (requests and tokens), and where to see your account's usage and limits.
set-key | Asks for a key without echoing it, tests it with a one-token request and saves it if it works.
env-key | Says whether a key for the provider was found in the environment, and whether TALOS uses it.
remove-key | Deletes the saved key of a provider.
configure | Sets the endpoint and/or the request timeout of a provider.
test | Checks that the provider answers, without generating tokens; prints its state, latency and what to do.
exclusions | Lists the providers OpenRouter must not use, for every model or for one.
exclude | Tells OpenRouter not to route your requests to a provider, for every model or for one model only.
allow | Lets OpenRouter use an excluded provider again, for every model or for one.

Without an operation, talos provider runs list.

Lists the providers with the state of their key and the environment variable that can supply one.

```
talos provider list
```

Signs in in the browser: to OpenRouter, saving the key it returns after testing it, or to ChatGPT, so that its models are paid by your plan.

```
talos provider login <provider> [--paste]
```

Arguments

provider
openrouter or chatgpt; no other provider supports sign-in.

Options

--paste
OpenRouter only: paste the code OpenRouter shows instead of waiting for the browser (for remote sessions).

- Needs an interactive terminal.
- ChatGPT: needs a ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan. With keys kept in memory (credentials.store set to memory) the command refuses, since the sign-in would be lost when it ends; sign in from /provider in the interactive screen instead (it lasts until TALOS closes). The browser must run on the computer where TALOS runs: in a remote session TALOS says so and prints the address to open there. If you sign in without allowing TALOS to use the plan, nothing can be sent with it until you sign in again and allow it.

Exit codes and errors6
Code | Exit | Meaning
exit | 11 | Sign-in failed or was not completed, the OpenRouter key did not pass the test and was not saved, or the ChatGPT plan was not allowed.
PROVIDER_REQUIRED | 12 | This command needs the id of a provider. Name it after the operation, for example talos provider login openai; the ids are in talos provider list.
PROVIDER_LOGIN_UNSUPPORTED | 12 | Only OpenRouter and the ChatGPT plan offer a sign-in; other providers use a key. Save a key with talos provider set-key <provider>.
PROVIDER_LOGIN_UNAVAILABLE | 12 | This sign-in is not available in this installation. Use a provider with a key: talos provider set-key <provider>.
LOGIN_REQUIRES_TTY | 70 | Signing in needs an interactive terminal. Run talos provider login <provider> in a terminal; a provider with a key can take one with talos provider set-key <provider>.
SECRET_INPUT_REQUIRES_TTY | 70 | TALOS could not finish this action. Try again; if it happens again, keep the log for a report.

```

pagine.descrizione: The environment variables TALOS CLI reads, and what each one changes.

sezioni.testo:
TALOS_CREDENTIAL_STORE
Where keys are kept for this process: system or memory. Overrides credentials.store.Valuessystemmemory
TALOS_MODELS_DEV
Set to off to turn off the models.dev catalog: nothing is sent.Valuesoff
TALOS_REDUCED_MOTION
Set to 1 or true to reduce animation in the interactive screen.Values1true
TALOS_RG_PATH
Path of the ripgrep binary to use for search, instead of the one shipped with the package.
TALOS_TRACE_ID
A trace id to reuse in failure reports (1 to 128 printable characters), e.g. from a parent process.
TALOS_CLI_UPDATE_CHANNEL
The default channel of talos update.Valuesstablepreview
TALOS_CHECKPOINT_AUTO_PRUNE
Set to 0 to turn off the background prune that brings a workspace past 100 checkpoints back to 50.Values0
TALOS_ACTIVE_RUN_RECONCILE
Set to 0 to keep the markers of runs that ended without cleaning up (by default they are removed at startup).Values0
TALOS_MAX_RETRIES
How many times a request is retried when the provider answers "too many requests" (HTTP 429), a timeout (408) or a server error (5xx): a whole number up to 15, default 10. The wait doubles from 0.5 s up to 32 s between tries, unless the provider says how long to wait. 0 turns retries off.
TALOS_TUI_TERMINAL_BACKGROUND
While the interactive screen is up, TALOS sets the terminal's background to the theme's color and gives it back when it leaves (never with the mono theme, inside tmux or GNU screen). On Windows and inside WSL it does so only in Windows Terminal. 0 turns it off everywhere; 1 turns it on in the other Windows consoles too (VS Code's terminal, for example).Values01
TALOS_ATTREZZI_DIFFERITI
Set to 0 to send the model the full list of tools with every request. By default the tools used only on request (notes, tasks, library, research, automations and the like) are left out of the first list and the model loads them when it needs them; connected directly, Gemini always gets the full list.Values0
NO_COLOR
Any value turns colors off, as --no-color does.
VISUAL
The editor used to compose a long prompt (checked before EDITOR).
EDITOR
The editor used to compose a long prompt, when VISUAL is not set.
APPDATA
Windows: the settings folder is %APPDATA%\TALOS-CLI.
LOCALAPPDATA
Windows: data, sessions and logs are under %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI.
XDG_CONFIG_HOME
macOS and Linux: if set, the settings folder; otherwise ~/.config/talos-cli.
XDG_STATE_HOME
macOS and Linux: if set, the data folder; otherwise ~/.local/state/talos-cli.
XDG_CACHE_HOME
macOS and Linux: if set, the cache folder; otherwise ~/.cache/talos-cli.

Each provider can take its key from the variables listed on Providers. A key found in the environment is not used until you approve it — talos provider env-key <provider> --use, or when the interactive screen asks. One-shot commands that run a model (talos research start, talos automation run) use it and say where the key came from.
