15 | A session, research or automation could not be found or used (also: an MCP server that is not healthy). | 28
16 | The update could not be completed. | —
70 | An internal error. | 165
130 | Interrupted (Ctrl+C) or cancelled. | 2
With --json, a failure is a JSON object with its code; in text it is the sentence below, and --verbose adds the trace id. A code without its own sentence uses the one of its exit code.

ARTIFACT_RESULT_INVALID
The artifact was not confirmed as saved. Check whether it exists before creating it again; TALOS does not retry this on its own.
AUTOMATION_CONFIRM_REQUIRED
This changes a task in Windows Task Scheduler, so TALOS waits for your confirmation. Run the same command again with --yes.
AUTOMATION_INSTRUCTIONS_REQUIRED
An automation needs its instructions. Write them in quotes: talos automation add "<instructions>" --when "<when>".
AUTOMATION_INVALID
That automation is not valid. Check its name, its schedule and its model, then try again.
AUTOMATION_MODE_INVALID
That is not a mode for an automation. Use plan, default, acceptEdits or bypassPermissions.
AUTOMATION_SCHEDULE_INVALID
That schedule is not valid. Give a local time as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, an interval in minutes, or a cron schedule.
AUTOMATION_STORE_INVALID
TALOS could not read the list of automations. Try again in a moment; if it keeps failing, keep talos logs for a report.
AUTOMATION_TASK_QUERY_FAILED
TALOS could not read its task in Windows Task Scheduler. Set it up again with talos automation install-runner --yes.
AUTOMATION_USERNAME_REQUIRED
TALOS could not tell which Windows account should run its task. Run the command from your own Windows account, in a normal terminal.
AUTOMATION_WHEN_INVALID
TALOS does not read that schedule. Use one of: "every 30m", "every 2h", "hourly", "hourly :15", "daily 09:00", "weekdays 09:00", "weekly mon 09:00", "once 2026-10-20 09:00", cron "0 9 * * 1-5" or "manual".
AUTOMATION_WHEN_REQUIRED
An automation needs to know when it runs. Add --when, for example --when "every 30m", "daily 09:00", "weekdays 09:00", "weekly mon 09:00", "once 2026-10-20 09:00" or "manual".

OpenAI did not recognise this TALOS installation. Sign out with talos provider logout chatgpt, then sign in again.
CHATGPT_IDENTITY_INVALID
The identity OpenAI sent could not be verified. Run talos provider login chatgpt again.
CHATGPT_PORT_INVALID
The local address for the sign-in could not be opened. Run talos provider login chatgpt again.
CHATGPT_REQUEST_INVALID

CHATGPT_RETURN_UNKNOWN
The browser came back to an address TALOS was not waiting on. Run talos provider login chatgpt again and use the address it prints.
CHATGPT_ROUTE_UNKNOWN
That operation on the ChatGPT account does not exist. Try again.
CHATGPT_SIGN_IN_INVALID
The ChatGPT connection was not accepted. Sign in again with talos provider login chatgpt.
CHATGPT_STORE_ENTRY_INVALID
The stored ChatGPT sign-in could not be read. Sign in again with talos provider login chatgpt.
CLI_USAGE_ERROR
The command line is not valid.
COMMAND_ENVIRONMENT_CONTRACT_REQUIRED
The engine in this installation cannot apply the shell choice yet. Reinstall TALOS with npm install -g talos-code, then try again.
COMMAND_ENVIRONMENT_INVALID

COMMAND_EXECUTOR_CON

TRACT_REQUIRED

CONFIG_INVALID_AGENTS
The "agents" section of the configuration is not valid. Use only maxConcurrent, maxDepth, model and reasoningEffort, for example "agents": {"maxConcurrent": 10}.
CONFIG_INVALID_AGENTS_MAX_CONCURRENT
agents.maxConcurrent in the configuration is not a number of agents TALOS can run at once. Use a whole number from 1 to 32 (TALOS uses 10 when it is not set).
CONFIG_INVALID_AGENTS_MAX_DEPTH
agents.maxDepth in the configuration is not a delegation depth TALOS allows. Use a whole number from 1 to 4 (TALOS uses 2 when it is not set).
CONFIG_INVALID_AGENTS_MODEL
agents.model in the configuration does not name a provider and a model. Write it as "provider:model", for example "openrouter:qwen/qwen3-coder".
CONFIG_INVALID_AGENTS_REASONING_EFFORT
agents.reasoningEffort in the configuration is not a reasoning effort. Use low, medium, high, xhigh or max.
CONFIG_INVALID_BUSY_INPUT
The busy-input mode in the configuration is not one TALOS knows. Use queue, steer or interrupt.
CONFIG_INVALID_CATALOG
The configuration’s catalog section is not valid: it accepts only modelsDev, true or false. Run talos config set catalog.modelsDev false (or true), or remove the catalog section.
CONFIG_INVALID_CONTEXT
The configuration’s context section is not valid: it accepts only compactAtTokens, a whole number of tokens from 8000 to 10000000, or null for no cap. Run talos config set context.compactAtTokens 200000 (or null), or remove the context section.
CONFIG_INVALID_MODELS
A model override in the configuration is not valid. Write it as "models": {"provider:model": {"contextWindow": 131072}}.
CONFIG_INVALID_MODEL_ROUTING
The OpenRouter routing of a model (providerRouting) in the configuration is not one OpenRouter accepts. Use only, ignore and order as lists of provider slugs (such as deepinfra or z-ai), quantizations from the list OpenRouter publishes (fp8, bf16, fp4…), requireParameters and allowFallbacks as true or false, sort as price, throughput or latency.
CONFIG_INVALID_MODEL_WINDOW
A model's context window or output limit in the configuration is not a number of tokens TALOS can use. Use a whole number between 1024 and 10000000, with the output limit below the window.
CONFIG_INVALID_REASONING_DISPLAY
The reasoning display setting in the configuration is not one TALOS knows. Use collapsed or visible.
CTX_INVALID_SUMMARY
The summary the model wrote to compact this conversation was not in the form TALOS asked for, so it was not used. Automatic compaction waits a while before trying again; /compact tries now. If it keeps happening, choose another model for this conversation.
CTX_SUMMARY_RESPONSE_INVALID
The summary the model sent back to compact this conversation could not be read. Try again; if it keeps happening, choose another model for this conversation.
CTX_TOKEN_MODEL_INVALID
The model’s

window settings are not valid for counting tokens. Check the context window set for this model with talos config list.
CTX_TOKEN_PORT_INVALID
The token counter is not set up correctly. Keep talos logs for a report.
CTX_TOKEN_PROFILE_INVALID
The provider address used for counting tokens is not valid. Fix the provider address, then test it.
CTX_TOKEN_REQUEST_INVALID
The request to count tokens could not be built. Keep talos logs for a report.
CTX_TOKEN_RESPONSE_INVALID
The token counter answered with data TALOS cannot read. Try again; if it keeps happening, keep talos logs for a report.
DECISION_LOG_INVALID
The list of recent decisions could not be read. It starts again with the next decision; keep the log for a report if it happens again.
ELICITATION_ANSWER_INVALID
The MCP server cannot accept these values: one is missing or not of the kind it asked for. Check the fields and send again.
EXPORT_USAGE
That is not a format TALOS can export to. Use /export md, /export json or /export jsonl, optionally with a file name.
FOLDER_INVALID
The destination folder is not valid. Choose a folder inside the project.
FORGE_PACKAGE_SCHEMA_INVALID
The forged tool package is not valid. Check the package against the forge schema, then try again.
LIBRARY_STORE_INVALID
The library could not be read. Run talos doctor, or keep the log for a report.
LIBRARY_VERSION_INVALID
The version is not a number of this entry. See the numbers with talos library versions <id>, then restore one of them.
MEMORY_STORE_INVALID
The memories could not be read. Run talos doctor, or keep the log for a report.
MODEL_INVALID
The model id given to /model or --model is not a usable model id (it contains spaces or control characters). Give a model id like provider:model (for example openai:gpt-5-mini) with no spaces.
MODEL_STORE_MISCONFIGURED
The local model folder is not set up correctly. Keep talos logs for a report.
NOTES_STORE_INVALID
The notes could not be read. Run talos doctor, or keep the log for a report.
OUTPUT_INVALID_INPUT
The request to read a saved output is not valid. Check the offset and limit, then try again.
PLAN_DECISION_INVALID
TALOS does not know this choice on the plan. Choose again on the plan card; if it keeps happening, keep the log for a report.
PRE_MUTATION_CONTRACT_REQUIRED
The engine in this installation cannot take a checkpoint before changes yet. Reinstall TALOS with npm install -g talos-code, then try again.
PROCESS_OUTPUT_CONTRACT_REQUIRED
The engine in this installation cannot keep command outputs yet. Reinstall TALOS with npm install -g talos-code, then try again.
PROCESS_OUTPUT_READ_CONTRACT_REQUIRED
The engine in this installation cannot read kept command outputs yet. Reinstall TALOS with npm install -g talos-code, then try again.
PROJECT_TRUST_INVALIDATED
This folder no longer matches what you trusted, so TALOS did not load it. Review it with talos project status, then trust it again with talos project trust.
PROJECT_TRUST_REQUIRED
This folder is not trusted,

so TALOS did not load its instructions or tools. Review it with talos project status, then trust it with talos project trust.
READ_INVALID_UTF8
The file’s bytes at that position are not valid UTF-8 text. Read from an offset a previous read returned, or read the bytes as hex.
REQUIRED
The command is missing its {name}. Add it to the command; the command's --help shows how it is written.
RETRY_CAP_INVALID
The limit on the wait between retries is not a valid number. Keep talos logs for a report.
RULE_STORE_INVALID
The project permission settings are not a valid list. Fix the "permissions" entry of the project configuration.
TALOS_RUNTIME_NOT_FOUND
TALOS could not find its runtime files. Reinstall TALOS, or run it from its install folder.
TASK_BOARD_INVALID
The task board could not be read. Run talos doctor, or keep the log for a report.

CHATGPT_SIGN_IN_DENIED
The sign-in was refused in the browser. Run talos provider login chatgpt again and allow it.
OAUTH_DENIED
The sign-in was cancelled in the browser. Start it again and allow access on the OpenRouter page.
PATH_NOT_ALLOWED
This path is outside the folders TALOS may use. Use a path inside the project folder.
PERMISSION_RULE_EMPTY
The rule is empty, so nothing was saved. Write it as Tool(pattern), for example Bash(npm test:*) or Read(src/**).
PERMISSION_RULE_INVALID
A permission rule in the configuration is not valid, so TALOS did not start. Fix or remove the rule in the file named below.
PERMISSION_RULE_READ_ONLY

PERMISSION_RULE_UNREADABLE
TALOS cannot read that rule, so nothing was saved. Write it as Tool(pattern), for example Bash(npm test:*) or Read(src/**).
PLAN_MODE_READ_ONLY

SANDBOX_REQUIRED_UNAVAILABLE

CHATGPT_AUTHORIZATION_REFUSED
OpenAI refused the authorization. Run talos provider login chatgpt again.
CONFIG_INVALID_CREDENTIALS
The credentials section of the configuration is not valid. Make credentials an object with a store of system or memory, or remove it.
CONFIG_INVALID_CREDENTIAL_STORE
The credentials.store setting in the configuration is not valid. Set credentials.store to system or memory, or remove it.
CREDENTIAL_STORE_INVALID
The credential store TALOS was asked to use is not one it knows. Set TALOS_CREDENTIAL_STORE (or credentials.store in the configuration) to system or memory.

KEYMAP_INVALID
The key map in the configuration is not valid. Fix the keymap entry of the configuration.
OAUTH_CALLBACK_UNAVAILABLE

OAUTH_CANCELLED

OAUTH_CODE_MISSING
That is not a code from OpenRouter. Paste the code OpenRouter shows, or the whole address the browser landed on.
OAUTH_TIMEOUT
The sign-in took longer than 10 minutes. Start it again; the code OpenRouter gives lasts 10 minutes.
PROJECT_CREDENTIAL_STORE_IGNORED
The project configuration tried to choose where TALOS keeps your keys, so that setting was ignored. Set credentials.store in your user or project-user configuration, or use TALOS_CREDENTIAL_STORE.
PROVIDER_KEY_INVALID
The key is not valid (empty, too long, or with line breaks). Paste the key again, on one line.
PROVIDER_KEY_MISSING
No API key is available for this provider. Add one with talos provider set-key <id>.
PROVIDER_KEY_NOT_FOUND

PROVIDER_KEY_REQUIRED
No key was entered. Enter a key before saving it.
PROVIDER_KEY_SPEND_LIMIT

RUNTIME_OPERATION_KEY_REUSED

MODEL_PROVIDER_INVALID

OPENROUTER_ALL_PROVIDERS_EXCLUDED

OPENROUTER_ENDPOINTS_UNAVAILABLE

OPENROUTER_LOGIN_UNAVAILABLE

PROVIDER_ADDRESS_INVALID

PROVIDER_BUDGET_OCCUPIED
Other requests are using this OpenRouter key’s in-flight budget. Wait for them to finish, then try again.
PROVIDER_CREDIT_LIMIT

PROVIDER_EMPTY_RESPONSE
The model answered with neither text nor a tool call. Try again, or choose another model.
PROVIDER_ENDPOINT_NOT_CHOSEN
No address is chosen yet for this provider's key, so your key was not sent anywhere. Choose one in /provider, or for Z.AI: talos provider configure zai --address plan (or balance, plan-china, balance-china).
PROVIDER_EXCLUSIONS_UNAVAILABLE

PROVIDER_EXCLUSION_REFUSED

PROVIDER_EXCLUSION_REQUIRES_PROVIDER

PROVIDER_FALLBACK_BUSY

PROVIDER_LOGIN_UNAVAILABLE

PROVIDER_LOGIN_UNSUPPORTED

PROVIDER_LOGOUT_UNSUPPORTED

PRO

VIDER_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE

PROVIDER_NEUTRAL_FOLDER_UNSAFE

PROVIDER_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN_ESAURITO

PROVIDER_POOL_FULL

PROVIDER_RUNTIME_INVALID

PROVIDER_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE

PROVIDER_SETTINGS_NOT_SAVED

he model provider. Check the network and the provider address, then try again.

COMPACTION_SUMMARY_TOOL_CALL
TALOS did not compact the conversation: the model answered with a tool call instead of a summary. Try /compact again; if it keeps happening, choose another model for this conversation.
CTX_PENDING_TOOLS
A tool call in this conversation has no result yet, so it cannot be compacted now. Nothing was changed. Wait for the running tools to finish, or send a message so the turn closes, then try /compact again.
HOOK_FILE_LINK
A hook command names a symbolic link, which TALOS does not accept. Point the hook at the real file instead of the link.
HOOK_FILE_TOO_LARGE
A file named by a hook command is too large to fingerprint. Use a smaller script file for the hook.
HOOK_FILE_UNREADABLE
The files this hook runs cannot be read, so it cannot be checked. Check that the files exist and can be read, then trust the hook again.
HOOK_REFUSED
A hook of this project said no to a tool, so the tool did not change anything. See why with talos hook dry-run <id> pre_tool_call; a hook whose command has shell operators is always refused.
KERNEL_TOOL_LIST_UNAVAILABLE
TALOS could not start: this runtime does not say which tools the model may use, so it cannot leave out questions when nobody can answer them. Reinstall TALOS with npm install -g talos-code; if it keeps happening, keep the log for a report.
MCP_SCRIPT_UNREADABLE
The scripts this MCP server runs cannot be read, so it cannot be checked. Check that the files exist and can be read, then trust the server again.
TOOL_RESULT_INVALID
A tool did not say whether it succeeded, so its outcome is unconfirmed. Check its effects before running it again; TALOS does not retry it on its own.

CHATGPT_SIGN_IN_TIMEOUT
The sign-in was not completed in the browser in time. Run talos provider login chatgpt again.
CONFIG_INVALID_QUESTION_TIMEOUT
How long questions wait, in the configuration, is not a value TALOS knows. Use never, 1m, 5m or 10m, or change it in /config.
CTX_COMPACTION_TIMEOUT
The summary of the conversation took too long, so TALOS stopped waiting for it and compacted without the model. Nothing to do: the turn goes on. If it happens often, choose a faster model for this conversation, or lower context.compactAtTokens so summaries stay shorter.
MODEL_LIST_TIMEOUT
A provider did not answer in time when TALOS asked which models it has. Nothing to do: the models of the providers that answered can still be used. Try again in a moment for the others.
RUN_TIMEOUT
The run went past its time limit and was stopped. Give it more time with --timeout, or split the task into smaller steps.

AUTOMATION_NOT_FOUND
There is no automation with that id. See the automations and their ids with talos automation list.
CHECKPOINT_NOT_FOUND
There is no checkpoint here to undo or redo. TALOS makes a checkpoint when it changes files in this project; talos checkpoint list shows them.
CHECKPOINT_SESSION_MISSING
TALOS could not associate the recovery checkpoint with a session. Inspect the project changes and keep talos logs for a report before continuing.
OUTPUT_SESSION_UNAVAILABLE
Saved outputs cannot be read for this session. Open the session again, then retry.
SESSION_BUSY
A turn is running or messages are queued. Stop the turn or wait for it, then try again.
SESSION_CHANGED_ELSEWHERE
Another TALOS changed this conversation since it was opened here, so nothing was written. Open the conversation again (talos --resume) before going on.
SESSION_DELETE_FAILED
TALOS could not delete that conversation; it is still there.
SESSION_DELETE_UNAVAILABLE
This TALOS runtime cannot delete conversations. Update TALOS, then try again.
SESSION_LEASED
This conversation is open in another TALOS. Go on there, or close it there and try again.
SESSION_LEASE_CLOSED
TALOS is closing and takes no new work on this conversation. Start TALOS again.
SESSION_LIST_INDEX_INVALID_ROOT
The session list index did not get its data folders. Run talos doctor and keep the log for a report.
SESSION_LIST_INDEX_UNKNOWN_ID
The sessions folder holds a file that is not a TALOS session. Move that file out of the sessions folder, or run talos doctor.
SESSION_NOT_FOUND
That session was not found.
SESSION_NOT_READY
That conversation is busy saving, so nothing was changed. Try again in a moment.
SESSION_QUEUE_FAILED
TALOS could not put the message in the queue of the running turn. Send it again when the turn ends; if it happens again, run talos doctor and keep the log for a report.
SESSION_STILL_RUNNING
That conversation is still running, so it was not deleted. Stop it first, then delete it.
SESSION_STORE_AMBIGUOUS
The session store found more than one record for this session. Keep talos logs for a report before continuing.
SESSION_STORE_BAD_ARGUMENT
The session store was called incorrectly. Keep talos logs for a report.
SESSION_STORE_BAD_POLICY
The session store received a write policy it does not know. Keep talos logs for a report.
SESSION_STORE_BUSY
The session store is finishing another write. Wait a moment, then try again.
SESSION_STORE_FLUSH_EXHAUSTED
The session kept writing, so its store could not finish saving before closing. Stop the running answer with Esc, then close again.
SESSION_STORE_HEADER_EXISTS
This session already has a saved record. Resume the session instead of starting it again.
SESSION_STORE_HEADER_FAILED
The session record could not be started on disk. Check free disk space and that the TALOS data folder is writable.
SESSION_STORE_INSPECTION_FAILED
The session could not be inspected for recovery. Check the session id, then try again.
SESSION_STORE_PRECONDITION_FAILED
The

session changed before its record was written, so nothing was saved. Try again.
SESSION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE
This step needs the session store on disk, and it is not available. Check that the TALOS data folder is writable.
WORKFLOW_ROOT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND
The session that proposed this workflow no longer exists. Start the workflow again from an open session.
WORKFLOW_STEP_SESSION_AMBIGUOUS
Two sessions claim the same workflow step. Keep talos logs for a report before continuing.

AGENT_CONTROL_FORBIDDEN
An agent tried to stop a sub-agent that is not one of its own. Nothing to do: the sub-agent keeps running. Stop it from the agents panel if you want it to end.
AGENT_DIALOGUE_FORBIDDEN
A delegated agent can talk only to its direct parent, and that parent is no longer available. Continue from the parent session, or start the delegation again.
AGENT_DIALOGUE_STORE_FAILED
The question between agents could not be saved, so it was not sent. Check that the TALOS data folder is writable, then try again.
ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE
The artifact is larger than TALOS accepts. Make the page smaller, or split it into several artifacts.
AUTOMATION_HOST_NOT_ANSWERING
The TALOS process that runs the automations did not answer. Check that it is not stuck (talos automation serve shows it), then try again.
AUTOMATION_HOST_RUNNING
Another TALOS process is running the automations, so this one did not check them. Leave it to that process, or stop it first; talos automation run <id> works while it runs.
AUTOMATION_LEGACY
This automation was made by an older TALOS and cannot run or be edited. Delete it and make it again with instructions: talos automation add "<instructions>" --when "<when>".
AUTOMATION_NOTHING_TO_CHANGE
Nothing to change was given. Say what to change: --instructions, --when, --name, --folder, --model, --mode, --repeat, --coordination or --timezone.
AUTOMATION_NO_RUN_IN_PROGRESS
This automation is not running. There is nothing to stop.
AUTOMATION_OPERATION_REMOVED
That operation was for the old format of automations. Change when it runs with talos automation edit <id> --when "<when>", and see the next run with talos automation show <id>.
AUTOMATION_PROPOSAL_DECIDED
This proposal was already approved or discarded. There is nothing left to decide for it.
AUTOMATION_PROPOSAL_NOT_FOUND
That run did not propose new instructions. Pick a run that has a proposal.
AUTOMATION_PROPOSAL_STALE
The instructions changed after this proposal was made. Compare them again before changing them.
AUTOMATION_REPEAT
The number of times to run must be a whole number, at least 1. Write it as a number, for example --repeat 3.
AUTOMATION_RUN_IN_PROGRESS
This automation is already running. Wait for that run to end, or stop it.
AUTOMATION_RUN_NOT_STARTED
The automation could not start its run. Read the detail below, then try talos automation run <id> again.
AUTOMATION_SCHEDULE_PAST
That time has already passed. Choose a time in the future.
AUTOMATION_SCHEDULE_TOO_FREQUENT
That schedule runs too often. Choose a longer interval.
AUTOMATION_STORE_READ_FAILED
TALOS could not read that automation from the disk just now. Try again in a moment; if it keeps failing, check that nothing else holds the files in the TALOS data folder.
AUTOMATION_TASK_DEFINITION_MISMATCH
The TALOS task in Windows Task Scheduler is not the one TALOS set up. Set it up again with talos automation install-runner --yes.
AUTOMATION_TASK_FAILED
Windows Task Scheduler did not accept the change. Read the

detail below; in Task Scheduler the task is called «TALOS CLI Automation Runner».
CHATGPT_CLIENT_MISMATCH
The browser came back for a different sign-in than the one TALOS started. Run talos provider login chatgpt again.
CHATGPT_CODE_MISSING
The browser came back without the sign-in code. Run talos provider login chatgpt again.
CHATGPT_ERROR
The request to the ChatGPT plan did not complete. Try again. If it keeps failing, the details are in talos logs; if ChatGPT says you are signed out, run talos provider login chatgpt.
CHATGPT_EXCHANGE_REFUSED
OpenAI refused to complete the sign-in. Run talos provider login chatgpt again.
CHATGPT_MODEL_LIST_UNREADABLE
The model list of the ChatGPT plan could not be read. Try again; if it goes on, sign in again with talos provider login chatgpt.
CHATGPT_NETWORK
OpenAI could not be reached. Check the connection and try again.
CHATGPT_NOT_CONNECTED
No ChatGPT account is connected. Sign in with talos provider login chatgpt, or pick another provider with /provider.
CHATGPT_OTHER_ACCOUNT
A different ChatGPT account answered than the one connected before. Sign out with talos provider logout chatgpt, then sign in with the account you want.
CHATGPT_PLAN_LIMIT
The ChatGPT plan usage limit was reached. Go on now with another model: /model. Or wait for the limit to come back (ChatGPT Settings → Usage).
CHATGPT_PLAN_NOT_ALLOWED
The ChatGPT plan cannot be used with this account, workspace or policy. Use an OpenAI API key or another provider with /provider.
CHATGPT_PLAN_NOT_ENABLED
Using the ChatGPT plan is not enabled for this sign-in. Run talos provider login chatgpt again and allow the plan, or pick another provider with /provider.
CHATGPT_RENEWAL_FAILED
The ChatGPT session could not be renewed. Try again; the session was kept.
CHATGPT_REQUEST_INCOMPLETE
The request for the ChatGPT plan was incomplete. Try again; if it goes on, sign in again with talos provider login chatgpt.
CHATGPT_REQUEST_NOT_SUPPORTED
This request uses something the ChatGPT plan does not support. Pick another model or provider for it.
CHATGPT_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
The ChatGPT plan is temporarily unavailable. Try again later.
CHATGPT_SIGN_IN_CANCELLED
The sign-in was cancelled. Run talos provider login chatgpt again when you want to sign in.
CHATGPT_SIGN_IN_EXPIRED
The ChatGPT sign-in is no longer valid. Sign in again with talos provider login chatgpt.
CHATGPT_SIGN_IN_REPLACED
This sign-in was closed: a newer ChatGPT sign-in started in another TALOS. Finish the sign-in in the other TALOS, or run talos provider login chatgpt here again.
CHATGPT_STATE_MISMATCH
The browser came back for a sign-in TALOS did not start. Run talos provider login chatgpt again and use the address it prints.
CHATGPT_STORE_FAILED
The ChatGPT credentials could not be stored in the system keyring. Check the keyring with talos doctor, then sign in again.
CHATGPT_STORE_MISSING
The system keyring is not available, so the ChatGPT sign-in cannot be kept. Check the keyring with talos doctor

.
CHATGPT_STORE_NOT_KEPT
Credentials are kept in memory only, so a sign-in made by this command would be lost the moment it ends. Sign in from /provider inside TALOS (it lasts until TALOS closes), or set credentials.store to system to keep it.
CHATGPT_UNAVAILABLE
A ChatGPT account cannot be connected on this computer: the system keyring is not available. Use an OpenAI API key or another provider with /provider.
CHATGPT_UNEXPECTED_ANSWER
OpenAI answered in a way TALOS does not understand. Try again later.
CHECKPOINT_CONFLICT
A file changed after this checkpoint was made, so undoing or redoing it would overwrite that change. Nothing was changed. The details name the file. Undo works only while the files are as the turn left them: put that file back, or keep things as they are.
CHECKPOINT_FINALIZE_FAILED
TALOS could not save the checkpoint of this turn; the work itself is done. /undo cannot go back to before this turn. Check the free space and permissions of the TALOS data folder (talos doctor).
CHECKPOINT_OWNER_CHANGED
TALOS could not verify the recovery checkpoint after the runtime restarted. Inspect the project changes and talos logs before continuing in a new session.
CLI_NOTICE
TALOS has a notice about this turn. Read the notice; nothing has failed.
COMMAND_ENVIRONMENT_CHANGED
The shell changed after the model prepared the command, so the command did not run. Ask the model to prepare the command again for the current shell.
COMMAND_ENVIRONMENT_CLOSED
TALOS is closing, so no new command can start. Run the command again after TALOS restarts.
COMMAND_ENVIRONMENT_PENDING
A change to the command shell is still being saved. Wait a moment, then run the command again.
COMMAND_ENVIRONMENT_UNSUPPORTED
This session cannot use a Windows or WSL shell. Use the default shell for this session.
COMMAND_NEVER_FINISHED
TALOS stopped before this command finished: nothing was left running that could give its answer. Run it again; if it happens again, run talos doctor and report it with the command you ran.
COMPACTION_AT_MINIMUM
TALOS did not compact the conversation: it is over the compaction threshold, but what is left is the part TALOS always keeps word for word (your first request, your latest requests and the latest exchanges), already shortened as far as it goes. It can be compacted again once a few newer requests push the long ones out of the latest; for a new task, start a new conversation.
COMPACTION_FAILED
TALOS did not compact the conversation, and the kernel did not say why. Try /compact again; if it keeps happening, start a new conversation with /clear.
COMPACTION_INEFFECTIVE
TALOS did not compact the conversation: the summary was written, but it would have made the conversation longer, so it was not used. Nothing to do now; TALOS compacts by itself when a summary can make the conversation smaller.
COMPACTION_LITTLE_GAIN
TALOS did not compact the conversation: a summary would save little now, because the older part is too small to make it noticeably sho

rter. It pays off after a few more exchanges; TALOS compacts by itself when a summary is worth it.
COMPACTION_NOT_FOUND
That compaction is not the latest one, so it cannot be undone. Only the most recent compaction can be undone.
COMPACTION_NOT_SAVED
TALOS did not compact the conversation: the summary was written but could not be saved. Check that the TALOS data folder has free space and can be written, then try /compact again.
COMPACTION_NO_SUMMARY
TALOS did not compact the conversation: the model answered, but its summary was cut short or empty. That request was billed. Try /compact again; if it keeps happening, choose another model for this conversation, or one with more output room.
COMPACTION_SUMMARY_EMPTY
TALOS did not compact the conversation: the model sent back an empty summary. Try /compact again; if it keeps happening, choose another model for this conversation.
COMPACTION_SUMMARY_EXHAUSTED
TALOS did not compact the conversation: the summary already failed three times in a row in this turn, so it was not asked again. Send your next message, then try /compact again; if it keeps failing, choose another model for this conversation.
COMPACTION_SUMMARY_FAILED
TALOS did not compact the conversation: the summary request failed. Try /compact again; if it keeps happening, choose another model for this conversation.
COMPACTION_SUMMARY_REFUSED
TALOS did not compact the conversation: the model refused to write the summary. Choose another model for this conversation and try /compact again.
COMPACTION_SUMMARY_TRUNCATED
TALOS did not compact the conversation: the summary was cut off before it finished. Try again; if it keeps happening, choose a model with more output room, or set models.<provider:model>.maxOutputTokens.
CONTEXT_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE
This TALOS runtime cannot report how full the context is. Go on working: the context is still managed; /compact compacts it on request.
CTX_COMPACTION_FAILED
Compacting this conversation did not work; the previous context stays in use. Try /compact again; if it keeps happening, start a new conversation with /clear.
CTX_CONTEXT_OVERFLOW
This conversation is too big for the model’s context window, even after compaction. Run /compact or start a new conversation with /clear. If the model’s window is larger than TALOS measured, set it: talos config set models.<provider:model>.contextWindow <tokens>.
CTX_CONTEXT_TOO_SMALL
The room TALOS keeps for the answer (the response reserve) plus its instructions do not fit in the model’s context window. Lower the reserve: talos config set models.<provider:model>.maxOutputTokens <tokens>. If the window is larger than TALOS measured, set it: talos config set models.<provider:model>.contextWindow <tokens>. /context shows both.
CTX_EMPTY_SUMMARY
The model sent back an empty summary, so this conversation was not compacted. Try /compact again; if it keeps happening, choose another model for this conversation.
CTX_HISTORY_DIVERGED
This conversation no longer matches its saved conte

xt, so TALOS stopped before sending anything. Nothing was lost. Continue it in a new session with /fork (it keeps the whole conversation), or start fresh with /clear.
CTX_JOB_INTERRUPTED
A compaction was interrupted because the TALOS process running it stopped; nothing was changed. Nothing to fix: the next request or /compact starts it again.
CTX_NOTHING_TO_COMPACT
There is nothing to compact yet: the conversation has no earlier exchanges to summarize. Nothing to do; compaction becomes possible once the conversation grows.
CTX_NO_REDUCTION
The summary did not make this conversation smaller, so the previous context stays in use. Start a new conversation with /clear, or choose a model with a larger context window.
CTX_SEGMENT_TOO_LARGE
Part of this conversation is too large to summarize with this model. Start a new conversation with /clear, or choose a model with a larger context window.
CTX_TOKEN_HTTP
The provider’s token counter answered with an error. Try again; if it keeps happening, check the provider’s status.
CTX_TOKEN_NETWORK
TALOS could not reach the provider’s token counter. Check the network, then try again.
CTX_TRUNCATED_SUMMARY
The summary that compacts this conversation was cut off before it finished. Try again; if it keeps happening, choose a model with more output room, or set models.<provider:model>.maxOutputTokens.
DELEGATION_READ_ONLY
This delegation is read-only, so it cannot make changes. Start a new delegation that is allowed to edit.
DIAGNOSTIC_REDACTION_FAILED
The diagnostic bundle was not written: the conversation could not be proved free of secrets. Nothing was exported. Make the bundle without --session, or report this.
ELICITATION_ANSWER_FAILED
TALOS could not deliver your answer to the MCP server. Answer again; if it keeps failing, keep the log for a report.
ELICITATION_NOT_OPEN
This request from the MCP server is already closed. Nothing to do; if the server still needs it, it asks again.
ELICITATION_NOT_PENDING
The MCP server is no longer waiting for this answer. Nothing to do; if the server still needs it, it asks again.
EXECUTION_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE
No isolation backend is available, so the command did not run. See the sandbox section of talos doctor.
FORK_CUT_UNAVAILABLE
This TALOS cannot start a conversation before an earlier message yet. Fork from «latest», or update TALOS.
FORK_CUT_UNCONFIRMED
The new conversation did not confirm where it starts, so it is not used.
FORK_POINT_COMPACTED
That message is inside the part of this conversation that was summarized, so nothing was forked. Pick a message after the last summary, or fork from «latest».
FORK_POINT_NOT_FOUND
TALOS could not find that message in this conversation, so nothing was forked. Fork from «latest», or pick another message.
HEADLESS_RESUME_NO_PROMPT
No prompt was given, so the stored session was replayed as-is and the pending turn was not restarted. Pass a prompt with -p (or pipe one in) to continue the turn.
LIBRARY_EXTRA_ARGUMENT
The command got more

words than it takes, so nothing was changed. Write it as talos library versions <id>, or talos library restore <id> <version>.
LIBRARY_IMAGE_NO_VERSIONS
This Library entry is an image: images have no versions. Versions are kept for text entries, such as the artifacts the model updates.
LIBRARY_NOT_FOUND
There is no Library entry with that id, or no such version of it. See the entries with talos library list, and an entry’s versions with talos library versions <id>.
LINE_INPUT_REQUIRES_TTY
This question needs an interactive terminal to answer it. Run the command in a terminal, or give the answer as an option (for the Z.AI address: --address plan, balance, plan-china or balance-china).
LINUX_HOME_CLOSED
The Linux environment of this session was already closed. Send the request again: a new turn opens it again.
LINUX_HOME_ENVIRONMENT_MISSING
The Linux environment was started without its process environment. This is an internal error: run talos doctor and report it.
LINUX_HOME_EXITED
The Linux environment of this session stopped while it was working. Send the request again: the next one starts it again.
LINUX_HOME_PATH_NOT_ON_DRIVE
This path is not on a Windows drive, so Linux cannot reach it. Use a folder on a local Windows drive.
LINUX_HOME_PATH_UNREACHABLE
This path cannot be reached from Linux (a network share or another distribution). Nothing was done. Use a folder on a local Windows drive, or work on Windows for this path.
LINUX_HOME_START_FAILED
TALOS could not start the Linux environment for this session. Check that WSL works (wsl --status), then try again.
LOCAL_RUNTIME_NOT_READY
The local model engine is not running. Start the local engine, or pick another model with /model.
LOGIN_REQUIRES_TTY
Signing in needs an interactive terminal. Run talos provider login <provider> in a terminal; a provider with a key can take one with talos provider set-key <provider>.
METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED
That kind of request is not accepted there. Run talos provider login chatgpt again and open the address it prints in a browser.
MODELS_DEV_TOO_LARGE
The models.dev catalogue answered with more data than TALOS accepts, so it was not used. Nothing to do: model windows come from the other sources until the next try.
MODEL_CALL_FAILED
The call to the model failed. Try again; if it keeps happening, run talos doctor.
MODEL_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE
This TALOS cannot ask the model for one token yet, so the model was not checked. Send a message to see it answer, or update TALOS.
MODEL_CORRUPT
The saved description of a local model is damaged. Remove the model and download it again.
MODEL_EXISTS
A local model with this name already exists. Use the existing model, or remove it first.
MODEL_IMAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED
The selected model does not accept images. Pick a model with vision with /model.
MODEL_LOCKED
That local model is in use by another operation. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
MODEL_NOT_FOUND
That local model is not installed. Check the name, or download the model first.
MOD

EL_READ_FAILED
A local model could not be read. Check that the TALOS data folder is readable.
MODEL_WRITE_FAILED
A local model could not be saved. Check free disk space and that the TALOS data folder is writable.
MODE_WORKFLOW_RETIRED
The Workflow mode has been retired. Choose another mode for this session.
MXC_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE
The Windows sandbox could not be started for this command. See the sandbox section of talos doctor.
NATIVE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED
The request was larger than the model’s context window, so the model stopped before it finished. Start a new conversation with /clear, or choose a model with a larger window with /model. If the model’s window is larger than TALOS measured, set it: talos config set models.<provider:model>.contextWindow <tokens>.
NEEDS_PERSON
This needs a person's yes (a change of the excluded providers, signing out of ChatGPT, or letting a model that repeats itself go on), and nobody can be asked in this mode. Run the task in the TALOS screen and answer the question. You can also do it yourself: talos provider exclude and talos provider allow change the excluded providers, talos provider logout chatgpt signs out of ChatGPT.
NETWORK_NEEDS_PERSON
TALOS did not run the command with network access: outside Full access only a person can open the network for a command, and nobody can be asked in this mode. Run the task in the TALOS screen and answer the question, or use Full access (--permission-mode bypassPermissions) if the commands may reach the network.
NETWORK_PATH_NEEDS_PERSON
TALOS did not open a network path: opening it sends your Windows credentials to that computer, and only a person can allow that. Run the task in the TALOS screen and answer the question, or copy the file into the project first.
NOTIFICATION_ARCH_UNSUPPORTED
Native Windows notifications are unavailable on this CPU architecture. Use bell or off for ui.notifications. Terminal progress remains available.
NOT_FOUND
The session was not found.
OUTPUT_CAPTURE_FAILED
The command’s output could not be saved in full. The command may still have run: check its effects before running it again.
OUTPUT_DECODER_UNAVAILABLE
This installation cannot decode the text encoding of the command’s output. Keep talos logs for a report.
OUTPUT_EXECUTION_UNCERTAIN
TALOS could not confirm whether the command ran. Check its effects before running it again.
OUTPUT_INTEGRITY_FAILED
The saved command output failed its integrity check. Run the command again if you need its output.
OUTPUT_NOT_FOUND
That saved command output no longer exists. Run the command again if you need its output.
OUTPUT_OFFSET_NOT_TEXT_BOUNDARY
The read position falls in the middle of a character. Read from the offset the previous read returned.
OUTPUT_PIPE_CLOSED
The command’s output stream closed before the command finished, so the output is incomplete. Check the command’s effects before running it again.
OUTPUT_RECEIPT_FAILED
The receipt for the command’s output could not be recorded. Check the

command’s effects before running it again.
OUTPUT_STORE_IO
The command output store could not read or write its files. Check free disk space and that the TALOS data folder is writable.
PAYLOAD_LIMIT
The upload is larger than TALOS accepts. Send a smaller file.
PLAN_ALREADY_PENDING
A plan is already waiting for your decision. Approve or reject that plan first.
PLAN_ANSWER_FAILED
TALOS could not deliver your choice on the plan. Choose again; if it keeps failing, keep the log for a report.
PLAN_DECISION_NOT_SAVED
Your decision on the plan could not be saved. Check that the TALOS data folder is writable, then decide again.
PLAN_NOT_OPEN
This plan is already closed: it was decided, or it ended with the turn. Nothing to do; if the model still needs your approval, it proposes the plan again.
PLAN_NOT_PENDING
No plan is waiting for a decision. Nothing to do.
PLAN_STALE
That plan was replaced by a newer one. Review the latest plan and decide on that one.
PLATFORM_PACKAGE_MISSING
The Windows sandbox is missing: npm did not install the optional package with the programs for this computer. Reinstall TALOS with npm install -g talos-code, without --omit=optional.
PROCESS_TREE_PROBE_ABORTED
The sandbox check was stopped because TALOS was closing, so it gave no result. Nothing to do: TALOS checks the sandbox again the next time it starts.
PROJECT_AGENTS_IGNORED
The project configuration tried to set the delegated agents' limits or model, so that setting was ignored. Set agents in your user or project-user configuration.
PROJECT_MODELS_IGNORED
The project configuration tried to set a model's context window, so that setting was ignored. Set models in your user or project-user configuration.
PROJECT_UNTRUSTED_IGNORED
The project's own rules are not applied: this project is not trusted. Trust it with talos project trust if you want its rules to apply.
QUESTION_ALREADY_PENDING
A question is already waiting for your answer. Answer that question first.
QUESTION_ANSWER_FAILED
TALOS could not deliver your answer to the questions. Answer again; if it keeps failing, keep the log for a report.
QUESTION_ANSWER_NOT_SAVED
Your answer could not be saved. Check that the TALOS data folder is writable, then answer again.
QUESTION_CHILD_FORBIDDEN
Only the main agent can ask you questions. Nothing to do: the delegated agent was told to ask its parent instead.
QUESTION_NOT_OPEN
These questions are already closed: they were answered, cancelled or ended with the turn. Nothing to do; if the model still needs an answer, it asks again.
QUESTION_NOT_PENDING
No question is waiting for an answer. Nothing to do.
QUEUE_BUSY
The queue is already sending its messages. Wait for the queue to finish, then try again.
QUEUE_ENTRY_DELIVERED
That queued message was already sent: it went into the turn before the change arrived. Read the answer to it; to change course, send a new message or steer with Ctrl+Enter or Alt+S.
REGISTRY_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE
This action is not available in this TALOS runtime. Upd

ate TALOS with talos update; if it is already current, keep the log for a report.
REMOTE_NOT_AVAILABLE
Remote control is not available in TALOS CLI yet. Pair a device and turn remote control on in TALOS Desktop. To ask the model about it, put the question in quotes: talos "remote …".
REPLAY_EVENTS_EXPIRED
This view asked for session events older than the ones TALOS keeps in memory. Reopen the session with /resume: it reloads the whole conversation from disk.
REQUEST_TOO_LARGE
The message is too large for this model. Nothing was summarized. Shorten it, or send it as an attachment with --attach-if-too-large: the model gets its start and end and reads the rest from a file.
RESOURCE_DIRECTORY_SYMLINK_UNSUPPORTED
A plugin or a .talos folder of this project contains a link to another place, which TALOS does not follow, so the project is not trusted. Replace the link with the real files, then run talos project trust again.
RULE
"Allow always" answers for this session only; approve it again next time.
RULE_COMMAND_UNSUPPORTED
This command cannot be split into parts TALOS can judge, so no rule is saved for it.
RULE_COMPOUND_COMMAND
A command made of several parts is not remembered as a rule.
RULE_MATCHES_NOTHING
The rule for this request would not match the request itself, so it is not saved.
RULE_UNREADABLE
The rule for this request could not be read back, so it is not saved.
RUNTIME_NOT_AVAILABLE
No model runtime is available for this session. Pick a provider and a model with /provider and /model.
SERVER_SHUTTING_DOWN
TALOS is shutting down and accepts no new work. Try again after TALOS restarts.
TIMELINE_READ_FAILED
TALOS could not read the older part of the agents' history from the session file. The recent part is still shown; try again, and if it keeps failing keep the log for a report.
TUI_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE
The model and provider list is not available in this TALOS runtime. Restart TALOS; if it happens again, run talos doctor and keep the log for a report.
WORKFLOW_STEP_TERMINAL_NOT_DURABLE
The workflow step finished, but its end was not saved to disk. Treat the step as unconfirmed and check its effects.

ABORT_ERR
This was stopped before it finished. Run it again if you still need it.
CANCELLED
Cancelled.

pagine.descrizione: Where TALOS CLI keeps settings, sessions, logs, checkpoints and trust records.

sezioni.testo:
What | Windows | macOS and Linux
Settings (user scope: config.json) | %APPDATA%\TALOS-CLI | ~/.config/talos-cli
Data | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI | ~/.local/state/talos-cli
Cache | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI\cache | ~/.cache/talos-cli
Sessions | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI\sessions | ~/.local/state/talos-cli/sessions
Logs | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI\logs | ~/.local/state/talos-cli/logs
File checkpoints | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI\checkpoints | ~/.local/state/talos-cli/checkpoints
Your per-project settings (project-user scope) | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI\projects | ~/.local/state/talos-cli/projects
Queued messages | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI\queues | ~/.local/state/talos-cli/queues
Trust records: hooks | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI\trust\hooks | ~/.local/state/talos-cli/trust/hooks
Trust records: MCP servers | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI\trust\mcp | ~/.local/state/talos-cli/trust/mcp
Trust records: plugins | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI\trust\plugins | ~/.local/state/talos-cli/trust/plugins
Trust records: projects | %LOCALAPPDATA%\TALOS-CLI\trust\projects | ~/.local/state/talos-cli/trust/projects

- .talos-cli/config.json: the project settings (the project scope).
- .talos-cli/commands/: custom commands, see talos command.
- .talos-cli/extensions/: installed plugins.

talos init creates them.

pagine.descrizione: The options of talos itself, given before a subcommand or with a prompt.

sezioni.testo:
These options go before a subcommand (talos --project ../api session list) or with a prompt (talos -p "…" --json).

-p, --print <prompt>
Run one prompt without the interactive screen (headless) and print the answer.
--json
Print one JSON result at the end instead of text. Same as --output-format json.
--output-format <format>
text (default), json (one result at the end) or stream-json (one JSON event per line, as they happen). Valuestextjsonstream-json
--protocol <version>
The version of the headless event and result format, v1 (default) or v2. v2 needs --json or --output-format stream-json, and only applies to headless runs. Valuesv1v2
--project <path>
The project folder. Default: the current folder.
--model <provider:model>
The model for this run, e.g. openai:gpt-5-mini. Overrides the configured one.
--permission-mode <mode>
How actions are approved for this run. See Permissions. ValuesdefaultacceptEditsplanautodontAskbypassPermissions
--resume <id|last>
Continue a session; last is the most recent.
--fork <id>
Start a new session from a copy of a session.
-v, --verbose
Show more detail when something fails, including the trace id.
--no-color
Plain text, without colors.
--timeout <seconds>
Stop a headless run after this many seconds (a positive integer). Default 180.
--version
Print the version and exit.
-h, --help
Print the usage and exit.
--attach-if-too-large
Not yet described.

- --resume and --fork are mutually exclusive.

pagine.descrizione: Every command, option, setting, variable, key and code of TALOS CLI 0.6.14, read from the release itself.

sezioni.testo:
Running talos

```
talos [prompt…]
```

Opens the interactive screen in the current folder; a prompt, if given, is the first message.
```
talos setup
```

Opens the guided setup: provider, key and model.
```
talos -p <prompt> [--json | --output-format stream-json]
```

Runs one task without the interactive screen (headless) and prints the answer, a JSON result, or a stream of JSON events.
```
talos --resume <id|last> [-p <prompt>]
```

Continues a session; last is the most recent one.
```
talos --fork <id> [-p <prompt>]
```

Starts a new session from a copy of an existing one.
```
talos <family> <operation> [arguments] [options]
```

Runs a subcommand: see the families below.

- Headless: when no prompt is given and the standard input is not a terminal, the prompt is read from the standard input.
- A headless run stops after 180 seconds unless --timeout says otherwise.
- In headless runs nothing can be asked: an action that needs approval is denied, and the run says so.

Command families · 22

- talos project Whether TALOS trusts the project folder, and the files in it that can run code. 5
- talos config Reads and writes settings in the user, project and project-user scopes; simulates a permission decision. 9
- talos provider The model providers: keys, sign-in, endpoints and health. 12
- talos model Lists models, picks the model TALOS uses and its reasoning effort. 3
- talos session Lists, finds, labels, resumes, forks, shares, exports, imports and deletes sessions. 15
- talos mcp The MCP servers TALOS can use: list, trust, untrust, test. 4
- talos hook Commands that run on session events: list, trust, test with a synthetic event, history, quarantine. 8
- talos plugin Extension packages: install, remove, list, trust, quarantine. 8
- talos command Your own commands, skills and workflows written in Markdown: list, show, expand. 3

pagine.descrizione: How TALOS CLI decides whether an action runs, asks or is denied: modes, rules and their order.

sezioni.testo:
Choose a mode with --permission-mode, the permissionMode setting, or in the interactive screen.

defaultAsk before editsdefault
Reads freely; asks before changing files, running commands or any other action no rule allows.
acceptEditsAccept edits
Also allows, without asking, file edits inside the project and simple file commands (mkdir, touch, rm, rmdir, cp, mv) — never in protected folders.
planPlan
Read only: writing files, editing, hooks, plugins and shell commands that change anything are denied.
autoAuto
A classifier decides for actions no rule covers: it allows, denies, or lets TALOS ask you. Never in protected folders.
dontAskDon't ask
Never asks: whatever would need your approval is denied.
bypassPermissionsFull access
Allows every action that would otherwise ask, when no rule names it. Warning. Use it only in a disposable environment you can restore. Deny and ask rules, and the block on writing outside the project, still apply.

- A write or an edit outside the project folder is denied.
- A deny rule that matches denies.
- In plan mode, writing, editing, hooks, plugins and shell commands that change anything are denied.
- An action you allowed for this session is allowed.
- An allow rule that matches allows.
- An ask rule that matches always asks: no mode skips it.
- Otherwise the mode decides: acceptEdits, auto and bypassPermissions may allow (see Modes).
- If nothing allowed it: in dontAsk mode, or when nothing can be asked (a headless run), it is denied. Otherwise TALOS asks you.
- When TALOS asks, you can allow it once, for the session, or always (an allow rule is written), or always deny it (a deny rule is written).

A rule is written Tool(pattern) on one line, e.g. Bash(npm test) or Edit(./src/**). It goes in permissions.allow, permissions.ask or permissions.deny of a settings file. A rule that cannot be read stops TALOS from starting, and says which one.

Bash: the pattern is a command, matched word by word. Bash(npm test) matches exactly npm test; Bash(npm run:*) matches every command that starts with npm run; Bash(*) matches any command. A command with &, |, ;, <, > or parentheses never matches a rule.

Read, Write, Edit: the pattern is a path relative to the project. * and ** match any characters (not spaces); ./** is anything inside the project; * alone is any path. A pattern that starts with . never matches a path outside the project.

Mcp: the pattern is server:operation, e.g. Mcp(github:*). TalosService: operation or resource:operation. The other tools match their operation or resource.

Tool | What a rule on it covers
Read | Reading a file. Pattern: a path.
Write | Creating or overwriting a file. Pattern: a path.
Edit | Changing a file. Pattern: a path.
Bash | A shell command. Pattern: the command, or its first words followed by :*.
WebFetch | Fetching a web page. Pattern: the address.
Mcp | A tool of an MCP server. Pattern: server:operation.
Hook | Running a hook. Pattern: the hook.
Plugin | Running a plugin. Pattern: the plugin.
TalosService | A TALOS service (memory, notes, tasks…). Pattern: operation or resource:operation.

Try a rule without running anything: talos config permissions dry-run --tool Bash --command "npm test".

The acceptEdits and auto modes never allow changes in these folders of the project: they always ask.

.git/.talos-cli/.github/.vscode/.idea/.husky/

In acceptEdits mode these commands run without asking, with only these options, on paths inside the project:

Command | Options it may carry
mkdir | -p -v
touch | -a -m -c
rm | -r -R -f -rf -fr -d
rmdir | -p
cp | -r -R -f -n -p
mv | -f -n

pagine.descrizione: What changed in each version of TALOS Desktop, newest first, from the changelog of the release in force.

sezioni.testo: What changed in each version of TALOS Desktop, as its changelog says — read from the release of 0.1.38. Newest first; every published version is listed on Versions, and the three apps share one timeline.

Released Oct 25, 2026 · Release

### Fixed

- Attachments work again in the installed app. Adding a file to a conversation, from the window or from a paired device, failed with «could not copy the file into the attachments folder»: the installer shipped the small program that saves attachments without the fingerprint TALOS checks before running it, so every attachment was refused, and the attempt to rebuild it could open a second TALOS window. The parent does not wait for its child, so the parent’s next request — which repeats the delegated task inside its own tool call — could reach the engine first. - Reading a file stops at 1 MiB and says so, and a binary file’s bytes never end up in the conversation.

- Automatic compaction pauses after a refused summary, says for how long, and shortens the kept tail under pressure instead of giving up.

pagine.descrizione: Plan first or work normally, sub-agents and Coordination, the delegation diagram, workflows you approve, the Board, and runs on a schedule.

sezioni.testo: One session can involve more than one agent: the one you talk to, the sub-agents it hands work to, and the steps of a workflow you approved. Each one works under the same permissions — a sub-agent gets its parent’s, never more — and each one is visible.

sezioni.titolo: Work mode: normally, or plan first
sezioni.testo:
A session works in one of two modes, chosen in its permissions panel:

- Work normally — the agent acts as it goes, within its permissions.
- Plan first — the agent prepares a plan and takes no action; the permission pill reads Plan: read only. When the plan is ready it presents it and the turn pauses until you choose how to proceed.

When it needs a decision from you, it asks a question with options.

The agent can hand a self-contained piece of work to a child session: it starts with nothing but the instruction it was given, works on its own, and reports back only its result. None of its intermediate steps enter the main conversation; that is the point of it. By default it works in the same folder.

- At most 10 children at once under the same parent, and two levels deep: a child can have children, and there the chain stops.
- Permissions go through the parent. A child’s permission request appears in the parent session, and a “yes for this session” given there also holds for its children — never upward or sideways. A child can ask you a question the same way.
- You stay in control. A child can be paused, resumed, retried or stopped, by you or by the model. A paused child is still paused after a restart. Its result is judged from what it did, not from the words of its task.

You follow the children in the Agents tab of the session’s details column: each one with its state — running, waiting, paused, stopped, done or failed — and its conversation, which opens without moving the parent’s chat.

### Stop with agents at work

When you press Stop while agents are still working, a small menu opens over it — “2 agents are still working” — with Stop everything (the chat and its agents), Stop only the chat (the agents keep working; stop them from the Agents tab), and Remember my choice. Without agents at work, Stop is immediate. The chat then says Stopped 2 agents too. When the chat is idle and agents are still working, the button next to Send reads Stop the agent or “Stop the 2 agents”; their results stay queued and go with your next message. The model can stop them too when you ask: the row reads Stopped by the model on request. To set the answer once, open Settings → Chat and composer → Stop while agents are working: Ask every time, Stop everything, or Stop only the chat.

Coordination, in the permissions sheet, decides whether the model starts agents on its own. It is off by default: the model asks you first, with a card. On, it starts them by itself, up to 20 in a conversation; past that, it asks again. In Full access it never asks. An agent started this way says On its own (Coordination); one you allowed says Allowed by you.

Every delegation is drawn on the Workflow diagram, live, one request at a time, with the earlier requests one click away. Follow active keeps the working agent in the center; you can filter by state, isolate a branch, see the files each agent touched, and replay what the history saved.

The Board is the table of every session of TALOS Desktop: session, status, model, turns, tokens, cache, first token, why it closed, cost, and when it started. Usage columns count the whole session, not its last message. A session whose last turn ended in an error reads To resume, not “failed”; an old session with no recorded outcome reads Done · outcome not recorded — which is not “succeeded”.

An automation is an instruction TALOS carries out by itself, on a schedule, in a folder you chose. Create one from Automations, or ask any chat and approve a card. Each run starts fresh and cannot ask you questions; what it did is in its runs, and a run with something to tell you lands in To review. See Schedule an automation.

pagine.descrizione: The preamble TALOS Desktop sends before your message, your project's instructions, and how a long conversation is kept within the model's window.

sezioni.testo: Everything the model knows about your work, it reads in the conversation: a short preamble, your messages and attachments, and what its tools bring back. Knowing what goes in explains both what the agent knows and what a conversation costs.

Before your message, TALOS sends the model a preamble of four blocks, from the one that changes least to the one that changes most:

- The engine’s instructions — who the agent is and how it behaves. They cannot be edited.
- Your project’s instructions — the content of AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md in the folder you work on.
- The folder map — the shape of the project, not the list of every file. Files are searched when needed.
- The working card — the state of version control, the active permission, the model, and how the work is verified.

The preamble is paid at every message, not once. A long instructions file is the most common reason a conversation costs more than expected.

A file of instructions in the project reaches the model with every message: it is where you write the rules the agent must always follow.

- One file per folder, looked for in this order: AGENTS.md, then CLAUDE.md.
- A subfolder can have its own: it applies to that part of the project and wins over the one above.
- The search never climbs above the project’s root: an AGENTS.md in your home folder is not read.
- There is a cap: 24,000 bytes by default. A file over it keeps its start and its end, and the model is told how much was cut from the middle; a file left out entirely is named.

Keep them short. See Project files for every file a project can hold.

- Memory goes in at the start of a session: what you asked TALOS to remember, most recently updated first, up to 3,500 characters. What does not fit is said, and the model can find the rest with its memory tool. A memory that looks like an attack stays out, and you can see and delete it in Memory. Sub-agents get no memories. See Where work lives.
- The Library stays out. The model reads a Library document only when it searches for it or opens it.

What you attach with + in the composer is part of the message, and of every message after it. Each attachment shows an estimate of what it costs in tokens before you send. Up to 10 attachments per message, up to 200,000 characters each — about 50,000 tokens, half a window for one file. See Attach files and images.

A long conversation eventually fills the model’s window. TALOS keeps it within bounds:

- The measure — the Context tab and Context Manager show how much of the limit is in use, and where the count comes from (the provider, the engine, or an estimate marked “~”). The measure is the size of the last request’s prompt.
- Compaction — new conversations use the context engine: first old tool output is set aside, then, only if needed, the past is summarized, keeping your own requests word for word. It happens automatically before the limit, or when you choose Compact now. The originals stay in the archive: the summary is what the model reads, not what stays on disk.
- Facts to keep — facts that must survive the summary. They are kept apart from it, and you can add, edit and remove them.
- Versions — the saved summaries. You can restore an earlier one; later messages stay in the chat.

The model that writes the summary can follow the chat’s, or be chosen apart. See Keep a long conversation in bounds.

pagine.descrizione: The window and its local server, sessions you can replay, receipts, and what never leaves your computer.

sezioni.testo: TALOS Desktop is a coding agent that has to show it did the work. It works in a folder of your computer, with a real terminal, a review of what it changed, automations and extensions, driven by the model you choose.

- Explicit authority. What the agent may do on its own is decided before it starts, and stays on screen while it works. See Permissions.
- Verified outcomes. “The model says it worked” and “TALOS observed that it worked” are two different things; only the second counts as done.
- A receipt for every action. Every operation that changes something leaves a signed receipt: what was asked, what ran, what changed.

sezioni.titolo: Two parts: the window and the server
sezioni.testo:
The app is a window and a local server. Everything the window does — sessions, files, Git, models, the browser — goes through the server’s local API. The server answers this computer only: it listens on the loopback address, never on the network. It accepts changes only from the TALOS window (or a paired device), so other web pages and other local servers on the same computer cannot read or change anything.

- No telemetry. No usage data leaves the app.
- Settings stay here. They are kept on this computer and never synced.
- Keys stay in the system keyring, not in the window. See Models and providers.

A session is a conversation with an agent that works in one folder. It is recorded as a sequence of events, not as text: you can close TALOS, reopen it and resume the session where it stopped, and the events can be replayed. What a session streams is listed in Events.

Each session shows an honest status. Those that wait for you come first; a session you stopped is neither done nor failed, it is stopped; and an old session with no recorded outcome says so instead of being counted as a success.

There is no setup wizard: the Home says what is still missing. With no provider it reads No provider is set up, with Set up a provider; in a chat with no folder it asks you to Choose a folder — TALOS only reads and writes inside it. The model and the permission are chosen from the two pills of the composer. See Install TALOS Desktop.

Settings → Appearance and motion → Menu language is Follow the system, English or Italian. It translates menus and controls, not your messages. The server’s messages follow it too. TALOS’s own instructions to the model are in English.

- Permissions — what the agent may do on its own.
- What the model reads — the preamble, project instructions and long conversations.
- Models and providers — cloud models, local models and what they cost.
- Agents and automation — sub-agents, the Board and scheduled runs.
- Where work lives — notes, tasks, the Library, memory, research and projects.

pagine.descrizione: Which models TALOS Desktop can use, where their keys are kept, models that run on your computer, and how usage is counted.

sezioni.testo: TALOS Desktop does not ship a model. It works with the model you choose: one from a provider over the network, or one that runs on this computer.

A provider is who TALOS talks to in order to use a model over the network: OpenRouter, which reaches many models with one access, the direct providers — among them Anthropic, Gemini and OpenAI — and Hugging Face for models to download. Every provider TALOS knows, with its protocol, key and address, is on Providers. With a ChatGPT Plus or Pro account, your ChatGPT plan can take the place of an OpenAI key: see Use your ChatGPT plan.

Providers are configured in Settings → Model Lab, on its Provider tab. For each one it keeps three facts apart, because they are different:

- The credential — whether there is one, and where it comes from: a key you saved, a sign-in, or a key from the environment.
- The address of the service — the default, your own, or still to set.
- The test — whether someone actually tried to reach it, and how it went.

A saved key does not mean a working key: only the test says so. Keys are never kept in the window: they are kept in the operating system’s keyring. Without any access, the server still starts, but read-only: sessions cannot run.

When you run the server from the source, a key from an environment variable wins over the saved one and cannot be removed from the window. The installed app never reads keys from the environment.

A local model sends nothing over the network. TALOS knows three engines: its own, which it starts and stops itself, and two you may already have — Ollama and LM Studio.

For its own engine, TALOS says what the model runs on: the graphics card (by name), the processor, or a path you chose. Being reachable and having a model loaded are two different lines, on purpose. When the graphics card is not available, or its memory is too small for the model, TALOS says so and offers the processor — slower — without switching by itself. No model is recommended or forced: the engine’s settings come from the model file itself. See Run a model on your computer.

For a model that can think before answering, the pill next to the model in the composer sets how much: Auto, or one of the levels that model offers. Its tooltip names the Reasoning level that will actually run.

The same menu has Show reasoning. When it is off you only see how long the model thought — Thinking…, then Thought for and the time — and the text of the reasoning never opens. For a model whose reasoning cannot be adjusted there is no pill: Show reasoning is in the model panel instead.

Settings → Costs and usage counts what was really recorded: by day and by model, in tokens — input, output, and those read again from the cache. It shows no amount of money, by choice: the amount is on your provider’s statement, the only place where it is true. A usage that was not measured is a dash, never a zero, and the total of a session is the whole session, not its last message.

The usual suspects of a high usage are a long preamble and heavy attachments, which are paid at every following message.

pagine.descrizione: How much TALOS Desktop may do without asking — the four levels, what Full access still asks, the rule of each tool, Coordination, and where commands run.

sezioni.testo: Two gates decide whether TALOS acts on its own or stops to ask you: the permission of the session, and the rule of each tool. The tool’s rule wins over the session one.

It answers one question: how much may TALOS do here without asking? It applies to one session. The composer’s permission pill shows it and what passes without asking; click it to change it. A change made while the model works applies from its next tool call, and the model is told.

Permission | What it means | Risk
Read only | Reads the project and runs commands that change nothing. Every write is refused. | Low
Writes to the project | Writes on its own inside the session folder; to write outside it, it asks you. Commands and tests go through the gate. | Recommended
Asks first | Asks you to confirm before every action that leaves a trace: writes, commands, network. | Controlled
Full access | Files and network without the ordinary gates. Only if you already know what it is about to do. | Very high

The exact rules of each one are on Permissions in the reference. In Plan mode the pill reads Plan: read only.

sezioni.titolo: What asks at every level below Full access
sezioni.testo:
- Outside the project. Reading or listing anything outside the project folder asks first.
- Files with secrets. Reading a file that may hold keys or passwords, such as .env, asks — whatever spelling, link or wildcard leads to it — and writing one asks too. Search never returns their lines, names or counts.
- Network folders. A path on another computer (\\server\share) is never contacted without a yes.

Full access never asks for permission. Reading a secret file, writing after the model read suspicious content, and starting sub-agents all go ahead without a card. What still holds:

- A rule you set on a tool. An “Ask for confirmation” or “Always deny” you chose yourself still applies.
- Your computer’s login credentials. Reading a credential in your home folder (SSH keys, cloud and package-manager tokens) asks even in Full access, and those files (~/.ssh, .aws, .netrc, .npmrc…) are never written, at any level.
- The door to this computer. Turning remote control on, showing the pairing QR, and letting a device work in a folder always ask first, Full access too. See Use TALOS from your device.
- The floor. Commands that cannot be undone — deleting the root, formatting a disk, shutting down and the like — are refused at every level, also behind wrappers such as sudo -u, timeout or env.

In the permissions sheet, Per-tool permission gives five tools a gate of their own: writing a file (and changing part of one, which follows the same rule), running the project’s test suite, a shell command, generating a document, and generating an image. For each one: Same as the session, Always allowed, Ask for confirmation, or Always deny.

An “ask” on a tool turns on the approval channel for the whole session: while it stays on, TALOS also asks for the other actions that leave a trace. Files that steer TALOS itself — .claude/, the hooks and the other control files — are always confirmed one by one, even with “for this session”.

Capability in the sidebar lists every tool with the same four choices — Like the session, Always allow, Always ask, Deny — what it does to your computer, and how often the open session used it.

sezioni.titolo: Models without tools of their own
sezioni.testo:
Some local models cannot call tools. With them, TALOS reads the action the model writes in its answer and carries it out itself, and before each action it asks you with a card marked emulated.

- The card asks even with Full access. It offers Allow once, For this tool in this session and Deny.
- For this tool in this session applies to that tool only, for the rest of the conversation: its next actions do not ask again. Other tools still ask.
- Reading inside the project does not ask: listing, reading and searching files, notes, memory, tasks, research and conversations, the help pages and the state of goals, processes and workflows. Anything that goes on the web, or writes, still asks.
- A tool that already asks you on its own (a question, a plan, a deep research, and the tools that always ask) shows only its own card, not a second one.
- Writing outside the project, or to a file with secrets, shows only that card, and your yes counts for that action only.
- Rules, the session mode and the automatic check never answer this card: only a person does. If no screen can show it, the action is refused.
- In Read only, a tool that the level does not allow is refused at once, without a card.
- The first time a conversation shows this card, a note above it says why: “This model has no tools of its own: TALOS carries out its actions and asks you before each one.” It appears once per conversation, also after a reload.

sezioni.titolo: Coordination: agents started on their own
sezioni.testo: Coordination, in the same sheet, decides whether the model starts agents on its own in this conversation. It is off by default: the model asks you first, with a card. On, it starts them by itself, up to a cap per conversation. In a delegated agent, the main conversation decides. See Agents and automation.

Where commands run applies to the session: Automatic chooses by itself, and can change from one command to the next; Linux (WSL2) always runs in Linux, and says so when WSL is not there; Windows always runs on the home system, with the C: paths you see in File Explorer. With WSL, the model’s file tools run in the same Linux as its commands, and permissions still show the Windows path of the same file.

From two requests up, a bar above the composer lists the Pending requests, each with its full command or path. Allow all, with the number of requests next to it, answers “once” to each of the requests that can be read in full and are not shell commands; the others have See, which takes you to their card. Each yes still goes through its card, one at a time: if one does not go through, the bar stops and says how many are left. In Full access nothing asks, so the bar is not there.

sezioni.titolo: When you say no on a card

sezioni.testo:
- It is not a sandbox. The permission does not isolate the rest of your computer. In Linux, /mnt/c is your Windows disk.
- Closing writes does not close every way to write. A shell command, a document or an image can still leave a file on disk when the write tool is denied. To close that path, restrict the shell too.
Check, in this order: the session permission, then the rule of that tool.

pagine.descrizione: Conversations, notes, tasks, the Library, memory, deep research and projects — what TALOS Desktop keeps, and what each one is for.

sezioni.testo: A conversation ends; the work it produced stays. TALOS Desktop keeps it in a few places, each for one kind of thing, and the agent reads and writes them with the same tools you use from the sidebar.

Notes are documents for whoever reads them: what TALOS jotted down while working, and what you write. A note has no state and no assignee — that is what tasks are for. A note without a title takes its first line of text; a note without a date shows none.

Notes apply to all projects: the Notes section lists them and lets you write one even with no session open. Each note can be downloaded as a Markdown file.

The to-dos of the work, each with a state — to do, in progress, done — and a priority — low, normal, high. The summary at the top counts open and done tasks, and those whose state was not recorded, apart. Tasks have no due dates or reminders. A task is also what an automation starts again by itself.

Where the files made during the work end up — documents, images, artifacts — each with its name, when it was made and with which model. There is no bin: deleting a file deletes it for real, which is why it is the only action that asks for confirmation. The model reads a Library file only when it searches for it or opens it; its content never enters the context by itself. See Work with the Library.

A deep research produces a report, not a conversation: one question, many readings, and a document with its claims, steps, verdicts and sources. The report and its evidence are what you consult; the session is only how it was made. Its state says where it stands — running, paused, done, canceled, failed, without a report, blocked, turns exhausted — and only done means there is a report. See Run a deep research.

Projects groups sessions by project, not by folder: a project can live in several working folders. Each project shows its three most recent sessions and what it cost — turns and tokens — ordered by when you last worked on it. Sessions with no project still have a place. Projects are not created by hand: they come from the folders you work on.

pagine.descrizione: One task per page — from attaching a file to scheduling an automation — each checked against the TALOS Desktop release it names.

sezioni.testo: Each guide does one thing, in the order you would do it, and says what to do when it goes wrong. To understand how the parts fit together first, start with How TALOS Desktop works.

- Give a session a goal Type /goal, confirm the checks that prove it done, and let TALOS work turn after turn until they pass — or pause and say why.
- Undo the file changes of a turn Put the project's files back as they were before one of your messages — see the diff first, keep what you changed yourself, and redo if you change your mind.
- Use TALOS from your device (Remote Control) Pair your Android device with TALOS Desktop, confirm it on the computer, and drive the PC's sessions, approvals and models from the device.
- Attach files and images Add a project file, any file, an image or your last screenshot to a message, and see what it costs before you send.
- Retry or edit a message Ask again or change what you wrote without losing the answer you had — each try becomes a branch, and arrows move between them.
- Dictate and listen Speak a message into the composer, or have an answer read aloud — and what each one sends where.
- Improve a prompt Have what you wrote rewritten into a clearer brief before you send it, at the depth you choose.
