- Keep a long conversation in bounds See how full a chat is, let TALOS compact it without waiting, compact it by hand or with /compact, choose who writes the compaction and who stands in, and undo one.
- Make visuals, images and documents Ask for an interactive visual in the chat, an image saved to the project, or a real document file — and how an artifact keeps its versions.
- Run a deep research Turn one question into a report with claims, steps, verdicts and sources, and follow, pause, resume or check it again.
- Search the web and read pages Choose where the agent searches, check it, and follow every page it read — or open one yourself.
- Read files, documents and PDFs Open a file in the reader — text, Markdown, CSV, images, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HTML pages — and what the model gets when it reads an Office or PDF file.
- Use the terminal The real terminals of a session, the read-only tabs where you watch the agent's commands, and the Processes tab where you stop them.
- Review what a session changed See every file a session touched, line by line, with the turn that wrote it and its signed receipt.
- Connect a provider Give TALOS Desktop access to a model over the network — a key, a sign-in or your ChatGPT plan — test it, and choose which OpenRouter providers serve your requests.
- Run a model on your computer Load a model into TALOS Desktop's own engine, or use Ollama or LM Studio, open one from the chat, and choose what happens when its window fills up.
- Forge a tool Build a new tool for the agent from capabilities TALOS already has, without code, and turn it on when you are ready.
- Schedule an automation Have TALOS do something by itself on a schedule — create it from its page or ask any chat — and read what each run did.
- Add skills, MCP servers, plugins and hooks Extend TALOS Desktop from your project, read what each extension declares, and trust it only after.
- Work with the Library, notes

, tasks and memory Open, download, rename and delete the files of the work, and keep notes, tasks and memories by hand or through the agent.
- Check your setup with Doctor Read the report of what is ready and what is not on this computer, worst first, and what each check does not prove.
- Keyboard shortcuts The seven shortcuts of TALOS Desktop, where each one works, and the keys of the terminal's tabs.
- Find a setting The ten sections of TALOS Desktop's settings, the search across them, and moving your preferences to another computer.
- Change a setting from the chat Ask TALOS to change a setting, or type /settings, approve the card, and undo the change from the chat, from Settings or from the notifications.
- See what is waiting for you The bell in the left bar counts only what needs you; the panel has To do and All, marks entries as seen, and can notify you outside the window.
- Report a problem Open Report a problem from the TALOS menu or ask the model for a draft; read the diagnostics, and open the report on GitHub yourself.
- Ask on the side Ask a quick question about the conversation in the Aside tab without adding it to the chat, and turn it into a conversation if it is worth keeping.

pagine.descrizione: Ask for an interactive visual in the chat, an image saved to the project, or a real document file — and how an artifact keeps its versions.

sezioni.testo:
Three things the model can make instead of describing. There is no button for them: you ask in words — “make me a chart of…”, “generate an image of…”, “write me a PDF with…” — and the agent calls the tool.

You ask for | You get
A chart, a live table, a small interface | An artifact: a small interactive page shown in the chat, kept in the Library
An image | A real file saved in the project
A document | A real file — PDF, Word, spreadsheet, presentation — saved in the project

Ask for a change and the model updates the same artifact instead of making a new one; every version is kept in the Library. Each card says which version it shows — v2 of 3, or · latest. When a later turn updated it, the card says so, with Show latest and Back to v…. Open in a new tab opens it on its own.

An artifact has no access to your data: it is a page served apart, with security rules of its own.

A read-only session, and every workflow step, can still show an artifact but does not copy it into the Library. Its card then says Temporary preview: it may be unavailable after restart. If you will need it, ask for its content as a document, which is written to disk.

The tools behind these are governed in Capability, like every other: to stop TALOS from generating images, set that tool to deny. Keep in mind that generating an image and creating a document write to disk even when the write tool is denied — see Permissions.

- Preview unavailable — the card says why; check the entry in the Library.
- An image is not in the project — check that the generation finished; the file is written at the end.

pagine.descrizione: Ask a quick question about the conversation in the Aside tab without adding it to the chat, and turn it into a conversation if it is worth keeping.

sezioni.testo:
Sometimes you want to ask something about the conversation — what a term means, what the agent just did — without adding it to the chat. Open the Aside tab of the right panel.

- Write in Ask on the side… and choose Ask. The answer reads the conversation up to here and does not write to it. It is not saved.
- While the main chat is working, the question waits: Waiting for the turn.
- What the side question costs is added to the session’s count.
- When the side exchange is worth keeping, Turn into a conversation makes it a new conversation of its own. While a turn is running it can be turned into a conversation when the turn ends.

A very long answer stops with Answer stopped: it was too long. After many exchanges the first ones leave the thread; to keep everything, turn it into a conversation.

This is a gesture for you: to ask the model, just ask in the chat.

pagine.descrizione: Add a project file, any file, an image or your last screenshot to a message, and see what it costs before you send.

sezioni.testo: The + in the composer does one thing: it attaches something to a message. Pasting and dragging work too.

An attachment stays in the context of every message that follows, not only the one you attach it to. A long file is paid again and again.

- Up to 10 attachments per message.
- Up to 200,000 characters per attachment — about 50,000 tokens, half a window for one file.
- The estimate is an order of magnitude; the model counts the real number when it receives the message.

If an attachment is heavy, remove it or replace it with the part that matters.

sezioni.titolo: To share a document without attaching it

sezioni.testo:
- You cannot add another one — the message already has ten.
- The conversation suddenly costs more — look at what you attached: a large attachment stays in the context of the messages that follow.

pagine.descrizione: Have TALOS do something by itself on a schedule — create it from its page or ask any chat — and read what each run did.

sezioni.testo: An automation is an instruction TALOS carries out by itself, on a schedule: “every weekday at 9, summarize yesterday’s commits”. Each run starts fresh, without the conversation it came from, and cannot ask you questions.

From its page:

- Open Automations in the sidebar and create a New automation.
- Give it a Name, and write What it does as you would in a chat.
- Choose When: only when you run it, every hour, every day, weekdays, every week, every few minutes, once, or a custom schedule (5 fields).
- Choose the Folder — it works only inside it — and What it may do there.
- Choose Repeat: until you turn it off, once only, or a number of times. Create automation.

It is on as soon as you create it, and it uses the model shown in the form.

From any chat: ask for it, for example “every 6 hours, check the dependencies”. The model shows a card with the automation; choose Approve, Edit (the form opens, you save it, and the model is told) or Cancel. The card warns when the automation goes beyond this chat: more permissions, another folder, a folder never opened in TALOS, or Coordination on. Creating, changing, turning on or running an automation always asks you first; pausing and stopping do not. In Full access the card is not shown: the conversation says what it would have shown, so you can check it.

The list filters All, Active, Paused and To review. Select an automation to see when it runs, where and how, and its Runs: running, done, failed, skipped or stopped, with the reason when one was skipped or failed — for example, TALOS was closed at that time, or the provider was busy. A run with something to tell you shows up in To review.

Its ⋯ menu, also on right-click, holds Run now (or Stop the run while one is going), Edit, Pause or Turn on, Open the chat it came from and Delete. The model can create, change, run, pause and stop automations, but it has no way to delete one: only you do, from this page.

A run may move its own next run. A run that asks to change its own instructions does not change them: the proposal waits in To review, with the current and the proposed text, until you Approve or Discard it.
An automation made before this version repeats a task from the test catalog. It is marked Old format: it can only be turned on, paused or deleted. Create a new one to give it your own instructions.

pagine.descrizione: Ask again or change what you wrote without losing the answer you had — each try becomes a branch, and arrows move between them.

sezioni.testo: Retrying an answer or editing one of your messages never cuts the conversation. Each try starts a branch: the answers you had stay, one click away.

- Open the actions of an answer and choose Retry — “New branch · this answer stays”.
- TALOS asks the same question again, in a new branch that starts right before that turn.

While TALOS is still answering, the choice reads Stop and retry: the running turn stops first.

- Choose the pencil on one of your messages: Edit and resend.
- Change the text in place, then Send. It goes as a new branch; the answers below stay.

Images and attachments are sent again with the message: remove the ones you do not want. Attached files that cannot be sent again from there are named, so you can attach them again from the composer. While TALOS is still answering, the button reads Stop and send: sending stops the answer first, and what it already did stays in the other branch.

Where branches split, Previous version and Next version arrows go back and forth. Open the branch tree — also Branch tree in the chat’s top bar — shows them all, with the delegations started from this session.

To branch the whole conversation instead, use Fork this session: same folder, same history, a new conversation.

- This point is no longer in the conversation — it was summarized. Branch the whole conversation from the session menu instead.
- This message is not saved yet — wait for it to settle, then try again.
- The running turn did not stop, so no branch was opened — try again, or wait for it to finish.

pagine.descrizione: Turn one question into a report with claims, steps, verdicts and sources, and follow, pause, resume or check it again.

sezioni.testo: A deep research turns one question into a report: many readings, then a document with its claims, the steps taken, the verdicts and the sources. The report is the thing you consult; the session is how it was made.

- Open Deep research in the sidebar, or ask the agent in a conversation — it starts one with research_start.
- Follow it in the list: its state says where it stands.
- Open the report when it is done. Citations export to the standard bibliography formats.

Depending on its state, a research can be paused, resumed, checked again or deleted. An action appears only in the states where it can do something.

State | What it means | What to do
Running | It is searching and reading. | Wait, or pause it.
Paused | Stopped half way. | Resume it.
Done | There is a report — the only state that says so. | Read it.
Canceled | Stopped before the report; what it gathered stays in its sources. | Start it again if needed.
Failed | It stopped on an error. | Run it again.
Interrupted by the provider | The model’s service stopped half way, for a passing reason. Not an error of the research. | Resume it.
Without a report | It reached the end without depositing the document. | Run it again.
Blocked | The session was read-only and could not deliver. | Resume it with a permission that writes.
Turns exhausted | It used up its turns before concluding. | Narrow the question and run it again.

A state the app does not know reads “state not recorded” — never “done”.
The model’s last message is not the report. It appears only under how the research went, labeled for what it is, and never in the report’s panel.

pagine.descrizione: Speak a message into the composer, or have an answer read aloud — and what each one sends where.

sezioni.testo: Two different things, in opposite directions: dictating turns your voice into text in the composer; listening reads an answer of the assistant aloud.

- In the composer, press and hold the microphone.
- Speak. The text appears while you talk, so you know it is following you.
- Release. The text stays in the field: read it and correct it before you send.

Recognition is set to Italian in this release. The service may stop by itself after a long silence, even if you have not released; the indicator then stops saying it is listening.

Dictation is not offline. It uses the speech recognition of the browser engine, which sends the audio to an online service: it runs inside the window, not inside this computer. There is no wake word and no always-on listening, and a window that loses focus also loses the microphone.
A button on an answer of the assistant reads it aloud, with the voices installed in your operating system. Reading aloud is local.

Each error has its own sentence:

- Microphone permission denied — allow the microphone for TALOS in the system or browser settings.
- No speech detected — no audio arrived.
- The speech service cannot be reached — it is the network.
- No microphone found — there is no device.
- Voice not available — this browser engine does not offer speech recognition at all.

pagine.descrizione: Read the report of what is ready and what is not on this computer, worst first, and what each check does not prove.

sezioni.testo: Doctor is the report of the local setup: a list of checks, each with its severity — failure, warning, note, OK — ordered from the worst. Open Doctor — in the sidebar, or from Settings → Account, Doctor and backup — and read from the top. Checks run only when you ask.

Doctor is a diagnosis, not support: it says whether something is configured, not whether it would work. Each check says so in its own words — a key is configured but its validity with the provider is not checked; the browsing tool is available but no page is opened; search is configured but no search is run. A check missing from the answer is not taken as good: it reads not observed.

Doctor repairs nothing by itself. When an operation of the local API fails, its error carries a Doctor reference that opens the recorded detail (see Health and diagnostics).

- No environment available (failure) — commands cannot run, and most work cannot start.
- Restore of sessions in red — one or more sessions could not be read again. The list names which, and why.
- Everything “not observed” — the diagnosis did not arrive whole: try again.

pagine.titolo: Add skills, MCP servers, plugins and hooks
pagine.descrizione: Extend TALOS Desktop from your project, read what each extension declares, and trust it only after.

sezioni.titolo: Add skills, MCP servers, plugins and hooks
sezioni.testo:
A project can add four kinds of things to TALOS, each declared in a precise place of the project’s folder:

Kind | Adds | Declared in
Skill | Instructions the agent loads when needed | the .talos/skills/ folder
MCP server | Tools provided by an external program | the .talos/mcp.json file
Plugin | Tools and hooks together | the .talos/plugins/ folder
Hook | A command that runs at a precise moment | the .talos/hooks.json file

The older names — .harness-ui-skills/, .harness-ui-mcp.json, .harness-ui-plugins/, .harness-ui-hooks.json at the root of the project — are still read, after the ones above.

A hook runs before a tool is used, after it, at the start of a session, or at its end. Every file, with its format, is on Project files; hooks in full are on Hooks.

- Put the files in the project, in the places above.
- Open the inventory of extensions — Settings → Account, Doctor and backup lists Agents, Hooks, Skills, Plugins and MCP — and refresh it.
- Read what each one declares. For hooks, MCP servers and plugins, open the file in the project: the inventory of a hook says when it runs, not the command it will run, on purpose.
- Only then, mark it as trusted.

Being declared does not make an extension active: until you trust it, it waits for your trust. Skills are the exception — they are only instructions, and are available at once. A hook’s trust is recorded outside the project, with a fingerprint of its command: if the command changes, it must be trusted again. A project you clone cannot trust its own hooks.

For MCP servers, the inventory shows what is declared, not whether it answers.

Hooks and MCP servers are trusted together with the project scripts they run: if one of those scripts changes, the trust falls and the list says why. A file changed within two seconds of being read is hashed again before it is trusted, as git does. The same rule is shared with the TALOS CLI, so trust saved there stays valid. A program placed in the project folder — a node.cmd, say — cannot start in place of the real one.

- A server that does not start is said in the conversation, once, with the reason and where to fix it: Capability › Connectors, whose list shows the same reason. The Markdown export of the conversation carries the same note.
- A server can ask you. When it needs details — a form with text, numbers, yes/no and choices — or wants you to open a page, such as a sign-in or a payment, the chat shows a card that names the server. The page opens only when you click, and what you type in the form goes to the server without staying on screen.

- An extension does not appear — the file or folder is not in the right place, or not in the folder of the open session.
- Trust not observed — the state was not read: refresh the inventory.
- A hook does not run — check that it is trusted, and that its event is the one you think.
- A trusted MCP server or hook is no longer trusted — one of the scripts it runs changed: read what changed, then trust it again.

pagine.descrizione: Type /goal, confirm the checks that prove it done, and let TALOS work turn after turn until they pass — or pause and say why.

sezioni.testo: A goal is a result TALOS keeps working toward on its own, turn after turn, until checks that you confirmed prove it is reached. Use it for work with a clear finish line: “the test suite passes”, “the retry delay is capped at one minute”.

- In the composer, type /goal followed by what must be true, and send it. The model can also propose a goal when you ask for one.
- TALOS writes the checks that will prove it — a command that must succeed, a file that must be there — and shows them on a card: Confirm how TALOS will check the goal.
- Read them, then choose Start the goal. Nothing runs before you confirm.

- After every turn the checks run in the session’s folder. A check that fails three times pauses the goal instead of looping; a check that cannot be verified does not use up a try.
- “Done” has to be earned. A judge must point to a file that is there now, and a separate read-only reviewer tries to prove the goal is not complete. Refuted twice, the goal pauses and says why.
- The goal strip sits above the composer and folds to one line. It opens by itself only when the goal pauses or ends.

Goal paused comes with its reason: no progress, a check that cannot be verified, an error, or you stopped it. Only you can resume a paused goal. A conversation nobody is watching — an automation — never gets a goal.

pagine.descrizione: Have what you wrote rewritten into a clearer brief before you send it, at the depth you choose.

sezioni.testo: When you know what you want but wrote it in a hurry, TALOS can rewrite it into a clearer brief before it goes. You see the proposal next to your text and decide whether to keep it.

- Write the message as it comes.
- Open Improve the prompt from the composer.
- Choose the depth, and if you like the model that does it — it can differ from the conversation’s.
- Read the proposal next to the original; keep it or discard it.

Depth | What it does
Lean | Same length. Clarifies the goal and the expected result, adds no sections.
Balanced | A clear brief: goal, expected result, the constraints you already wrote, two or three checks. The default.
Extended | A full brief: scope, format of the answer, constraints, edge cases and acceptance criteria.

For a long piece of work, Extended pays off: acceptance criteria written first are what later tells you whether the work is done.

- It sends nothing by itself. Sending stays your gesture.
- It does not know what you want. It orders and completes what you wrote: a constraint you did not write is not invented. When your text is already right and only needs clarity, use Lean.
- It costs a call to the model. It is real work, not local formatting.

- The proposal is longer but not clearer — go down to Lean: rewriting a good text a lot makes it worse.
- Nothing arrives — like any call to the model, it needs a configured access. See Connect a provider.

pagine.titolo: Work with the Library, notes, tasks and memory
pagine.descrizione: Open, download, rename and delete the files of the work, and keep notes, tasks and memories by hand or through the agent.

sezioni.titolo: Work with the Library, notes, tasks and memory
sezioni.testo: What each of these is for is explained in Where work lives. Here is how to work with them. The agent does the same through its tools.

Open Library in the sidebar. Every file has six actions, gathered under one … button and the right-click menu: Open, Download, Rename, Show in folder, Copy path and Delete.

- Rename happens inside the row: Enter confirms, Esc cancels. A name with characters the system does not accept is refused at once.
- Copy path appears only when the path was recorded; older entries have five actions, not six.
- Delete asks for confirmation, and the confirmation states the consequence: deleted for good, with no way back. Focus goes to the way out, not to the button that deletes, so one Enter too many destroys nothing.

There is no bin: deleting removes the file for real. The other five actions ask nothing, because none of them breaks anything.

If a file is listed but does not open, it was moved or deleted outside TALOS: Show in folder says where it should be.

Open Notes in the sidebar to create, open, edit and delete notes — yours and the agent’s, with the same functions. Times are relative for 24 hours (“today 14:32”, “yesterday 09:10”), then become dates.

Open Tasks in the sidebar to create, open, edit and delete tasks, filter them by state and search their text. The agent creates and updates the same tasks while it works. A row whose state or author was not recorded says so.

Open Memory in the sidebar to create, open, edit and delete memories, search their text and filter them by kind. A memory without a kind says so, instead of being filed under one of the four. If a memory you expected is missing, it was never written: memory is not an automatic recording of the conversation.

pagine.titolo: Run a model on your computer
pagine.descrizione: Load a model into TALOS Desktop's own engine, or use Ollama or LM Studio, open one from the chat, and choose what happens when its window fills up.

sezioni.titolo: Run a model on your computer
sezioni.testo: A local model answers without sending anything over the network. TALOS has its own engine, which it starts and stops, and also works with Ollama and LM Studio if you already have them.

- Open Settings → Model Lab, then its Hugging Face tab: models to download, and those installed.
- See which models are on disk and which one is loaded in memory, each with its size in GB and whether it fits in the memory available.
- Load or unload a model from there.

No model is recommended or forced: you choose, and the engine’s settings are read from the model file itself. The Downloads tab follows every download, with its progress, pauses and recovery; the System tab describes this computer. The operations behind it are in Local models.

For its own engine, TALOS says in plain words what the model runs on: the graphics card, by name, or the processor, or a path you chose. Being reachable and having a model loaded are shown on two separate lines.

When the graphics card is not available, the model runs on the processor, and TALOS says so. When the card’s memory is too small for the model, TALOS does not decide by itself: it tells you, and offers the processor — slower — in the menu of the local engine.

- The context window is the real one. TALOS reads it from the engine — at least 64K when the machine can hold it — so long conversations are summarised at the right moment, not too late.
- Fewer tools up front. With a small window (16K or 32K) the model starts with only the essential tools; the others are one search away. The tool definitions shrink from about 6,400 to about 4,400 tokens.
- One request at a time. TALOS’s own engine serves one request at a time, so a summary prepared at the end of a turn gives way to your next message at once instead of making it wait.
- Compactions never block the chat. A quick compaction made without the model comes first; at the end of the turn the open model writes its own, which takes the quick one’s place. On a slow engine TALOS estimates first and does not ask for a compaction that would not finish in time; while a turn waits, one line shows the progress with Skip and Stop. See Long conversations.
- A sub-task can use it too: a delegated agent can run on the local engine, Ollama or LM Studio, not only on a provider.
- One model at a time. When a chat asks for a local model other than the one open, TALOS changes the model; if another conversation is still answering with the open one, it waits for it first.

Opening a model takes a moment, and one live row says what is happening, with the seconds: Opening ‹model›, Loading ‹model›, Loading the part for images, Waking ‹model›, Freeing the graphics card, Waiting for the other conversation to finish, Reopening ‹model› with more room, or Trying again with the other engine. Stop works during the first load too: the turn then says it stopped while the model was still loading.

sezioni.titolo: Open or free a model from the chat
sezioni.testo: Besides the Model Lab, you can ask in the chat: “which local models do I have?”, “open Qwen”, “close the local model and free the memory”. TALOS lists the models downloaded on this computer, with their size, whether each one fits in memory and which one is open. Opening or closing one goes through a card you approve, except in Full access. A model that is still answering in another conversation is not closed. This does not change the model of the conversation: to change that, ask TALOS to change the setting, or use the model picker.

sezioni.titolo: When a local model’s window fills up
sezioni.testo:
By default, when a conversation outgrows the local model’s window, TALOS enlarges the window: the engine reopens the model with more room and the conversation goes on whole. A row says Window enlarged to ‹size› to fit the conversation; Details says by how much, and about how much more memory it uses. The choice is remembered for that model.

To change what happens, open Settings → Model Lab, card When a local model’s window fills up:

- Enlarge the window — keeps the whole conversation and uses more memory. If it cannot, it compacts.
- Compact — uses no extra memory; older details are condensed.
- Ask me — pauses with a card offering Enlarge the window, Compact and Choose another model.

TALOS never stops the conversation for this unless nothing can fit it. When the model knows in advance that it will need more — several large files to compare — it can ask to enlarge the window itself, on a card you approve.

With local models TALOS saves on disk where each conversation got to: when you come back, the model picks up from there and answers sooner, without reading it all again. Set the space in Settings → Model Lab → Conversation memory, Disk space (GB) — 8 GB by default. When the space runs out, the least recently used memory is deleted, never the conversation. 0 turns it off: the model then reads a conversation again from the start, and the first answer comes later. If a model answers slower with it, or cannot use it, TALOS turns it off for that model only and says so.

A long local job should not stop because the PC went to sleep. In Settings → Agent tools and permissions → Keep the PC awake, choose Never, While TALOS works (the default) or Always. The screen still turns off as usual. This works only in the installed app.

- The graphics card is not available: the model runs on the processor — a warning, not an error. It works, more slowly.
- The graphics card’s memory is not enough — choose the processor in the menu of the local engine, or a smaller model.
- “LM Studio is not running on this computer” — the model picker says this, instead of an empty list, when TALOS cannot reach LM Studio or Ollama. Start it, then open the picker again: its models appear.
- “The graphics card is slower than usual” — the row gives the tokens per second now and the best seen on this PC. Restarting the PC usually brings it back to full speed.
- “The window could not be enlarged” — compact the older part, or choose a model that reads more.
- The engine did not start — Doctor and the engine’s tab show the last error read.
- Generation ends at once — it happens with local models: a chat model served without its conversation format, a window already full, or a sampling that stops at the first token.

pagine.titolo: Keep a long conversation in bounds
pagine.descrizione: See how full a chat is, let TALOS compact it without waiting, compact it by hand or with /compact, choose who writes the compaction and who stands in, and undo one.

sezioni.titolo: Keep a long conversation in bounds
sezioni.testo:
A long conversation eventually fills the model’s window. TALOS keeps it in bounds by compacting it: the past is condensed, the conversation goes on, and every message stays in the archive. Why it matters is explained in What the model reads.

Everywhere on screen the gesture has one name: Compaction.

- The Context tab of the right panel says how much of the limit is used (“62% of the limit used”, or Over the compaction limit), how many tokens are left before compaction starts by itself, and What fills the window. When it is almost full it says The window is almost full, with Compact now. When tools weigh a lot, it suggests turning off the MCP servers you do not use, with Manage MCP servers. A count that is an estimate is marked “~”.
- The same tab lists the Compactions of this conversation: for each one, the turn it happened at, the tokens it freed, who wrote it — by the model, by the backup, or quick, without the model — and what it cost: “12,400 tokens spent”, no cost, or spent, not measured. Over time draws the window send by send; the dashes mark where a compaction freed space.
- When the provider’s prompt cache started over, the tab says when and why — the model changed, the tool list changed, the instructions changed, the conversation was compacted, or it expired after a pause — and about how many tokens were read again without the cache discount.
- Context Manager, in the chat’s top bar, opens the same measure in a window, with an Overview page and a Compact now… button.

New conversations use the context engine: first it sets old tool output aside, and only if that is not enough it compacts the past. Your own requests are kept word for word. The Context tab says which limit applies, and why.

- To change this for new conversations, open Settings → Memory and context → Context engine and switch off Use it for new conversations. New conversations then use the simple compaction, which compacts above 75% of the model’s window. Conversations already started keep the one they began with.

When a long conversation needs compacting, the chat does not wait: a quick compaction made without the model starts right away, and the model’s compaction replaces it as soon as it is ready. The row in the chat says which one you have:

- Quick compaction without the model — the model’s one is on its way and takes this one’s place at your next message. Nothing to do.
- Compaction improved by the model — the model’s compaction has replaced the quick one.

When a turn does have to wait, one line shows Compacting the context with its progress and an estimated time, and two buttons:

- Skip — go on with a compaction made without the model;
- Stop — stop the run.

The wait has a time ceiling. When the compaction is made without the model — because you skipped it, it took too long, the model’s one did not pass the check, or it failed several times in a row — TALOS says so, and why.

Three ways, the same result:

- Type /compact in the composer and send it. It compacts at once: nothing is sent to the model as a message. With a file attached it stays an ordinary message.
- In the Context tab, choose Compact now and confirm Compact the conversation now? The older turns become a compacted version; the last requests stay word for word.
- Open Context Manager from the chat’s top bar, choose Compact now…, and confirm.

When it does not compact, it says why: Nothing to compact yet, or This compaction freed no space. The conversation stays as it was.

sezioni.titolo: Choose who writes the compaction, and who stands in
sezioni.testo:
For all chats, open Settings → Memory and context. The card Conversation compaction always shows the chain in one sentence: “Now: ‹model›, then ‹backup› if it does not answer, then a quick compaction without a model.” Open Advanced to change it:

- Compaction model — writes the compactions of long conversations. Same as the conversation reuses that conversation’s cache, so it costs less.
- If it does not answer — the backup, used only when the compaction model is blocked or does not answer: None: quick compaction without the model, The conversation’s model, or a model you choose. It is never chosen for you.

When the chosen model cannot be used — a plan or provider limit until a given time, no network, no key, the provider not set up, no access with your account — the card says so in plain words and offers Choose another. The Settings page of Context Manager shows the same sentence under For all chats, with Change the model and Choose a backup.

For one chat only, open Context Manager → Settings. Under For this chat, Manage automatically is on by default. Advanced holds Compaction model (Follow the chat model, or Choose a model with its Provider and Model), Start automatically at (%), Target after compaction (%) — it must be below the start, or the settings are not saved — Recent exchanges to keep and Compaction instructions. Then Save settings.

A conversation started with the simple compaction shows a simpler Context Manager: you can compact it by hand, but facts to keep, versions and these settings are only in conversations that use the context engine.

In the Not to be forgotten page, Add a fact that must survive the compaction, and Save fact. These facts stay separate from the compaction; you can edit and remove them. When TALOS proposes to change one, the proposal waits for you: Accept proposal, or Keep the fact.

sezioni.titolo: Undo a compaction, or go back to an earlier one
sezioni.testo:
- Each compaction leaves a row in the chat. With the context engine it reads Context compacted, and View context opens Context Manager. With the simple compaction it reads Conversation compacted, with the tokens saved, and its ⋯ menu can Show what was compacted and Undo the compaction: the whole conversation goes back to the model.
- Versions and sources lists the saved compactions. Restore an earlier one and confirm; the messages after it stay in the chat.

If compactions stop making the conversation shorter, TALOS pauses the automatic ones and says so once, in a row: Automatic compactions paused — the last ones did not make the conversation shorter; /compact still runs one.

- Your message alone is too large — TALOS says how many tokens it needs out of the model’s window, and that nothing was compacted. Send as attachment puts the text in a file and attaches it.
- Conversation not compacted · no model available — neither the compaction model nor the backup could do it: the conversation stays whole. Check the card in Settings → Memory and context.
- Compaction by ‹model› (backup) — the compaction model was not available, so the backup wrote it. The row says why.
- Automatic compaction failed — the row says how many times in a row, and when the next automatic try is.
- The context changed — someone, or the model, changed it while you were editing. The data is refreshed: review and repeat your change.
- Measurement not available yet — it says so instead of showing a zero.

pagine.titolo: See what is waiting for you
pagine.descrizione: The bell in the left bar counts only what needs you; the panel has To do and All, marks entries as seen, and can notify you outside the window.

sezioni.titolo: See what is waiting for you
sezioni.testo: Every session, automation and change that needs you ends up in one place: the bell at the top of the left bar, next to TALOS. It works for the sessions you are not looking at, too.

The number on the bell counts only what is waiting for you: a permission to decide, or a question to answer. Its label says it — Notifications: none, Notifications: 1 thing is waiting for you, or “Notifications: 3 things are waiting for you”. Finished turns, automation results and what you did yourself are not counted: they are in All.

Choose the bell. The panel always opens on To do, and its title says Waiting for you when something is.

- To do — what still needs you, the thing first: the name of the session or file, then what it wants (“Has a question:”, “It wants to create this document:”, or the sentence of its permission card), then the time. Choose a row to go to it. When nothing waits, it says Nothing to do and shows the Latest three entries.
- All — everything, newest first, grouped by Today, Yesterday and earlier days, with Show more past the first fifty. Your own answers are there in a lighter row: You allowed:, You denied:, You answered:, You skipped:, You changed:. A text longer than two lines has More next to it.
- Mark all as seen — only in All. Seen does not mean decided: a request still waits in To do until you answer it.

A change of settings made by the model, or from a paired device, also arrives here: see Change a setting from the chat.

At the bottom of the panel, Notify me outside the window too asks the system for permission. Once it is on, TALOS notifies you when it is hidden, and for what is waiting for you even while you look at something else. If it reads Blocked in the browser settings, turn it back on there, not in TALOS.
There is nothing to ask the model here: notifications are what TALOS writes when a session, an automation or a change needs you. Answer a request from its card in the chat, or from the panel.

pagine.descrizione: Give TALOS Desktop access to a model over the network — a key, a sign-in or your ChatGPT plan — test it, and choose which OpenRouter providers serve your requests.

sezioni.testo: Without at least one access, sessions cannot run. Connecting a provider is the first thing to do: on a first start the Home says No provider is set up and offers Set up a provider. What a provider is, and where keys are kept, is explained in Models and providers.

- Open Settings → Model Lab, then its Provider tab — or choose Set up a provider on the Home.
- Pick the provider and choose Configure. All the providers TALOS knows, with their protocol and address, are on Providers.
- Paste the key, or sign in where the provider offers it: the provider’s site opens, your password does not pass through TALOS, and a key comes back at the end.
- If the provider needs it, set the address of the service. Save.
- Test connection.

The test answers in precise words: the credential was accepted, or rejected (with its HTTP status); the catalog was reached, with how many models it shows; the service could not be reached; or the address is missing. A saved key is not a working key until the test says so. Where a provider has no model list to test against, the test says so instead of judging the key.

Keys go to the operating system’s keyring. If Doctor reports that the keyring is not available, keys cannot be saved until it is.

With a ChatGPT Plus or Pro account, TALOS can use the models of your plan instead of an API key.

- Open Provider, then OpenAI → Configure.
- Choose Continue with ChatGPT. chatgpt.com opens in your browser to sign in; your password never passes through TALOS.
- Back in TALOS, the models of your plan appear in the model picker. Requests to them are paid by your subscription.

While a plan model is in use, a ChatGPT plan pill sits in the composer. Click it to see who is signed in, the requests TALOS counted in the last 5 hours and 7 days (use from ChatGPT or other apps is not included), and Manage usage, which opens your ChatGPT usage settings. At the plan’s usage limit the turn waits and tries again with your plan. Disconnect ChatGPT is in the same dialog.

sezioni.titolo: Z.AI: say where your key goes
sezioni.testo: Before saving a Z.AI key, answer How you pay Z.AI — GLM Coding Plan or Pay-as-you-go balance — and Where — International or China. The key goes only to the address you chose; TALOS does not try the others. A Z.AI chat without a choice stops before sending anything.

sezioni.titolo: Choose which OpenRouter providers serve you
sezioni.testo:
On OpenRouter one model can be served by several providers, and an answer says which one served it (“via …”).

- Exclude one from the answer’s ⋯ menu (Exclude … on OpenRouter), or add its short name — like deepinfra — to Excluded providers in OpenRouter’s settings. OpenRouter skips it from the next request.
- Excluded by default lists the providers TALOS skips for a model because they do not work with it, for example because they do not call tools. You can allow one again, and Exclude again puts it back.
- The model can list, exclude and allow OpenRouter providers too, from the chat, after you confirm a card.
The model of a conversation is chosen from the pill in the composer. Providers without an access are not offered. A model in the catalog exists; it is not necessarily covered by your access.

- Credential not accepted — the key is not valid for that service.
- Could not reach — it is the network or the address, not the key.
- Choose where the key goes first, in Configure — a Z.AI key without its address.
- The ChatGPT sign-in has expired — sign in again with Continue with ChatGPT.
- The usage limit of your ChatGPT plan was reached — check ChatGPT Settings → Usage.

pagine.descrizione: Open a file in the reader — text, Markdown, CSV, images, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HTML pages — and what the model gets when it reads an Office or PDF file.

sezioni.testo: A file opens in the reader: in the right column of a session, full screen, or from the Library. TALOS tells the kind of a file from its name and from its bytes, so a file whose name promises one format and holds another is said to be broken instead of shown wrong.

Kind | How it opens
Text and code | As text
Markdown | Preview or Text
CSV table | As a table; a long one shows its first rows, then Show all … rows
Image | With Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit to window
PDF | In the PDF reader built into the app
Word document, Spreadsheet, Presentation | Drawn inside TALOS, no Office needed
HTML page | Preview or Text — see below

The ⋯ menu of the reader has Copy the text and Open with the system app; Full screen and Close the reader are next to it. A format the reader does not draw says so — “This format is not shown here: it opens with the system app.”
An HTML page runs its own scripts in the Preview, but it cannot reach the network: it can draw itself, not send or fetch anything. Its source is one click away, in Text.

- A long text shows its beginning and says how much: “Showing the first … characters of …”.
- Above a size limit the preview stops, so the window does not slow down; Show anyway opens it all the same.
- A file with macros shows only its content: “the macros are not run.”

- “This Word document does not open here” (or spreadsheet, presentation) — the file is broken, or is not in the format its name promises. Open with the system app tries your own program.
- The model says a PDF has missing pages — they are probably scans. Its text holds only the pages that have text.

pagine.titolo: Use TALOS from your device (Remote Control)
pagine.descrizione: Pair your Android device with TALOS Desktop, confirm it on the computer, and drive the PC's sessions, approvals and models from the device.

sezioni.titolo: Use TALOS from your device (Remote Control)
sezioni.testo: With Remote Control, TALOS for Android uses TALOS on your PC: the PC’s sessions in Code, the PC’s models in the picker, approvals and questions answered from the device, and a notification when a session waits for you. The work still runs on the computer; the device is a window on it.

- On the PC, open Connected devices — the device icon in the header (it shows a dot when a device is online), or Settings › Connected devices.
- The first time, choose How does the device reach this computer away from home?: Free servers by n0 (works right away, with a traffic limit) or My own server (run talos-relay on a server of yours and paste its address). Then Continue. The connection is end-to-end encrypted, and direct at home when possible.
- The Connect your device window shows a QR code that works once and expires in a few minutes.
- On the device, open Computer, tap Connect a computer and scan the code.
- The PC asks Connect this device? and shows a 6-digit number. If the device shows the same number, it is yours: choose Connect. Device connected confirms it.

The paired device can do on this computer whatever you do, Full access included. The code alone connects nothing: you always confirm on the computer.

Settings › Connected devices lists each device, online or offline, with its connection (direct, N ms or via server, N ms) or when it was last seen. Revoke disconnects one at once; Connect another device pairs the next. Up to 16 devices; after too many wrong attempts, pairing pauses for 15 minutes.

You can also ask TALOS in the chat to list the paired devices, show the pairing code (a Connect a device card that asks you first, even in Full access) or revoke one (a confirmation card). The model never sees the code.

- Sessions. The PC’s sessions appear in Code on the device; start a new one on the PC in a folder it is allowed to use (see below).
- Approvals and questions. Permission cards and the model’s questions are answered from the device. A request made from the device reaches the PC at once.
- Models. The device’s model picker shows the PC’s models.
- Files and images. The device can attach files and images to a conversation on this PC. A transfer pauses when the connection drops and resumes where it stopped.
- Notifications. A device that is not connected is woken when a run fails or a session waits for you (never for a sub-agent).

sezioni.titolo: Folders the device can work in
sezioni.testo:
A device works only in folders of this PC that you allowed. It asks once for a folder, and you allow it from a card: Which folder can … work in?, then Allow this folder. From the device it can then read, write and run commands there, until you revoke it.

Settings › Connected devices shows each device’s Allowed folders: Add folder allows one in advance, and Revoke takes one back. The model can list, allow and revoke folders too, always behind a card — allowing one always asks, Full access too.

sezioni.titolo: Send a file to the device
sezioni.testo: A file in the conversation has Send to … (the device’s name) in its ⋯ menu and on right-click; with more than one device, Send to device… lets you choose. The model can send one too, with a card you confirm (no card in Full access). Under the file, a line says whether it was sent, is downloading, was downloaded, or changed on the PC before the download. A device that is offline gets the file when it connects again. Files up to 25 MB.

sezioni.titolo: Turn remote control on or off from the chat
sezioni.testo:
Ask TALOS in the chat. Turning it on shows a Turn on remote control card — asked every time, also in Full access — and can show the pairing QR in the chat. Turning it off shows Turn off remote control: connected devices will not reach this computer until you turn it on again, and they stay paired.

The device side is described in Remote Control on Android.

pagine.descrizione: Open Report a problem from the TALOS menu or ask the model for a draft; read the diagnostics, and open the report on GitHub yourself.

sezioni.testo: When something does not work, a model answers wrong, or you have an idea, TALOS prepares the report for you. Nothing is sent by itself: you read it, and you open it on GitHub with your own account.

Open the menu from ⋯ in the title bar and choose Report a problem…. The window Report a problem opens with the diagnostics already read.

- What do you want to report: Something does not work, Wrong answer from the model, or An idea.
- Write a Title, and What happened, and what you expected.
- Attach the diagnostics (you can read all of it below) is on: the version of TALOS and the system, the model and provider, the access level, the last errors, and whether the local engine and remote control are on. Turn it off to send without them.
- Choose Open on GitHub. The browser opens the report already filled in; you send it from there.

The diagnostics never hold your folder paths, your messages or your keys. The report on GitHub is public: if the text looks like a key or a folder path, the window warns you before you open it. If the text is too long for the address, it says so: Copy the text copies all of it, to paste on GitHub.

Ask the model — “report this as a bug”, “send the TALOS team this idea”. It writes only a Draft report in the chat, with its kind and title, and the buttons Review and open and Discard. Review and open opens the same window, marked Prepared by the model in the chat: read it before opening it. The model prepares a draft only when you ask for one, and writes only what happened in this conversation.

pagine.descrizione: See every file a session touched, line by line, with the turn that wrote it and its signed receipt.

sezioni.testo: Review shows what the session changed: the list of files it touched and, for each one, the comparison line by line between before and after.

- Open Review from the session.
- Go through the list of files. Each says in which turn it was written, whether it is a new file, and — when there is one — the signed receipt of that write.
- Select a file to see its comparison.

A receipt appears only when that change carries one: none is invented to fill the space.

Review shows; it does not decide. Accepting or discarding a single file, and opening it in an editor, are not there yet: they stay hidden until they work, rather than being buttons that do nothing. The changes are on disk: the review is for looking at them. The Git actions of a session’s folder are in the Git tab of the session details column, next to Context, Files, Agents and Processes; their operations are listed in Git and GitHub.
- A file you expect is missing — either it was not touched, or it was written by a path that does not go through the review, such as a command in the terminal.

pagine.titolo: Change a setting from the chat
pagine.descrizione: Ask TALOS to change a setting, or type /settings, approve the card, and undo the change from the chat, from Settings or from the notifications.

sezioni.titolo: Change a setting from the chat
sezioni.testo: You do not have to find a setting to change it. Ask in the chat — “switch to the dark theme”, “use a cheaper model for this conversation”, “turn off the animated background” — or type the change yourself with /settings. Every change can be undone, and TALOS remembers who made it.

- Write what you want in your own words.
- TALOS shows a card, Change settings: each setting with its value before and after, whether it applies to this app or to this conversation, and, when a model changes, the Price per million from the old value to the new one. The model adds one line that says why, in your words.
- Choose Apply, Not now, or Open in Settings to do it yourself.

What it can change includes the TALOS theme, Color mode, Menu language, Reply and dictation language, Animated background, the conversation’s Model, Reasoning level and Fast mode, the Execution permissions, the Compaction model, and When a local model’s window fills up. Several settings can change together: all of them, or none. The model changes settings only when you ask for it in your own message, never because a file, a web page or a note told it to.

### With Full access

In Full access the change is made without a card — except for the settings that touch security (the permissions, Coordination, the Linux user) and the updates: for those the card always shows, and says This card shows up even with Full access. under Touches security, with one sentence on what changes. If the model’s reason looks like it is pushing you to approve without reading, the card says so in a warning box, The model’s reason looks suspicious, quoting it.

Type /settings in the composer: a list suggests the settings and, for one setting, its allowed values. Write /settings key=value and send it. The change applies at once, and a note in the chat says You changed 1 setting, with Undo. A value that is not allowed is said in the list, with the values that are. A value that is already set reads Already set.

- In the chat, the row of the change — Changed 1 setting — has Undo in plain sight. After it, the row says Undone: the setting is back as it was.
- In Settings, under a value TALOS changed, a mark says Changed by TALOS at ‹time›, with Undo. It comes from the record TALOS keeps, so it is still there after a restart.
- A change made by the model, or from a paired device, also reaches the notifications of this PC: Changed 1 setting:, or Changed from your device:.
Secrets, accounts, trust and destructive actions are not settings here: keys, sign-ins, and deleting data stay in their own screens. Sub-agents and automations never change settings.

- Not undone: ‹setting› was changed afterwards. — someone changed it again in the meantime; change it by hand.
- No setting is called “‹key›”. — check the name in the list that /settings shows.
- “‹value›” is not valid for ‹setting›. — the message lists the allowed values.

pagine.descrizione: The ten sections of TALOS Desktop's settings, the search across them, and moving your preferences to another computer.

sezioni.testo: Open the settings from the sidebar, or with Mod ,. A search at the top goes through every section: search by word, accents or not. Every setting, with its values and what it changes, is listed on Settings in the reference.

Behavior — how the app behaves with you:

- Appearance and motion — theme, colors, how much animation, the language of the menus.
- Chat and composer — how you read and write. Model and permissions belong to each session.
- Agent tools and permissions — what the agent may do, and the source of web search.
- Memory and context — how the model’s window is shared, the limits available, and the Context engine switch for new conversations; see Keep a long conversation in bounds.
- Security and privacy — local data, and moving your preferences.
- Connected devices — the devices that can control TALOS on this computer; see Use TALOS from your device.

Infrastructure — what it works with:

- Model Lab — providers and their keys, models on this computer, downloads; see Connect a provider and Run a model on your computer.
- Costs and usage — usage by day and by model; see Models and providers.
- Files and workspace — the active folder and session.
- Account, Doctor and backup — automatic Updates, the inventory of agents, hooks, skills, plugins and MCP servers, and Doctor.

Settings stay on this computer: nothing is synced and nothing is sent. To take them elsewhere, open Security and privacy, export them to a file, and import it on the other computer; you can also restore the initial values. These actions move preferences, not conversations.

sezioni.titolo: If a setting has no effect
sezioni.testo: Some settings apply from the next session. Open a new one to check.

pagine.descrizione: The seven shortcuts of TALOS Desktop, where each one works, and the keys of the terminal's tabs.

sezioni.testo:
There are seven, and all of them work. Mod is Ctrl on Windows and Linux and ⌘ on a Mac: the labels in the app follow your computer by themselves.

Keys | Where | Does
Mod K | Anywhere | Open the commands
Mod N | Anywhere | New session
Mod , | Anywhere | Open the settings
Mod / | Anywhere | Show the shortcuts
Mod ⇧ M | In a chat | Change the model
Mod ` | In a session | Show or hide the terminal
Mod ⇧ ` | In a session | New terminal tab

Mod / opens the full list inside the app, the copy that never gets old. Shortcuts cannot be customized.
Inside the list of tabs of the terminal: arrows move, Home and End go to the ends, Delete closes, F2 renames.

Check that you are in the right place: three of the seven work only inside a chat or a session. A shortcut written in the app is a promise — if one is shown and does nothing, or shows a key your keyboard does not have, it is a fault worth reporting.

pagine.descrizione: The real terminals of a session, the read-only tabs where you watch the agent's commands, and the Processes tab where you stop them.

sezioni.testo: The terminal of a session is a real terminal, not a transcript of one. Every tab says who opened it and where it runs.

- Ctrl ` shows or hides the terminal; Ctrl ⇧ ` opens a new tab.
- Click a tab to select it; middle-click, or Ctrl and click, to close it. Its menu has Close, Close others, Close all and Rename.
- In the list of tabs: arrows move, Home and End go to the ends, Delete closes, F2 renames.
- Right-click inside a tab for Copy, Paste, Select all and Clear the screen.

A session keeps at most eight tabs. What you type right after opening a tab is kept and sent as soon as the shell is ready.

Each turn of the agent gets a read-only tab, agent · turn N, with its commands one under the other: the command, its output and how it ended. The tab appears without taking the one you are using. It can be closed but not renamed, and it is rebuilt when you reopen the session.

sezioni.titolo: Stop a command: the Processes tab
sezioni.testo:
Processes, in the session’s details column on the right, lists the commands run in this session — by the agent (agent · turn N) or by you — with their state, duration, exit, and the CPU and memory of each running one.

- Stop this command ends one. The model is told you stopped it, and the row says Cancelled, not that it failed. A command waiting for your consent says so.
- Send to background lets a long command keep running while the turn goes on. It shows under In the background; when it ends, the model is told and the conversation resumes by itself.
- Stop all stops every running command, background ones included; the agent keeps working and knows you stopped them. Remove from the list clears a finished one.

A command that prints nothing for a while is not stopped by TALOS: the row says it may be waiting for input. Commands that outlived a crash of the server are adopted again and can still be stopped; nothing is ever killed automatically.

- It is not isolated from the rest of your computer. See Permissions.
- A command can write files even when the write tool is denied. To close that path, restrict the shell too.

- You already have 8 tabs open: close one — a session keeps at most eight.
- The session’s folder no longer exists — the terminal says why instead of bringing the server down.

pagine.descrizione: Build a new tool for the agent from capabilities TALOS already has, without code, and turn it on when you are ready.

sezioni.testo: The Tool Forge is where a new tool for the agent is built without writing code: it puts together capabilities TALOS already has, and decides what happens under which conditions. The agent can propose one with tool_create; you decide whether it runs.

There are eight, and a forged tool can use only these:

Capability | Does | Risk
List tasks | Reads | R1
Create a task | Writes | R2
Change a task | Writes | R2
List notes | Reads | R1
Write a note | Writes | R2
Change a note | Writes | R2
Search memory | Reads | R2
Write to memory | Writes | R3

A forged tool carries the risk of its riskiest capability. Searching memory only reads, yet it is R2: memory is read again by the model in every future conversation, so reading it is not as harmless as reading a note. A forged tool has no access to the disk, the network or the terminal.

- Open Tool Forge in the sidebar.
- Select a tool to see its detail: capabilities, risk and when it was installed.
- Enable or disable it from the detail.

An enabled tool joins the agent’s tools and follows the rules of each tool like every other.

- A forged tool is never used — check that it is enabled, and that its rule is not set to deny.
- Unrecognized capability — the tool declares a capability this version does not know.
- No description, or no state — the row says so instead of guessing.

pagine.titolo: Undo the file changes of a turn
pagine.descrizione: Put the project's files back as they were before one of your messages — see the diff first, keep what you changed yourself, and redo if you change your mind.

sezioni.titolo: Undo the file changes of a turn
sezioni.testo: TALOS can put the folder back as it was before one of your messages. Everything after that message is undone too.

- Hover one of your messages, open its menu (More actions on your message) and choose Undo file changes from here.
- The Undo file changes window lists the files under Put back as they were, each with its state (Modified, Created by TALOS, Deleted by TALOS). Select one to see Changes that will be undone in it.
- Choose Undo changes to 1 file (or N files). A notice confirms what was put back, with Redo.

- A file you changed after TALOS, or one a command changed, is listed under Left as they are. Choose Include to put it back anyway.
- Files outside the session’s folder, and files over 10 MB, are not covered; the window says which.
- TALOS keeps a copy of how things are now, so Redo brings them back — except files you changed afterwards.

The model can propose an undo with a card in the chat: Undo file changes? with the diff of each file. Choose Undo changes or Keep as it is: you decide. A paired device can undo too (see Remote Control).

The window says why: Git must be installed on this computer (2.25 or newer), the folder is a whole disk or your user folder, the folder has more than 50,000 files, or the copy from that moment is not there.

pagine.titolo: Search the web and read pages
pagine.descrizione: Choose where the agent searches, check it, and follow every page it read — or open one yourself.

sezioni.titolo: Search the web and read pages
sezioni.testo: The agent can search the web and read a page with its web search and browsing tools. It decides when to use them, under the rule of each tool; you choose where it searches.

The Browser of a session gathers the web pages of that session:

- The agent’s readings — each page the agent read, showing the text the model actually received, with its address, time and length;
- Pages you open — type an address and the page opens inside TALOS, when the site allows it.

There are back and forward, reload, an editable address (Enter confirms, Esc cancels), copy the address, and Annotate, which prepares a comment about the page in the composer without sending it. You annotate the page, not one element inside a live page.

sezioni.titolo: Open a link from a chat
sezioni.testo:
Links in a chat are clickable, but TALOS asks first: Open this link? shows where the link goes, the whole site name, before anything opens.

- Open in TALOS opens it in the session’s Browser; Open in browser opens it in your own browser; Copy link copies it.
- Open links to … without asking remembers that site, and also where you opened it: in TALOS or in your browser.
- Don’t ask me where to open links again makes your last choice the rule for every other site.
- Key and account pages always open in your own browser, whatever you chose.
- An address that is not encrypted (http) is not opened: copy it and open it yourself if you trust it.

The sites that open without asking are listed in Settings → Links from chat, with Ask again next to each one and the choice of Where links open: Ask every time, In TALOS or In your browser.

- The search was refused — almost always DuckDuckGo’s traffic limit. Try later, or set up a source with a key.
- The agent never searches — check the rule of the search tool in Capability: it may be set to deny.
- A site will not open inside TALOS — that is the site’s choice. TALOS says why, and offers to have the agent read it instead.
- A reading is shorter than expected — the length shown is that of the text the model received: if it is short, the model saw little.

Doctor says whether search is configured; it never runs a search to check.

pagine.descrizione: What it needs, which file to take, how to check it, what you see the first time, and how it updates itself.

sezioni.testo:
- Windows 10 1809 or later, x64, or Windows 11 x64. Not yet tested on Windows 10.
- No Node.js installation and no administrator rights: the app includes what it needs.
- For GPU acceleration, a Vulkan-capable driver. Without one, TALOS runs models on the CPU.

The installer is a per-user setup with a welcome page and the licence (AGPL-3.0, with Next: it grants rights, it is not an agreement to accept). It installs under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\TALOS, adds a “TALOS” shortcut, and offers to start the app. It never asks for administrator rights and has no folder chooser. It speaks English, or Italian on an Italian Windows.

TALOS-Setup-0.1.38.exe · 217 MB · TALOS Desktop 0.1.38 SHA-25666823d382810f0b61c036e045bf73089d6791381decc285e46d8ca3793a44ed9

The ZIP holds the same app. Extract it completely into a writable folder and start TALOS.exe, keeping resources and the DLLs next to it. It uses the same user profile as the installer: it is not a portable mode.

TALOS-0.1.38-win.zip · 285 MB · TALOS Desktop 0.1.38 SHA-256ec9bec24c5d9b147a7194d505ee7941f43eb0336cc6a442269904c987701c298

Compare the file with SHA256SUMS.txt, attached to the same release:

```
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 .\TALOS-Setup-<version>.exe
```

Every release file also carries a GitHub provenance attestation. With the GitHub CLI installed:

```
gh attestation verify .\TALOS-Setup-<version>.exe --repo Ninozzz95/talos
```

sezioni.titolo: If Windows says “Windows protected your PC”
sezioni.testo: The installer is not code-signed, so SmartScreen may show an unknown publisher. After checking the SHA-256 above, choose More info, make sure the file name is TALOS-Setup-<version>.exe, then Run anyway. If the option is missing because of a device policy, ask its administrator. Keep SmartScreen and Defender on.

There is no setup wizard. TALOS opens on the Home, which says what is still missing:

- No provider is set up — choose Set up a provider and connect one; see Connect a provider. Ollama and LM Studio with a saved address count as ready.
- Choose a folder — TALOS only reads and writes inside it.

The model is chosen from the pill in the composer, and how much the agent may do on its own from the permission pill; see Permissions. The window follows your system’s language, English or Italian.

The installed app updates itself. Thirty seconds after start, and then every four hours, it looks for a newer desktop release, checks our signature on it, and downloads it in the background. A band under the title bar then says the new version is ready: it installs when you close the app, or at once with Restart now. If a session is working, Restart now asks first, because restarting would interrupt it. The installer shows its progress and TALOS reopens by itself.

To turn this off, open Settings → Account, Doctor and backup → Updates and switch off Automatic updates. Check now still works when it is off. Pre-releases are not offered as updates.

- Sessions, downloaded models, notes, tasks, memory, automations and provider settings live in %APPDATA%\TALOS.
- There is no telemetry. The network is used when you choose a remote provider, search the web, download a model, and when TALOS checks for updates.
- To uninstall, close TALOS (also from the tray), then Settings → Apps → Installed apps → TALOS → Uninstall (on Windows 10, Apps & features). Your data folder is kept: delete it yourself only if you also want to remove sessions, settings and models.

pagine.descrizione: The HTTP API of the TALOS Desktop server: 310 operations on 127.0.0.1, their address, access, answers, errors and streams.

sezioni.testo:
TALOS Desktop is two parts: the window, and a local server it talks to over HTTP. Everything the window does — sessions, files, Git, models, the browser — goes through this API. It is described here for transparency, to build on the server when you run it from the source, and to read what a session streams.

Base
http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/v1
Operations
310127 GET167 POST7 PATCH9 DELETE
Answers
JSON envelope talos.harness-ui.api.v1; 3 event streams
Access
loopback only; the talos_token cookie when a token is set
Errors
323 codes

The server listens on the loopback address only (127.0.0.1 by default; ::1 and localhost are accepted), never on the network.

- In the app: the port is chosen for your profile at the first start and kept, so the window’s storage stays with it. It is not 4174.
- From the source (node harness-ui/server.mjs): http://127.0.0.1:4174/, or the next free port, printed at start; TALOS_HARNESS_UI_PORT requires an exact one. See Environment variables.

Every path starts with /api/v1. What is not under /api/ is the window itself (static files).

When the server starts with a token (TALOS_HARNESS_UI_TOKEN, at least 32 characters), every /api/ request needs the talos_token cookie, or it answers 401 with AUTH_REQUIRED. Opening /?token=<token> sets the cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict) and redirects to /, so the token does not stay in the address bar. The app starts its server with a new random token every time and hands it only to its own window.

Three kinds of request carry more checks:

- Approvals and uploads (approving or revising a workflow, starting or controlling a run, deciding on a plan, uploading a file to the chat): the request must come from this TALOS window — its Origin must be the server’s own address, and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or none — or, from a program that is not a browser, from a server started with a token.
- Shutdown (POST /api/v1/admin/shutdown): from the loopback address only, with the shutdown token in x-talos-shutdown-token.
- Two paths without the cookie, each guarded by a narrower secret instead: the OpenRouter sign-in return (a one-time state of 32 random bytes, valid ten minutes) and the files of a rendered page (a 32-byte pass bound to a session and a folder).

Without a token (the server from the source, by default) the API answers whoever reaches the port on this computer; only the approvals above still refuse a program that is not a browser.

A JSON answer is an envelope:

```
{ "ok": true, "data": { … }, "meta": { "schema": "talos.harness-ui.api.v1", "generatedAt": "2026-09-30T12:00:00.000Z" } }
```

An error keeps the same shape with ok: false and an error:

```
{ "ok": false, "error": { "code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "…", "title": "…", "explanation": "…", "action": "…", "doctorReference": "…" }, "meta": { … } }
```

code is stable and listed on Error codes with its HTTP status. message, title, explanation and action are the sentences the window shows (in Italian in this release). doctorReference opens the recorded detail: GET /api/v1/doctor/{reference}. An unknown failure is 500 INTERNAL_ERROR.

Any operation can answer these; each operation lists the others it can raise:

Code | Status | Meaning
AUTH_REQUIRED | 401 | This server accepts only the TALOS window that started it (or, for shutdown, the right token).
QUERY_INVALID | 400 | The request is not valid: a query parameter or a body field is missing, unknown or malformed.
NOT_FOUND | 404 | Nothing answers at this address, or the resource it names does not exist.
METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED | 405 | The address exists, but not with this method; the Allow header lists the methods it takes.
PAYLOAD_LIMIT | 413 | The body is larger than the server accepts: shorten it, or put the text in a file and attach it.
INTERNAL_ERROR | 500 | An unexpected error on the server; the Doctor has the detail, under the reference shown.

Some operations answer bytes (a file, an image) or an event stream instead; each operation says which.

- GET reads, POST acts, PATCH changes and DELETE removes.
- Every GET also answers HEAD.
- A path that exists with another method answers 405 with the real Allow header; a path that does not exist answers 404.
- Most operations refuse a query parameter or a body field they do not read (400, QUERY_INVALID) rather than ignore it.

Address of a request
4 KiB at most (path and query); longer answers 413.
Body
10 MiB by default (TALOS_HTTP_BODY_MAX_BYTES); larger answers 413 PAYLOAD_LIMIT. Operations with a fixed-shape body (a sign-in code, a batch) keep smaller limits.
Batch
250 items and 64 KiB at most in one batch delete.
Streams
a comment line every 15 s keeps a stream alive; a turn has no maximum duration.

A session streams its events as server-sent events: GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/events. Each event is a data: line of JSON with an id: (its sequence number); on reconnection the browser sends Last-Event-ID and the stream replays only what came after. A comment line every 15 s keeps the connection alive. The events are listed on Events.

A workflow run has its own stream, and the live browser its screen. Both are described with their operations.

Cache-Control
Nothing is kept in a cache. no-store
Content-Security-Policy
What the window may load and run. default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-src 'self' http://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:* https:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'none'
Referrer-Policy
No address is sent onward. no-referrer
X-Content-Type-Options
The declared type is the only type. nosniff
X-Frame-Options
No other page may frame TALOS. DENY

- Sessions Start, list, fork, resume and configure sessions; their history, metrics, context, commands and attachments. 36
- Turns and approvals Follow a session live, answer its approvals and questions, queue and redirect messages, run your own commands, and give it a goal. 26
- Workflows Review, approve and start workflow proposals; follow and control their runs. 30
- Files and folders The session’s folder: browse, read, search, preview and change its files; choose folders for new sessions. 26
- Git and GitHub The Git state of a session’s folder and every Git action of the review panel; GitHub pull requests through gh. 39
- Library, notes, tasks, memory and research The project’s own records, the same the agent’s tools read and write; your notes, tasks and memory also without a session. 52
- Tools and extensions The agent’s tools, and the hooks, MCP servers, plugins, skills and forged tools of a project, with their trust. 12
- Terminals The real terminals of a session. 5
- Models and providers The models on offer, provider keys and addresses, OpenRouter sign-in, and the web search source. 31
- Local models Models that run on this computer: the engine, installed models, Hugging Face downloads and what fits. 21
- Browser The built-in browser: reading pages, framing local previews, and the live browser the agent drives. 11
- Automations Instructions that run on their own, on a schedule, each run in a new session. 12
- Health and diagnostics Whether the server is up, the Doctor’s readiness report, first-run state, shutdown, and two settings of the whole app: WSL and the context engine. 9
- Error codes Every code an operation can answer, with its HTTP status. 323

The same API as an OpenAPI 3.1 description, to import into an API client. It knows what this reference knows: paths, parameters, fields and their meaning, answers and error codes, not the types of fields.

pagine.descrizione: Instructions that run on their own, on a schedule, each run in a new session. 12 operations of the TALOS Desktop local API.

sezioni.testo: Instructions that run on their own, on a schedule, each run in a new session. Paths are relative to /api/v1.

List the automations: tasks that run on a schedule.

Answers The JSON envelope.

Errors1
Code | Status | Meaning
QUERY_INVALID | 400 | The request is not valid: a query parameter or a body field is missing, unknown or malformed.

Any operation can also answer the common errors.

Create an automation: instructions that run on their own, in a folder, on a schedule.

Two forms. The current one is recognized by istruzioni and needs nome, istruzioni, cartella and pianificazione; the folder must exist and be readable and writable now. The older form starts from a task template every so many minutes (taskId and intervalloMinuti, with an optional daily limit). Only from the TALOS window. An automation is on as soon as it is created.

Body

istruzioni
What each run must do, self-contained: every run starts a new session that does not see the chat it came from.
modello
The model it runs with, as vendor/model-name.
coordinazione
true lets each run start agents on its own (Coordination); default false.
ripeti
Stop after this many runs; absent or null to run until it is turned off.
pianificazione
When it runs, in its own time zone: { tipo: "manuale" }, { tipo: "ogni-ora", minuto }, { tipo: "giornaliera", ora: "HH:MM" }, { tipo: "feriali", ora } (Monday to Friday), { tipo: "settimanale", ora, giorno } (0 = Sunday), { tipo: "ogni-n-minuti", minuti }, { tipo: "cron", espressione } (5 fields) or { tipo: "una-volta", quando: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" }. Never more often than every 5 minutes.
taskId
Older form: the task template to start from.
nome
A name for the automation.
intervalloMinuti
Older form: how often it runs, in minutes.
limiteAlGiorno
Older form: the most runs per day.
cartella
