The folder it works in, as an absolute path.
fusoOrario
Its time zone (an IANA name); default: this computer’s.
permessi
What each run may do in its folder: Read only, Workspace write (default), On request or Full access.

Answers The JSON envelope.

Errors2
Code | Status | Meaning
AUTOMATION_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN | 403 | Automations can be changed only from the TALOS window.
QUERY_INVALID | 400 | The request is not valid: a query parameter or a body field is missing, unknown or malformed.

Any operation can also answer the common errors.

Delete an automation.

sezioni.testo: An error answer carries one of these codes in error.code. The code is what a program should read; the sentences next to it are for people.

Code | Meaning
DOVE_NON_VALIDO | Where commands run must be wsl2, windows or null.
SCELTA_NON_VALIDA | The choice sent for a command setting is not valid.
BROWSER_VIVO_GESTO_IGNOTO | The gesture is not recognized.
BROWSER_VIVO_SENZA_SESSIONE | The session the page belongs to is needed.
QUERY_INVALID | The request is not valid: a query parameter or a body field is missing, unknown or malformed. 272 operations
MODEL_ID_INVALID | The model name is not one this server recognizes (expected vendor/model-name). POST /sessionsPOST /sessions/customPOST /sessions/{sessionId}/settings
REASONING_INVALID | The reasoning level is not one of those allowed. POST /sessionsPOST /sessions/customPOST /sessions/{sessionId}/settings
PERMISSIONS_INVALID | The permissions are not among those allowed. POST /sessionsPOST /sessions/customPOST /sessions/{sessionId}/settings
NOTE_INVALID | The note is not valid.
TASK_INVALID | The task is not valid.
MEMORY_INVALID | The memory is not valid.
RESEARCH_INVALID | The request is not valid for deep research. 10 operations
ELICITATION_ANSWER_INVALID | The answer to the MCP request is not valid: accept, decline or cancel, with content only when accepting a form.
LIBRARY_NAME_EMPTY | A name needs at least one letter or digit.
LIBRARY_INVALID | The request is not valid for the library.
MODE_WORKFLOW_RETIRED | The Workflow mode no longer exists: choose normale or piano.
FOLDER_INVALID | Not yet described.
GOAL_TEXT_INVALID | The goal is empty, or longer than 4,000 characters.
WORKFLOW_REVISION_INVALID | The revision is not valid.
WORKFLOW_REVISION_EMPTY | The revision changes nothing.
HOST_FORBIDDEN | The server answers only requests addressed to this computer (localhost).
FIT_INVALID | The parameters of the check are not valid. GET /local-models/{modelId}/fitPOST /local-models/{modelId}/qualify
PROBE_CONSENT_REQUIRED | Running the model needs your explicit consent.
OAUTH_ATTESA_IGNOTA | This sign-in request is no longer valid: start again from “Sign in with OpenRouter”.
OAUTH_CODICE_MANCANTE | The confirmation code is missing: start again. POST /auth/openrouter/iniziaPOST /auth/openrouter/codiceGET /auth/openrouter/ritornoGET /auth/openrouter/ritorno/{state}
CHATGPT_RICHIESTA_NON_VALIDA | The ChatGPT sign-in request is not valid.
CHATGPT_RICHIESTA_NON_AMMESSA | This request uses something the ChatGPT plan does not support.

pagine.descrizione: The environment variables TALOS Desktop and its server read, and what each one changes.

sezioni.testo: The installed app starts its own server and passes it your environment, so the first group works there too. The second applies when you run the server from the source: the app sets those itself, or ignores them.

TALOS_GENERATION_IDLE_MS
How long the model may stay completely silent before the turn is given up, in milliseconds. It restarts on every byte the provider sends, so a model that is thinking or streaming is never cut. Values below 60000 are raised to 60 s; 0 turns the failsafe off. Default1800000
TALOS_COMPACTION_TOKEN_CAP
The ceiling, in tokens, above which the conversation is compacted: the trigger is the smaller of this and 0.75 × the model’s context window, when known. Default200000
TALOS_HTTP_BODY_MAX_BYTES
The largest request body the local API accepts, in bytes; a larger one gets a 413. Routes with a fixed-shape body keep their own smaller limits. Default10485760
TALOS_MCP_STARTUP_CONCURRENCY
How many trusted MCP servers start at once when a session begins, 1 to 8; anything else falls back to 1. Default1
TALOS_STREAM_IDLE_MS
How long a provider may send nothing useful (no text, reasoning or tool call) once its answer has begun, in milliseconds, before the call is given up and retried. Keep-alive signals do not count. 0 turns it off. Default300000
TALOS_MAX_RETRIES
How many times a provider call that fails with 429 or 5xx is retried, waiting from 0.5 s and doubling up to 32 s. Above 15 it is lowered to 15; 0 retries nothing. Default10
TALOS_PROCESS_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES
The most output kept per command for process_output and the Processes tab, in bytes (a positive integer). Default67108864
TALOS_RG_PATH
The ripgrep executable the cerca tool uses, instead of the one TALOS finds.
TALOS_ATTREZZI_DIFFERITI
0 sends the model the full list of tools with every request. By default the tools used only on request are left out of the first list, and the model finds and loads them when it needs them.
TALOS_HARNESS_UI_INSTANT_COMPACTION
0, false or off turns off instant compaction: the summary of a long conversation is then made at the limit, instead of being prepared in the background before it and swapped in at once.
TALOS_REMOTE_PC_NAME
The name paired devices show for this computer (printable text, up to 64 characters). Without it, the computer’s host name.
TALOS_ADB
The adb executable, for sessions that run on a connected Android device (otherwise it is looked for under ANDROID_HOME or ANDROID_SDK_ROOT).
HF_TOKEN
A Hugging Face token, for model searches and downloads that need one.

sezioni.titolo: When you run the server from the source
sezioni.testo:
TALOS_HARNESS_UI_HOST
The address the server listens on: loopback only (127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost). Default127.0.0.1
TALOS_HARNESS_UI_PORT
The port, 1024 to 65535. Unset: 4174, or the next free port. Set: exactly this port, or the server does not start. Default4174
TALOS_HARNESS_UI_TOKEN
When set (at least 32 characters, no spaces), every /api/ request needs the talos_token cookie, which GET /?token=<token> sets. The app sets a new one at every start.
TALOS_HARNESS_UI_SESSIONS_DIR
Where sessions are stored. Use a separate folder for a second instance, or the two share history. Default.sessions-store/ next to the server
TALOS_HARNESS_UI_PROJECT_DIRS
More project folders for the session picker, separated by ;. Each must exist and be readable and writable.
TALOS_HARNESS_UI_WORKFLOW_DIR
Where workflow data is stored (an absolute folder).
TALOS_HARNESS_UI_MODELS_DEV_URL
The public model catalog to read (an HTTP(S) address without credentials). Defaulthttps://models.dev/api.json
TALOS_LLAMA_SERVER_PATH
The llama-server executable of the local engine. The app sets it to the engine it ships.
TALOS_INTRO
0 skips the first-run introduction.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY
An OpenRouter key for the server run from source; without it the server starts read-only. The app ignores it: keys come from the window and live in the OS keyring.
TALOS_HARNESS_SEARCH_PROVIDER
The first web search source, until you choose one in Settings: tavily, brave, searxng or custom. The app ignores it. Defaulttavily
TALOS_HARNESS_SEARCH_API_KEY
The key of that search source. The app ignores it.
TALOS_HARNESS_SEARCH_ENDPOINT
The address of that search source, for one you host. The app ignores it.
TALOS_HARNESS_RECEIPT_KEY_ID
With the next one, sign the receipts of side-effecting operations with your own Ed25519 key: its id. Both or neither.
TALOS_HARNESS_RECEIPT_PRIVATE_KEY_B64
The Ed25519 private key (PKCS8 PEM, in base64) that signs receipts, with TALOS_HARNESS_RECEIPT_KEY_ID.
TALOS_HARNESS_UI_IMMAGINE_MODELLO
The OpenRouter model generate_image uses. Defaultbytedance-seed/seedream-4.5
TALOS_HARNESS_UI_IMMAGINE_NATIVA
1 when that model makes images through chat completions (a model whose outputs include images) rather than OpenRouter’s images endpoint.
A hook reads its event from TALOS_HOOK_EVENT (Hooks); a plugin’s tool reads its arguments from TALOS_PLUGIN_TOOL_ARGS. Both are JSON.
The server run from the source can take a provider’s key from the variables on Providers. The installed app does not: keys come only from the window.

sezioni.testo: A hook is a command your project declares. It runs at an event of the session, receives the event as JSON, and before a tool call it can refuse the call.

pagine.descrizione: What a TALOS Desktop session may do on its own: the four modes, per-tool exceptions, the rules that always ask, and protected files.

sezioni.testo: Choose the mode for a session in the composer, or send permessi when you start it through the API. It can change while the session runs.

Read only
The agent reads and searches; it cannot write files, run commands or make documents.
Workspace writedefault
The default. The agent writes and runs commands without asking, except where a rule below still asks.
On request
Every write, command and document asks you first (an approval card; the turn waits, without a timeout).
Full access
Like Workspace write, without the check on data leaving (below), and the agent may work on files outside the session’s folder. Per-tool chiedi and nega and the rules that always ask still apply.

For the tools below, a session can set its own rule (permessiPerAttrezzo), over the mode:

Toolsscrivifile_editprovashelldocument_creategenerate_image

sempre
Always allowed, without asking.
chiedi
Ask each time.
nega
Never: the tool is refused in this session.

- Plan mode (modalitaOperativa: "piano") refuses every tool that changes or runs something until the plan is approved: the agent explores and asks.
- A per-tool nega wins over everything; a per-tool sempre skips the question unless one of the rules below applies.
- Reading or running a command on a file of the secret class (keys, credentials, keychains) always asks, even with sempre.
- library_context_policy_update always asks, by construction.
- The check on data leaving: when a call would join private data, untrusted content and a way to send it out, it asks, even with sempre (not in Full access).
- A write by scrivi or file_edit to a control file (below) always asks, in every mode.
- A trusted pre_tool_call hook can refuse a tool that changes something (Hooks).

These files and folders steer TALOS itself — hooks, MCP servers, plugins, trust records, provider settings, instructions, skills, memory. A write to one of them asks you first, whatever the mode:

Files, anywhere
.harness-ui-hooks.json.harness-ui-mcp.json.provider-runtime.jsonCLAUDE.mdAGENTS.md
Folders, anywhere
.harness-ui-plugins/.hooks-trust/.mcp-trust/.plugin-trust/.claude/.memory-store/.talos/
At the root of the project
skills/

pagine.descrizione: The 80 tools the agent of TALOS Desktop can call, with their parameters and what each one may do.

sezioni.testo:
These are the tools a Desktop session offers its model. Each shows the description the model itself reads, and its parameters. MCP servers, plugins and Tool Forge add more, per project.

Marks: asks — always asks you first; per-tool — can be set to always, ask or never (Permissions); receipt — leaves a signed receipt; hooks — a pre_tool_call hook can refuse it (Hooks); not in workflows — not offered to the steps of a workflow run.

Read, find and change the files of the session’s folder, run its tests and commands, undo the file changes of a turn.

### elenca

List a folder of the workspace, one level below included.

percorso string
folder to open, relative to the workspace root; omit it for the root
depth integer
levels below the folder to show (default 1: the folder and one level below it)
limit integer
max entries per page; without it a big folder comes in pages of about 7,000 characters
cursor string
the cursor given at the end of the previous page, to continue
browse_every_page boolean
Set true ONLY when the person explicitly asked to see or act on EVERY entry of the folder. It unlocks further pages of the same listing, up to a hard ceiling. Never set it to look around or to count files.

### cerca

Find files by content and/or name, at any depth.

testo string
text to look for inside files
nome string
fragment of the file name or path
dentro string
limit the search to this subfolder of the workspace, e.g. "src/kernel"
offset integer
Skip this many matching files (default0); use nextOffset with unchanged filters. Live search, not a snapshot.
continua string
Reference of a search still running, given by a previous cerca reply (e.g. "r1"): returns its results so far, or all of them once it has finished. testo, nome and dentro are ignored.

### leggi

Read one file.

percorso string required
The file, relative to the workspace.
offset integer
First line to read, 1-based (default 1). With format:"hex": start byte offset.
limit integer
Number of lines to read (default 2000). With format:"hex": number of bytes, 4..4096. With byteOffset: bytes to read inside the line, 4..102400 (default 102400).
byteOffset integer
Continue inside a line that was too long to show: use the byteOffset given at the end of that line or by the previous read. Not with offset or hex.
format string
Default text. Explicit hex returns original bytes as hexadecimal, with a default and maximum limit of 4096 bytes. Valuestexthex

### scrivi

per-tool receipt hooks Write a file: replace it, or append to it.

percorso string required
the file path, relative to the workspace, e.g. "src/prezzo.mjs"
contenuto string required
the text to write; with mode:"append", only the part to add at the end
mode string
omit (or "create") to replace the whole file; "append" adds contenuto at the end of that same file, creating it if it does not exist Valuescreateappend

### file_edit

per-tool receipt hooks Replace an exact piece of a file, leaving the rest untouched.

percorso string required
the file to change, relative to the workspace, e.g. "src/prezzo.mjs"
old_string string required
the exact text to replace, copied from the file as it is
new_string string required
the text that takes its place; "" deletes the matched text
replace_all boolean
replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match (default false)

per-tool receipt Run the project’s test command (the session’s proof).

timeout number
max milliseconds to wait for this test suite before it is moved to the background (NOT killed; its output keeps going to a file you can read with leggi). Default 120000, max 600000
background boolean
true to start this test run in the background right away (like Claude Code run_in_background): the tool returns immediately with the output file path; read that file later with leggi

per-tool receipt hooks Run a command in the project’s folder.

comando string required
the command, as you would type it in a terminal
descrizione string
a short, active-voice description of what this command does, shown to the user in place of the raw command
timeout number
max milliseconds to wait for this command before it is moved to the background (NOT killed; its output keeps going to a file you can read with leggi). Default 120000, max 600000
background boolean
true to start this command in the background right away (like Claude Code run_in_background): the tool returns immediately with the output file path; read that file later with leggi
network boolean
true to run this command with network access, when it failed because of a blocked network (install, fetch, push…). The person is asked first; only the network is opened, the rest of the sandbox stays

Read the retained output of a command, a page of bytes at a time, without running it again.

outputId string required
The output, exactly as the command’s result names it.
stream string
stdout or stderr. Valuesstdoutstderr
offset integer
Where to start, in bytes (follow nextOffset for the next page).
limit integer
How many bytes, 4 to 4096.
encoding string
Optional, explicit: interpret the retained bytes with this encoding only when the program is known to write it (for example cp850 for Italian cmd.exe). Never guessed; default UTF-8.

hooks not in workflows Propose to undo the file changes of earlier turns, only when you ask; you confirm on a card that shows the files (except in Full access).

turns_back integer
how many earlier messages that changed files to go back; 1 by default
include array
relative paths changed by the person or a command to put back anyway, only when the person asked for them

### web_search

query string required
what to search for
maxResults number

### naviga

Read a public web page.

url string required

Make files and visuals.

### document_create

per-tool receipt hooks Save a real document: PDF report, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, text or code.

format string required
The actual output file format and final filename extension. Valuesmdcsvhtmldocxxlsxpptxpdftxtjsonxmljsjsxtstsxvuecssscssphppyrbgorsjavaktktsswiftchcpphppcsshbashzshps1sqlyamlymltomlini
title string required
The document title; it also becomes the file name.
body string
Prose content, or exact UTF-8 source text for a code-file format. With format:"html", a body that already starts with "<!doctype html>" or "<html>" is written byte for byte, exactly as you wrote it; anything else is wrapped in a minimal page.
mode string
omit (or "create") for a new file; "append" adds body at the end of the file with the same title, instead of creating a second, numbered one. Text formats only (md, csv, txt and the source formats) — for a long HTML page build it with scrivi and mode:"append". Valuescreateappend
rows array
Table content. The first row is the header.
slides array
Slides, for pptx.
report object
PDF ONLY: a laid-out report — cover, headings, KPI cards, tables, bar and pie charts. Prefer it over body when the user asks for a report, and never send both. For any other format use body or rows.

### artifact_create

Show an interactive visual in the chat, isolated from everything.

titolo string required
short label shown on the card, e.g. "Grafico vendite"
html string required
a complete HTML document: <!doctype html>...</html>, CSS/JS inline, no external resources

### generate_image

per-tool receipt hooks Generate an image and save it in the workspace.

prompt string required
What to draw, in full: subject, composition, style, colours, mood.
shape string
The proportions of the picture. Default square. Valuessquareportraitlandscape

### delega_sottotask

not in workflows Hand a self-contained task to a new child session.

task string required

cartella string

modalita string

### tool_create

receipt hooks Propose a new tool built from the built-in capabilities; it stays off until you enable it in Tool Forge.

id string required
Lowercase slug, e.g. "log-water-intake" (3-64 chars, a-z0-9_- only). Becomes the permanent id and the tool's exposed name (forge_<id>).
title string required
Short human title, e.g. "Log water intake" (1-80 characters).
description string required
One sentence explaining what it does — shown on the consent card (1-400 characters).
input_schema object
Flat named fields the new tool asks for. Omit if it takes no input. Shape: {properties: {fieldName: {type: "string"|"number"|"integer"|"boolean"|"array", description?, enum?}}, required: [fieldName, ...]}.
flow object required
The DAG this tool runs when called. Shape: {entry: "<node id>", maxTransitions: <1-256>, nodes: [<node>, ...]}. Node types (each needs a unique "id"): "capability" — {id, type:"capability", capability:"<one of the ids above>", input:<expr>, target?:"$.state.x", next:"<node id>"} — target, if given, stores the capability's result so a later node can read it. "if" — {id, type:"if", condition:{left:<expr>, op:"eq"|"neq"|"truthy"|"exists"|"contains"|"gt"|"gte"|"lt"|"lte", right?:<expr>}, then:"<node id>", else:"<node id>"}. "return" — {id, type:"return", value:<expr>} — ends the flow, value becomes the tool's result. "fail" — {id, type:"fail", code:"SOME_CODE", message:"human message"} — ends the flow with an error. An <expr> is either a literal JSON value, or {"$ref":"$.input.fieldName"} to read the tool's own input, or {"$ref":"$.state.fieldName"} to read something a capability node stored via "target" — refs can appear nested inside objects/arrays. Every "capability" node needs "next" pointing to the following node id.

pagine.descrizione: A session in TALOS Desktop — agents and their verifiers, the terminal and the review, and what the workspace keeps.

sezioni.testo: A session is a conversation with an agent that works in your project. Its activity streams as it happens: the tools it calls and what they return. Each tool runs under a permission you set — allow, ask or deny — and the permission of a run is shown under your message.

A request can be split across several agents working in parallel, each with a verifier on its result. Every delegation is drawn on the Workflow diagram, live, one request at a time: Follow the work, filter by state, isolate a branch, see the files each agent touched, and Replay from the start.

- Terminal. A real terminal, not a transcript.
- Review. The diff of what the session changed, before you accept it.
- Undo. Put the files back as they were before one of your messages, after seeing the diff — see Undo the file changes of a turn.

Type /goal and TALOS proposes the checks that prove it done; once you confirm them it works turn after turn until they pass, and a read-only reviewer tries to refute “done” first. See Give a session a goal.
With Remote Control, TALOS for Android drives the PC’s sessions, approvals and models; you pair the device once and confirm it on the computer. See Use TALOS from your device.
Six systems stay with the workspace: Library, Notes, Tasks, Memory, Deep Research and Tool Forge. Memory holds what a session should carry forward — a rule, a procedure, a fact.

- Automations are scheduled runs, each with its own history.
- Extensions: hooks (trusted by their SHA-256), MCP servers, skills and plugins.

- Board lists the sessions with their title, model and an honest status: concluded, interrupted or in progress.
- Doctor is a read-only report of how ready the local setup is.
Every session is a replayable event log, and every operation with side effects leaves a signed receipt. The local service listens on this computer only.

pagine.descrizione: Local or cloud, on each surface — the engines, the providers, and where your keys are kept.

sezioni.testo:
- Local: the model runs on your own hardware, and the conversation stays on the device.
- Cloud: the model runs at the provider you choose, with your own API key. The conversation goes straight to that provider, with no TALOS server in between.

Downloading a model or searching the web uses the network for that action only.

- Local engine. llama.cpp is included, in a CPU and a Vulkan build. The app picks the graphics card when Vulkan lists one, otherwise the processor; the Local engine menu (Automatic · Graphics card · Processor) lets you choose.
- Models. GGUF models download inside the app, in the Model Lab, their size and SHA-256 checked before they are used; a file that does not match is rejected.
- Cloud. 23 providers with your own key, from OpenAI and Anthropic to Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI; Ollama and LM Studio on your computer too.

- Local engines, with no key: Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp.
- Cloud, 22 providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Mistral, Groq, xAI, Kimi, Qwen, Z.AI, MiniMax, Cerebras, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Novita, Nebius, Hugging Face, Azure AI Foundry, Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI.
- TALOS never falls back from a local model to a cloud one on its own.
- /provider sets up a provider, /model (or Alt+P) picks the model, and talos doctor says what is ready.

- On the device: GGUF models through llama.cpp inside the app. The GPU backend is offered only after the device passes a real qualification check. Before you download, each quantization is measured against the device’s memory.
- Cloud: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek and OpenRouter with your own key, or your own Ollama endpoint.
- Codice, the coding agent, needs a cloud provider for now: a model on the device cannot drive it yet.

Surface | Where the key is kept
Desktop | The operating system’s keyring, never the browser
CLI | The operating system’s credential store, typed in hidden input; never a file. A key already in your environment is used only after you agree once.
Android | With the app’s settings, on the device: there is no TALOS backend.

pagine.descrizione: Check what you downloaded, get past the warnings safely, and find out what is wrong when something is.

sezioni.testo:
A checksum tells you the file is the one that was published; the provenance attestation tells you it was built by the TALOS repository’s own workflow. A checksum is not a publisher signature.

```
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 .\TALOS-Setup-<version>.exe
gh attestation verify .\TALOS-Setup-<version>.exe --repo Ninozzz95/talos
```

```
sha256sum TALOS-<version>.apk
gh attestation verify TALOS-<version>.apk --repo Ninozzz95/talos
```

The published SHA-256 of every file is on the Download page and in each release.

The Desktop installer is not code-signed. After checking its SHA-256, choose More info, check the file name, then Run anyway. If the option is missing because of a device policy, ask its administrator. Do not turn off SmartScreen or Defender.

- If the graphics card is missing or lost while a model loads, TALOS Desktop restarts the model once on the CPU and the Model Lab says so, with Retry on the graphics card.
- If the card runs out of memory, the app does not switch by itself: choose Processor in the Local engine menu. That restarts the service and stays until you change it.
- The Desktop log opens from the app’s menu.

sezioni.titolo: The CLI says something is missing
sezioni.testo:
```
talos doctor
talos diagnostic bundle --out talos-diagnostic.zip
```

talos doctor says what is missing. The diagnostic bundle is a redacted report for a bug: it contains no prompt and no file content. talos --help lists every command, /help does the same inside the interactive screen.

Every TALOS server answers only whoever entered it. The installed app enters by itself; a browser enters with a link that works once and lasts 60 seconds, so any other program on the computer — a command run by the model included — cannot answer a card, change a setting or run a command in your place.

- “TALOS needs a new link” — the server restarted, or this browser never entered. Start TALOS again, or ask for a new link.
- “This link no longer works” — the link was already used, or more than 60 seconds went by. Ask for a new one.
- Started by hand from a terminal — the server prints the link on start, in English and Italian. Open it within 60 seconds.

sezioni.titolo: Android behaves differently on your device
sezioni.testo: Android makers differ in Accessibility, background execution, lock-screen behavior and battery management. TALOS checks what the device allows at runtime instead of assuming, and treats unsupported, denied, failed and verified success as different states. If an action does not happen, check the permission it needs in Install TALOS for Android.

- Bugs and questions: open an issue in the TALOS repository on GitHub. For the CLI, attach the diagnostic bundle.
- Vulnerabilities: use the repository’s private security reporting, not a public issue.

pagine.descrizione: What TALOS is, the three places it runs, what they share, and where to begin.

sezioni.testo: TALOS is an AI environment where agents do real work on your projects — they write and review code, research, and remember what matters — on the model you choose. It runs where you work.

- TALOS Desktop — the full workshop on Windows: agents as a graph, context handled for you, memory, deep research and local models. Start with Install TALOS Desktop.
- TALOS CLI — a coding agent in your terminal, installed from npm as talos-code. Start with Install the CLI.
- TALOS for Android — an assistant that runs your device: say “Hey TALOS” and it acts across it. Published as a testing build. Start with Install TALOS for Android.

The current version of each, and its files, are always on the Download page.

- Your model. Local models run on your own hardware; cloud models connect with your own key. Models & providers explains the choices on each surface.
- It asks first. Every tool is allowed, asked or denied, and you decide which.
- No account, no telemetry. No TALOS product requires a TALOS account or sends TALOS telemetry. Choosing a cloud provider, searching the web or downloading a model uses the network for that action.
- Open source. TALOS is licensed under AGPL-3.0-only, across the repository.

- You want the whole workspace on a Windows computer: TALOS Desktop.
- You work in a terminal: the CLI.
- You want TALOS on your device, and a testing build is fine: TALOS for Android.

- Install the one you chose, from its guide above.
- Pick a model: Models & providers.
- Check what you downloaded: Verify & troubleshoot.
